type stubWidget struct {
	got int
}

func (s *stubWidget) Handle(ctx *components.EventContext, ev xui.Event) {
	if _, ok := ev.(xui.KeyEvent); ok {
		s.got++
		ctx.Consume = true
	}
}

func (s *stubWidget) Draw(components.DrawContext) components.Surface {
	return components.NewSurface(1, 1, s)
}

func TestDispatchSkipsFocusMissingFromSurface(t *testing.T) {
	root := &stubWidget{}
	chat := &stubWidget{}
	a := &App{
		root:     root,
		focused:  chat,
		lastSurf: components.NewSurface(8, 4, root),
	}
	a.dispatch(&components.EventContext{}, xui.KeyEvent{Press: true, Code: xui.KeyRune, Rune: 'j'})
	assert.Equal(t, 0, chat.got)
	assert.Equal(t, 1, root.got)
	assert.Equal(t, root, a.focused)
}

func TestDispatchKeepsFocusWhenPainted(t *testing.T) {
	root := &stubWidget{}
	chat := &stubWidget{}
	surf := components.NewSurface(8, 4, root)
	surf.Children = []components.SubSurface{{Surface: components.NewSurface(8, 2, chat)}}
	a := &App{root: root, focused: chat, lastSurf: surf}
	a.dispatch(&components.EventContext{}, xui.KeyEvent{Press: true, Code: xui.KeyRune, Rune: 'j'})
	assert.Equal(t, 1, chat.got)
	assert.Equal(t, 0, root.got)
}
package app

import (
	"time"

	"github.com/pulseaiclub/xui"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/chat"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/palette"
)

// App is the vxfw-style application runtime.
type App struct {
	vx       *xui.XUI
	loop     *xui.Loop
	root     components.Widget
	focused  components.Widget
	lastSurf components.Surface
	redraw   bool
	// Anim requests a redraw on every frame tick (spinners, etc).
	Anim bool
	// pending is a single push-back slot used when coalesceWheel peeks past a
	// non-wheel event (must not Post to the end of the queue — that reorders).
	pending xui.Event
	// exitCode is set by widgets to request a specific process exit code.
	exitCode int
}

// NewApp creates an App around an existing Vaxis.
func NewApp(vx *xui.XUI) *App {
	return &App{vx: vx, redraw: true}
}

// RequestRedraw schedules a frame from any goroutine (stream updates, etc).
func (a *App) RequestRedraw() {
	if a == nil {
		return
	}
	if a.loop != nil {
		a.loop.Post(xui.TickEvent{})
		return
	}
	a.redraw = true
}

// Run starts the event loop and drives root until quit.
// It returns the exit code set via SetExitCode, or 0 on normal quit.
func (a *App) Run(root components.Widget) (int, error) {
	a.root = root
	a.loop = xui.NewLoop(a.vx)
	a.loop.Start()
	defer a.loop.Stop()

	if err := a.vx.EnterAltScreen(); err != nil {
		return a.exitCode, err
	}
	a.vx.NotifyWinsize(a.loop)
	a.vx.QueryTerminal(500 * time.Millisecond)
	_ = a.vx.EnableMouse()

	// Init event
	ctx := &components.EventContext{Redraw: true}
	a.dispatch(ctx, xui.FocusEvent{Focused: true})
	if ctx.Focus != nil {
		a.focused = ctx.Focus
	}
	a.redraw = true
	if err := a.draw(); err != nil {
		return a.exitCode, err
	}
	a.redraw = false

	ticker := time.NewTicker(time.Second / 60)
	defer ticker.Stop()

	for {
		var ev xui.Event
		if a.pending != nil {
			ev = a.pending
			a.pending = nil
		} else {
			select {
			case ev = <-a.loop.Events():
			case <-ticker.C:
				if a.Anim {
					a.redraw = true
				}
				if a.redraw {
					if err := a.draw(); err != nil {
						return a.exitCode, err
					}
					a.redraw = false
				}
				continue
			}
		}
		ev = a.coalesceWheel(ev)
		if a.handleEvent(ev) {
			return a.exitCode, nil
		}
		if a.redraw {
			if err := a.draw(); err != nil {
				return a.exitCode, err
			}
			a.redraw = false
		}
	}
}

// coalesceWheel merges back-to-back wheel events into one with a summed Wheel
// count so a fast trackpad flick triggers a single redraw instead of dozens of
// partial paints (which leave CJK/ASCII ghost columns on the TTY).
func (a *App) coalesceWheel(ev xui.Event) xui.Event {
	m, ok := ev.(xui.MouseEvent)
	if !ok || (m.Button != xui.MouseWheelUp && m.Button != xui.MouseWheelDown) {
		return ev
	}
	if m.Wheel <= 0 {
		m.Wheel = 1
	}
	for {
		next, ok := a.loop.TryEvent()
		if !ok {
			break
		}
		n, ok := next.(xui.MouseEvent)
		if !ok || (n.Button != xui.MouseWheelUp && n.Button != xui.MouseWheelDown) {
			a.pending = next
			break
		}
		step := n.Wheel
		if step <= 0 {
			step = 1
		}
		if n.Button == m.Button {
			m.Wheel += step
			continue
		}
		// Opposite direction: net the deltas onto the surviving button.
		if m.Wheel > step {
			m.Wheel -= step
			continue
		}
		if m.Wheel < step {
			m.Button = n.Button
			m.Wheel = step - m.Wheel
			continue
		}
		m.Wheel = 0
	}
	if m.Wheel == 0 {
		m.Button = xui.MouseNone
		m.Action = xui.MouseMotion
	}
	// Full refresh heals any prior TTY desync before the scrolled frame paints.
	a.vx.QueueRefresh()
	return m
}

func (a *App) handleEvent(ev xui.Event) (quit bool) {
	ctx := &components.EventContext{}
	switch e := ev.(type) {
	case xui.ResizeEvent:
		a.vx.Resize(e.Cols, e.Rows)
		ctx.Redraw = true
	case xui.KeyEvent:
		if e.CtrlC() {
			return true
		}
		a.dispatch(ctx, e)
	case xui.TickEvent:
		ctx.Redraw = true
	case xui.MouseEvent:
		hit, lx, ly := a.lastSurf.HitTestAt(e.X, e.Y)
		if hit != nil {
			// Only text-entry widgets take keyboard focus. Transcript blocks
			// (tool/thinking/bash headers) consume clicks to expand, and used
			// to steal focus — leaving the composer cursor visible but dead.
			if e.Action == xui.MousePress {
				if acceptsKeyboardFocus(hit) {
					a.focused = hit
				} else if a.focused != nil && !acceptsKeyboardFocus(a.focused) {
					// Drop stale focus on list rows so keys bubble to the composer.
					a.focused = a.root
				}
			}
			local := e
			local.X, local.Y = lx, ly
			hit.Handle(ctx, local)
			if ctx.Consume {
				break
			}
		}
		// Bubble unconsumed mouse (absolute coords) so root can run selection / overlays.
		a.dispatch(ctx, e)
	default:
		a.dispatch(ctx, ev)
	}
	if ctx.Focus != nil {
		a.focused = ctx.Focus
		ctx.Redraw = true
	}
	if ctx.Quit {
		return true
	}
	if ctx.Redraw {
		a.redraw = true
	}
	return false
}

func (a *App) dispatch(ctx *components.EventContext, ev xui.Event) {
	// Capture → target → bubble (simplified: focused then root).
	// If the focused widget is no longer in the painted tree (full-screen
	// overlay), drop it so keys don't keep going to a hidden ChatInput.
	if a.focused != nil && a.focused != a.root {
		if !surfaceHasWidget(a.lastSurf, a.focused) {
			a.focused = a.root
		} else {
			a.focused.Handle(ctx, ev)
			if ctx.Consume {
				return
			}
		}
	}
	if a.root != nil {
		a.root.Handle(ctx, ev)
	}
}

func surfaceHasWidget(s components.Surface, w components.Widget) bool {
	if w == nil {
		return false
	}
	if s.Widget == w {
		return true
	}
	for _, ch := range s.Children {
		if surfaceHasWidget(ch.Surface, w) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// RequestFocus moves keyboard focus to w (nil = root). Safe from the UI goroutine.
func (a *App) RequestFocus(w components.Widget) {
	if a == nil {
		return
	}
	if w == nil {
		w = a.root
	}
	a.focused = w
	a.redraw = true
}

// SetExitCode requests a specific exit code when the app quits.
func (a *App) SetExitCode(code int) {
	if a != nil {
		a.exitCode = code
	}
}

// ExitCode returns the requested exit code, or 0 if none was set.
func (a *App) ExitCode() int {
	if a == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return a.exitCode
}

// acceptsKeyboardFocus reports whether a mouse-press target should become the
// keyboard focus. Message-list rows handle clicks (expand/select) but typing
// must stay on the composer / palette / text fields.
func acceptsKeyboardFocus(w components.Widget) bool {
	switch w.(type) {
	case *chat.ChatInput, *palette.CommandPalette:
		return true
	default:
		return false
	}
}

func (a *App) draw() error {
	cols, rows := a.vx.Screen().Size()
	ctx := components.DrawContext{
		Min:    components.Size{},
		Max:    components.Size{Width: cols, Height: rows},
		Method: xui.WidthUnicode,
	}
	surf := a.root.Draw(ctx)
	a.lastSurf = surf
	win := a.vx.Window()
	win.Clear()
	if cur := surf.Render(win); cur != nil {
		a.vx.Screen().SetCursor(cur.X, cur.Y)
	} else {
		a.vx.Screen().ClearCursor()
	}
	if err := a.vx.Render(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return nil
}

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/pulseaiclub/xui"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/session"
)

// cellCheck spot-checks the style painted at one buffer cell.
type cellCheck struct {
	x, y  int
	style xui.Style
}

func TestAssistantBlockDraw(t *testing.T) {
	th := components.DefaultTheme()

	tests := []struct {
		name           string
		text           string
		state          session.State
		width          int // Max.Width; <= 0 exercises the 40 default
		wantWidth      int
		wantMinHeight  int
		wantContains   []string
		wantNotContain []string
		wantCells      []cellCheck
	}{
		{
			name:         "plain text",
			text:         "hello world",
			width:        60,
			wantWidth:    60,
			wantContains: []string{"hello world"},
		},
		{
			name:         "empty width falls back to 40",
			text:         "hi",
			width:        0,
			wantWidth:    40,
			wantContains: []string{"hi"},
		},
		{
			name:          "hard newlines produce rows",
			text:          "line one\nline two",
			width:         60,
			wantWidth:     60,
			wantMinHeight: 2,
			wantContains:  []string{"line one", "line two"},
		},
		{
			name:          "long text soft-wraps",
			text:          strings.Repeat("word ", 20),
			width:         12,
			wantWidth:     12,
			wantMinHeight: 3,
			wantContains:  []string{"word word"},
		},
		{
			name:           "inline code strips backticks and highlights",
			text:           "run `go test` now",
			width:          60,
			wantWidth:      60,
			wantContains:   []string{"run ", "go test", " now"},
			wantNotContain: []string{"`"},
			wantCells: []cellCheck{
				{x: 0, y: 0, style: th.Foreground}, // "run "
				{x: 4, y: 0, style: th.ToolName},   // code token
			},
		},
		{
			name:         "paths highlighted",
			text:         "see internal/components/block.go",
			width:        60,
			wantWidth:    60,
			wantContains: []string{"internal/components/block.go"},
			wantCells: []cellCheck{
				{x: 4, y: 0, style: th.ToolName}, // path token start
			},
		},
		{
			name:         "error renders red prefixed body",
			text:         "boom",
			state:        session.StateError,
			width:        60,
			wantWidth:    60,
			wantContains: []string{"Error: boom"},
			wantCells: []cellCheck{
				{x: 0, y: 0, style: th.Destructive}, // "Error:" label
				{x: 7, y: 0, style: th.Destructive}, // error body
			},
		},
		{
			name:           "error with empty text renders no label",
			state:          session.StateError,
			width:          60,
			wantWidth:      60,
			wantNotContain: []string{"Error:"},
		},
		{
			name:          "cancelled appends muted label",
			text:          "partial",
			state:         session.StateCancelled,
			width:         60,
			wantWidth:     60,
			wantMinHeight: 2,
			wantContains:  []string{"partial", "(cancelled)"},
			wantCells: []cellCheck{
				{x: 0, y: 1, style: th.Muted}, // "(cancelled)" row
			},
		},
		{
			name:           "cancelled with empty text renders no label",
			state:          session.StateCancelled,
			width:          60,
			wantWidth:      60,
			wantNotContain: []string{"cancelled"},
		},
		{
			name:           "complete state renders no label",
			text:           "done",
			state:          session.StateComplete,
			width:          60,
			wantWidth:      60,
			wantContains:   []string{"done"},
			wantNotContain: []string{"cancelled"},
		},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			assistantBlock := &AssistantBlock{
				Text:  tt.text,
				State: tt.state,
				Theme: th,
			}
			surface := assistantBlock.Draw(components.DrawContext{
				Max:    components.Size{Width: tt.width},
				Method: xui.WidthUnicode,
			})

			// The surface must carry the block as its widget identity.
			assert.Same(t, assistantBlock, surface.Widget)

			assert.Equal(t, tt.wantWidth, surface.Size.Width, "surface width")
			assert.GreaterOrEqual(t, surface.Size.Height, max(1, tt.wantMinHeight), "surface height")

			txt := components.SurfaceText(surface)
			for _, want := range tt.wantContains {
				assert.Contains(t, txt, want)
			}
			for _, notWant := range tt.wantNotContain {
				assert.NotContains(t, txt, notWant)
			}

			for _, cc := range tt.wantCells {
				require.True(t, cc.y < surface.Size.Height && cc.x < surface.Size.Width,
					"cell (%d,%d) outside surface %dx%d", cc.x, cc.y, surface.Size.Width, surface.Size.Height)
				got := surface.Buffer[cc.y*surface.Size.Width+cc.x]
				assert.True(
					t,
					cc.style.Equal(got.Style),
					"style at (%d,%d): want %+v, got %+v (char %q)",
					cc.x,
					cc.y,
					cc.style,
					got.Style,
					got.Char,
				)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestBashBlockRendersOutput(t *testing.T) {
	var lines []string
	for range 20 {
		lines = append(lines, "file.go")
	}
	b := &block.BashBlock{
		Command:  "ls",
		Output:   strings.Join(lines, "\n"),
		Status:   status.ToolDone,
		Expanded: true,
		Theme:    components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	s := b.Draw(components.DrawContext{Max: components.Size{Width: 60, Height: 40}})
	joined := components.SurfaceText(s)
	require.Contains(t, joined, "$")
	require.Contains(t, joined, "ls")
	require.NotContains(t, joined, "Show more")
	require.NotContains(t, joined, "lines truncated")
	require.Contains(t, joined, "file.go")
}

func TestUserAndAssistant(t *testing.T) {

	usText := components.SurfaceText(us)
	require.True(t, strings.Contains(usText, "$ hello") || strings.Contains(usText, "hello"),

	a := &block.AssistantBlock{Text: "see `xui` and examples/", Theme: components.DefaultTheme()}
	as := a.Draw(components.DrawContext{Max: components.Size{Width: 60, Height: 5}})
	txt := components.SurfaceText(as)
	require.Contains(t, txt, "xui")

}

	a := &block.AgentBlock{
		Name:   "agent_spawn",

		Status: status.ToolDone,
		Children: []block.ChildTool{
			{Name: "read", Detail: "a.go", Status: status.ToolDone},

	require.Contains(t, txt, "bash")
	require.Contains(t, txt, "Findings")
	require.Contains(t, txt, "fixed")

import (

const cjkHowTo = `【怎么做】
1. 翻出几篇你满意的笔记，找出共同点：标题怎么起、开头几句话说什么、分几段、写多少字
2. 把规律一条条写清楚。越具体越好：别写"写得好一点"，要写"每段1-2行，全篇不超过800字"
3. 把每次会变的部分用{{占位符}}代替，比如{{主题}}
4. 让AI照着写一篇试试，哪里不对就改说明书，改到满意为止`

func TestCJKSampleNoBlankGapsAfterClearRender(t *testing.T) {
	th := components.DefaultTheme()
	a := &block.AssistantBlock{Text: cjkHowTo, Theme: th}
	const w = 80
	s := a.Draw(components.DrawContext{Max: components.Size{Width: w, Height: 20}, Method: xui.WidthUnicode})

	screen := xui.NewScreen(w, s.Size.Height+2)
	win := xui.NewWindow(screen)
	win.Clear()
	s.Render(win)

	txt := components.SurfaceText(s)
	for _, want := range []string{"翻出几篇你满意的", "把每次", "笔记"} {
		require.Contains(t, txt, want, "surface missing %q", want)
	}

	var b strings.Builder
	_, h := screen.Size()
	for y := range h {
		for x := 0; x < w; {
			c := screen.GetCell(x, y)
			step := int(c.Width)
			step = max(step, 1)
			if !c.Trail && c.Char != "" && c.Char != " " {
				b.WriteString(c.Char)
			}
			x += step
		}
		b.WriteByte('\n')
	}
	got := b.String()
	for _, want := range []string{"翻出几篇你满意的", "把每次"} {
		require.Contains(t, got, want, "screen missing %q\n%s", want, got)
	}

	screen.MarkRefresh()
	for _, d := range screen.Diff() {
		require.False(t, d.Cell.Trail, "Diff emitted Trail at (%d,%d)", d.X, d.Y)
	}
}

package block

import (
	"github.com/pulseaiclub/xui"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/text"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/session"
)

// AssistantBlock renders assistant Markdown (GFM) with themed typography,
// path highlights, and syntax-colored fenced code.
type AssistantBlock struct {
	Text  string
	State session.State
	Theme components.Theme
}

func (assistantBlock *AssistantBlock) theme() components.Theme {
	if assistantBlock.Theme.Success.Fg.Kind == 0 && assistantBlock.Theme.Foreground.Fg.Kind == 0 {
		return components.DefaultTheme()
	}
	return assistantBlock.Theme
}

// Handle is a no-op; assistant output is read-only.
func (*AssistantBlock) Handle(_ *components.EventContext, _ xui.Event) {}

// CopyText returns the assistant message body.
func (assistantBlock *AssistantBlock) CopyText() string { return assistantBlock.Text }

// Draw renders the assistant markdown body with themed typography.
func (assistantBlock *AssistantBlock) Draw(ctx components.DrawContext) components.Surface {
	th := assistantBlock.theme()
	w := ctx.Max.Width
	if w <= 0 {
		w = 40
	}
	spans := text.RenderMarkdown(assistantBlock.Text, th)
	if assistantBlock.State == session.StateError && assistantBlock.Text != "" {
		// Error turns read like tool failures: red body under an "Error:" label.
		spans = append([]components.Span{{Text: "Error: ", Style: th.Destructive}}, spans...)
		for i := range spans {
			spans[i].Style = th.Destructive
		}
	}
	if assistantBlock.State == session.StateCancelled && assistantBlock.Text != "" {
		if len(spans) > 0 {
			spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: "\n", Style: th.Muted})
		}
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: "(cancelled)", Style: th.Muted})
	}
	return components.PaintRichLines(w, components.WrapSpans(spans, w, ctx.Method), ctx.Method, assistantBlock)
}
package block

import (
	"fmt"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"github.com/pulseaiclub/xui"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/chrome"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/status"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/util"

// BashBlock renders a bash tool / "!cmd" row:
//
//	$ go test ./...
//	  ok      github.com/x/y  0.4s
//	  ok      github.com/x/z  0.1s
//	  … +118 more lines ▶
//
//	$ go test ./...
//	  FAIL github.com/x/y
//	  --- FAIL: TestFoo
//	  [Showing lines 1-1000 of 1000. Full output: /tmp/a1-bash-….log]
//
// A collapsed row always keeps a tail of the output (BashCollapsedTailLines)
// so the user can see how a command ended without expanding. Expanding shows
// everything the tool retained, including its own truncation notice and
// temp-file dump link.
type BashBlock struct {
	Command  string
	Output   string
	Status   status.ToolStatus
	ExitCode int
	Expanded bool
	Theme    components.Theme

	// OnToggle is called when the user expands/collapses (click title / Enter).
	OnToggle func(expanded bool)

	titleH int // title row count; body clicks don't toggle (allow selection)
}

func (bashBlock *BashBlock) theme() components.Theme {
	if bashBlock.Theme.Success.Fg.Kind == 0 && bashBlock.Theme.Foreground.Fg.Kind == 0 {
		return components.DefaultTheme()
	}
	return bashBlock.Theme
}

// Handle toggles expansion on Enter/space or a left-click on the title row.
func (bashBlock *BashBlock) Handle(ctx *components.EventContext, ev xui.Event) {
	switch e := ev.(type) {
	case xui.KeyEvent:
		if e.Code == xui.KeyEnter || (e.Code == xui.KeyRune && e.Rune == ' ') {
			if bashBlock.hasBody() {
				bashBlock.toggle(ctx)
			}
		}
	case xui.MouseEvent:
		if e.Action != xui.MousePress || e.Button != xui.MouseLeft {
			return
		}
		// Only the title toggles expand; body stays selectable for copy-on-select.
		if bashBlock.hasBody() && e.Y >= 0 && e.Y < bashBlock.titleH {
			bashBlock.toggle(ctx)
		}
	}
}

// toggle flips expansion, notifies OnToggle, and schedules a redraw.
func (bashBlock *BashBlock) toggle(ctx *components.EventContext) {
	bashBlock.Expanded = !bashBlock.Expanded
	if bashBlock.OnToggle != nil {
		bashBlock.OnToggle(bashBlock.Expanded)
	}
	ctx.ConsumeAndRedraw()
}

// CopyText returns "$ command" plus output when present.
func (bashBlock *BashBlock) CopyText() string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	sb.WriteString("$ ")
	sb.WriteString(bashBlock.Command)
	out := strings.TrimRight(bashBlock.Output, "\n")
	if out != "" {
		sb.WriteByte('\n')
		sb.WriteString(out)
	}
	return sb.String()
}

// BashCollapsedTailLines is how many trailing output lines a collapsed bash
// row keeps. Enough to show a test summary, a build error, or a diffstat
// without flooding the transcript; the rest is one Enter away.
const BashCollapsedTailLines = 8

func (bashBlock *BashBlock) hasBody() bool {
	return strings.TrimSpace(bashBlock.Output) != "" || bashBlock.Status == status.ToolError
}

// collapsedBody renders the tail shown when the row is closed: the last
// BashCollapsedTailLines of output, plus a dim trailer naming the hidden count.
// A row within the budget shows all of its lines and no trailer, so a short
// command reads exactly like an expanded one.
//
// The budget is measured on wrapped lines rather than source lines, because a
// single 400-column log line occupies eight surface rows once wrapped — and an
// untrimmed row would still blow the budget it exists to bound.
func (bashBlock *BashBlock) collapsedBody(
	th components.Theme,
	width int,
	method xui.WidthMethod,
) []components.RichLine {
	lines := bashBodyLines(bashBlock.Output, th, width, method)
	if len(lines) <= BashCollapsedTailLines {
		return lines
	}
	out := make([]components.RichLine, 0, BashCollapsedTailLines+1)
	out = append(out, lines[len(lines)-BashCollapsedTailLines:]...)
	trailer := fmt.Sprintf("… +%d more lines", len(lines)-BashCollapsedTailLines)
	out = append(out, components.WrapSpans([]components.Span{{Text: trailer, Style: th.Muted}}, width, method)...)
	return out
}

// Draw renders the "$ command" title and, when expanded, the truncated output body.
func (bashBlock *BashBlock) Draw(ctx components.DrawContext) components.Surface {
	th := bashBlock.theme()
	w := ctx.Max.Width
	if w <= 0 {
		w = 40
	}

	titleWrapped := components.WrapSpans(bashBlock.titleSpans(th), w, ctx.Method)
	titleH := len(titleWrapped)
	bashBlock.titleH = titleH

	var bodyLines []components.RichLine
	if bashBlock.hasBody() {
		bodyW := w
		if bodyW > 2 {
			bodyW -= 2
		}
		switch {
		case bashBlock.Expanded:
			// Everything the tool retained, including its own "[Showing lines
			// …]" notice and the temp-file dump link.
			bodyLines = bashBodyLines(bashBlock.Output, th, bodyW, ctx.Method)
		case bashBlock.Status == status.ToolError:
			// A failure is the one case where a collapsed row must not hide
			// anything: the reason is the only thing on screen.
			bodyLines = bashBodyLines(bashBlock.Output, th, bodyW, ctx.Method)
		default:
			// Tail preview: what happened, without the flood.
			bodyLines = bashBlock.collapsedBody(th, bodyW, ctx.Method)
		}
	}

	h := titleH + len(bodyLines)
	h = max(h, 1)
	s := components.NewSurface(w, h, bashBlock)
	y := 0
	for _, line := range titleWrapped {
		components.PaintSpans(&s, 0, y, line, ctx.Method)
		y++
	}
	for _, line := range bodyLines {
		components.PaintSpans(&s, 2, y, line, ctx.Method)
		y++
	}
	return s
}

// titleSpans builds the "$ command [exit code] [arrow]" header spans.
func (bashBlock *BashBlock) titleSpans(th components.Theme) []components.Span {
	prefixStyle := th.IdentityOrSuccess()
	switch bashBlock.Status {
	case status.ToolError:
		prefixStyle = th.Destructive
	case status.ToolRunning, status.ToolQueued:
		prefixStyle = th.ToolName
	case status.ToolCancelled, status.ToolRejected:
		prefixStyle = th.Muted
	}

	cmdStyle := th.Foreground
	if bashBlock.Status == status.ToolCancelled || bashBlock.Status == status.ToolRejected {
		cmdStyle.Strikethrough = true
	}

	title := []components.Span{
		{Text: chrome.BashPrompt, Style: prefixStyle},
		{Text: bashBlock.Command, Style: cmdStyle},
	}
	if suf := chrome.StatusSuffix(bashBlock.Status); suf != "" {
		title = append(title, components.Span{Text: suf, Style: th.Muted})
	}
	if bashBlock.Status == status.ToolDone && bashBlock.ExitCode != 0 {
		it := xui.Style{Italic: true}
		title = append(
			title,
			components.Span{Text: " (", Style: it},
			components.Span{Text: "exit code: ", Style: it},
			components.Span{
				Text:  strconv.Itoa(bashBlock.ExitCode),
				Style: xui.Style{Italic: true, Fg: th.Destructive.Fg},
			},
			components.Span{Text: ")", Style: it},
		)
	}
	if bashBlock.hasBody() {
		title = append(title, components.Span{Text: chrome.ExpandArrow(bashBlock.Expanded), Style: th.Muted})
	}
	return title
}

func bashBodyLines(output string, th components.Theme, width int, method xui.WidthMethod) []components.RichLine {
	if output == "" {
		return nil
	}
	text := strings.TrimRight(util.ReplaceAll(output, "\r", ""), "\n")
	fg := th.Foreground
	fg.Dim = true
	spans := []components.Span{{Text: text + "\n", Style: fg}}
	if width < 1 {
		width = 1
	}
	return components.WrapSpans(spans, width, method)
}

import (
	"github.com/pulseaiclub/xui"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components"
)

// CompactionBlock is a transcript marker shown after context compaction
// (Cursor-style italic "Compacted").
type CompactionBlock struct {
	Theme components.Theme
	// TokensBefore is the context size before the cut; 0 hides the count.
	TokensBefore int
}

func (b *CompactionBlock) theme() components.Theme {
	if b.Theme.Muted.Fg.Kind == 0 && b.Theme.Foreground.Fg.Kind == 0 {
		return components.DefaultTheme()
	}
	return b.Theme
}

// Handle is a no-op; the compaction marker is not interactive.
func (*CompactionBlock) Handle(_ *components.EventContext, _ xui.Event) {}

// Draw renders the italic marker line, with the pre-cut context size when known.
func (b *CompactionBlock) Draw(ctx components.DrawContext) components.Surface {
	th := b.theme()
	w := ctx.Max.Width
	if w <= 0 {
		w = 40
	}
	st := th.Muted
	st.Italic = true
	st.Dim = true
	label := "Compacted"
	if b.TokensBefore > 0 {
		label = "Compacted from " + components.FormatTokens(b.TokensBefore) + " tokens"
	}
	lines := components.WrapSpans([]components.Span{
		{Text: label, Style: st},
	}, w, ctx.Method)
	return components.PaintRichLines(w, lines, ctx.Method, b)
}
// Package block provides transcript widgets for tool and activity rows.
package block
package block

import (
	"strings"

	"github.com/pulseaiclub/xui"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/chrome"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/status"
)

// ThinkingBlock renders reasoning: collapsible header with spinner
// while streaming, ✓ when done, and dim italic body when expanded.
type ThinkingBlock struct {
	Text        string
	Streaming   bool
	Interrupted bool
	Expanded    bool
	Theme       components.Theme
	Spinner     *status.Spinner
	OnToggle    func(expanded bool)

	titleH int
}

func (t *ThinkingBlock) theme() components.Theme {
	if t.Theme.Success.Fg.Kind == 0 && t.Theme.Foreground.Fg.Kind == 0 {
		return components.DefaultTheme()
	}
	return t.Theme
}

// Handle toggles expansion on Enter/space or a left-click on the title row.
func (t *ThinkingBlock) Handle(ctx *components.EventContext, ev xui.Event) {
	switch e := ev.(type) {
	case xui.KeyEvent:
		if e.Code == xui.KeyEnter || (e.Code == xui.KeyRune && e.Rune == ' ') {
			t.Expanded = !t.Expanded
			if t.OnToggle != nil {
				t.OnToggle(t.Expanded)
			}
			ctx.ConsumeAndRedraw()
		}
	case xui.MouseEvent:
		if e.Action == xui.MousePress && e.Button == xui.MouseLeft && e.Y >= 0 && e.Y < t.titleH {
			t.Expanded = !t.Expanded
			if t.OnToggle != nil {
				t.OnToggle(t.Expanded)
			}
			ctx.ConsumeAndRedraw()
		}
	}
}

// CopyText returns thinking body text.
func (t *ThinkingBlock) CopyText() string { return t.Text }

// Draw renders the "Thinking" header with spinner/done icon and the
// dim italic reasoning body when expanded.
func (t *ThinkingBlock) Draw(ctx components.DrawContext) components.Surface {
	th := t.theme()
	w := ctx.Max.Width
	if w <= 0 {
		w = 40
	}

	icon := chrome.Ok
	iconSt := th.Success
	labelSt := th.Muted
	if t.Streaming {
		icon = chrome.Busy
		iconSt = th.ToolName
		if t.Spinner != nil {
			icon = t.Spinner.Glyph()
		}
		labelSt = th.ToolName
	}
	if t.Interrupted {
		icon = chrome.Stop
		iconSt = th.Warning
		labelSt = th.Warning
	}

	spans := []components.Span{
		{Text: icon + " ", Style: iconSt},
		{Text: "Thinking", Style: labelSt},
	}
	if t.Interrupted {
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: " (interrupted)", Style: th.Warning})
	}
	spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: chrome.ExpandArrow(t.Expanded), Style: th.Muted})

	titleLines := components.WrapSpans(spans, w, ctx.Method)
	t.titleH = len(titleLines)

	var bodyLines []components.RichLine
	if t.Expanded && strings.TrimSpace(t.Text) != "" {
		body := th.Muted
		body.Italic = true
		body.Dim = true
		bodyW := w
		if bodyW > 2 {
			bodyW -= 2
		}
		bodyLines = components.WrapSpans([]components.Span{{Text: t.Text, Style: body}}, bodyW, ctx.Method)
	}

	h := len(titleLines) + len(bodyLines)
	h = max(h, 1)
	s := components.NewSurface(w, h, t)
	y := 0
	for _, line := range titleLines {
		components.PaintSpans(&s, 0, y, line, ctx.Method)
		y++
	}
	for _, line := range bodyLines {
		components.PaintSpans(&s, 2, y, line, ctx.Method)
		y++
	}
	return s
}
package block

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"github.com/pulseaiclub/xui"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/chrome"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/status"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/util"
)

// DiffBlock renders a file edit (write / edit / apply_patch) as a
// Claude-Code-style card:
//
//	✎ internal/x/y.go  +12 -3
//
//	 a  b  c  old
//	 d  e  +  new
//
// The body is a unified diff with per-line +/- coloring and old/new line
// numbers. Added and removed lines are counted from the diff itself, so the
// header stat is never a guess. The card stays collapsed until the user
// expands it, or a run explicitly asks to start open.
type DiffBlock struct {
	// Path is the display path shown in the header.
	Path string
	// Diff is the unified-diff text produced by the edit tool. It may carry
	// ---/+++ file headers and @@ hunk headers, which are recognized and
	// rendered rather than shown as content.
	Diff string
	// Status drives the glyph and header style.
	Status status.ToolStatus
	// Error is the failure text, shown when the edit was rejected or failed.
	Error string
	// Expanded controls whether the diff body is drawn.
	Expanded bool
	Theme    components.Theme
	Spinner  *status.Spinner
	// OnToggle is called when the user expands/collapses.
	OnToggle func(expanded bool)

	titleH int // title row count; body clicks don't toggle (allow selection)
}

func (diffBlock *DiffBlock) theme() components.Theme {
	if diffBlock.Theme.Success.Fg.Kind == 0 && diffBlock.Theme.Foreground.Fg.Kind == 0 {
		return components.DefaultTheme()
	}
	return diffBlock.Theme
}

// HasBody reports whether the row has anything to show beyond its header.
func (diffBlock *DiffBlock) HasBody() bool {
	return strings.TrimSpace(diffBlock.Diff) != "" || strings.TrimSpace(diffBlock.Error) != ""
}

// Handle toggles expansion on Enter/space or a left-click on the title row.
func (diffBlock *DiffBlock) Handle(ctx *components.EventContext, ev xui.Event) {
	if !diffBlock.HasBody() {
		return
	}
	switch e := ev.(type) {
	case xui.KeyEvent:
		if e.Code == xui.KeyEnter || (e.Code == xui.KeyRune && e.Rune == ' ') {
			diffBlock.toggle(ctx)
		}
	case xui.MouseEvent:
		if e.Action == xui.MousePress && e.Button == xui.MouseLeft && e.Y >= 0 && e.Y < diffBlock.titleH {
			diffBlock.toggle(ctx)
		}
	}
}

func (diffBlock *DiffBlock) toggle(ctx *components.EventContext) {
	diffBlock.Expanded = !diffBlock.Expanded
	if diffBlock.OnToggle != nil {
		diffBlock.OnToggle(diffBlock.Expanded)
	}
	ctx.ConsumeAndRedraw()
}

// CopyText returns the path, the stat line, and the raw diff.
func (diffBlock *DiffBlock) CopyText() string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	sb.WriteString(diffBlock.Path)
	if added, removed := diffBlock.Stat(); added > 0 || removed > 0 {
		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, " (+%d -%d)", added, removed)
	}
	if diffText := strings.TrimRight(diffBlock.Diff, "\n"); diffText != "" {
		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "\n%s", diffText)
	}
	return sb.String()
}

// Stat counts added and removed lines in the diff. File headers, hunk headers,
// and split-at/collapse markers are not counted.
func (diffBlock *DiffBlock) Stat() (added, removed int) {
	for ln := range strings.SplitSeq(diffBlock.Diff, "\n") {
		switch {
		case strings.HasPrefix(ln, "+") && !strings.HasPrefix(ln, "+++"):
			added++
		case strings.HasPrefix(ln, "-") && !strings.HasPrefix(ln, "---"):
			removed++
		}
	}
	return added, removed
}

// Draw renders the "✎ path +N -M" header and, when expanded, the diff body.
func (diffBlock *DiffBlock) Draw(ctx components.DrawContext) components.Surface {
	th := diffBlock.theme()
	w := ctx.Max.Width
	if w <= 0 {
		w = 40
	}

	titleWrapped := components.WrapSpans(diffBlock.titleSpans(th), w, ctx.Method)
	diffBlock.titleH = len(titleWrapped)

	var bodyLines []components.RichLine
	if diffBlock.HasBody() {
		bodyW := w
		if bodyW > 2 {
			bodyW -= 2
		}
		// A failure is the one thing the user must see without expanding: a
		// rejected edit normally means the model needs to retry.
		errText := strings.TrimSpace(diffBlock.Error)
		showBody := diffBlock.Expanded || errText != ""
		if showBody {
			if errText != "" {
				bodyLines = append(bodyLines, components.WrapSpans([]components.Span{
					{Text: "Error: " + errText, Style: th.Destructive},
				}, bodyW, ctx.Method)...)
			}
			bodyLines = append(bodyLines, diffBodyLines(diffBlock.Diff, th, bodyW, ctx.Method)...)
		}
	}

	h := len(titleWrapped) + len(bodyLines)
	h = max(h, 1)
	s := components.NewSurface(w, h, diffBlock)
	y := 0
	for _, line := range titleWrapped {
		components.PaintSpans(&s, 0, y, line, ctx.Method)
		y++
	}
	for _, line := range bodyLines {
		components.PaintSpans(&s, 2, y, line, ctx.Method)
		y++
	}
	return s
}

// titleSpans builds the "✎ path +N -M ↓" header.
func (diffBlock *DiffBlock) titleSpans(th components.Theme) []components.Span {
	icon, iconSt := chrome.ToolIcon(diffBlock.Status, th, diffBlock.Spinner)
	spans := []components.Span{
		{Text: icon + " ", Style: iconSt},
		{Text: diffBlock.displayPath(), Style: th.ToolName},
	}
	if added, removed := diffBlock.Stat(); added > 0 || removed > 0 {
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{
			Text:  fmt.Sprintf(" +%d -%d", added, removed),
			Style: th.Muted,
		})
	}
	if suf := chrome.StatusSuffix(diffBlock.Status); suf != "" {
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: suf, Style: th.Muted})
	}
	if diffBlock.HasBody() {
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: chrome.ExpandArrow(diffBlock.Expanded), Style: th.Muted})
	}
	return spans
}

// displayPath reduces the row's path field to the path alone.
func (diffBlock *DiffBlock) displayPath() string {
	path := strings.TrimSpace(diffBlock.Path)
	if base, _, ok := strings.Cut(path, "#"); ok {
		path = strings.TrimSpace(base)
	}
	if path == "" {
		return "file"
	}
	return path
}

// diffBodyLines renders a unified diff with per-line coloring, right-aligned
// line numbers, and hunk separators. File headers (---/+++) are dropped: the
// path is already in the card header.
func diffBodyLines(diff string, th components.Theme, width int, method xui.WidthMethod) []components.RichLine {
	if width < 1 {
		width = 1
	}

	addSt := th.Success
	delSt := th.Destructive
	hunkSt := th.Muted

	// A body with no "@@" hunk header (a brand-new file shown as plain + lines)
	// still begins at line 1; without this the first row has no number and the
	// rest are shifted by one.
	oldNo, newNo := 0, 1
	var out []components.RichLine
	// Tracks whether a hunk separator has any diff content before it, so one is
	// never emitted ahead of the first region (only between two).
	seenContent := false

	for raw := range strings.SplitSeq(util.ReplaceAll(diff, "\r", ""), "\n") {
		// The tool separates its summary from the body with a blank line.
		if raw == "" {
			continue
		}
		// Tools prepend a one-line summary ("Created x (3 lines).", "Updated
		// x.") ahead of the diff body. It is prose, not a unified-diff line, so
		// it is rendered dim and never advances the line counters — otherwise
		// the very first real line is numbered against a line that does not
		// exist in the file.
		if isDiffPrologue(raw) {
			out = append(out, components.WrapSpans([]components.Span{{Text: raw, Style: hunkSt}}, width, method)...)
			continue
		}

		switch {
		case strings.HasPrefix(raw, "---") || strings.HasPrefix(raw, "+++"):
			continue
		case strings.HasPrefix(raw, "@@"):
			oldNo, newNo = parseHunkStart(raw)
			if seenContent {
				out = append(
					out,
					components.WrapSpans(
						[]components.Span{{Text: strings.Repeat("·", min(width, 24)), Style: hunkSt}},
						width,
						method,
					)...)
			}
			continue
		}

		var (
			kind byte
			text string
			no   int
		)
		switch {
		case strings.HasPrefix(raw, "+"):
			kind, text, no = '+', raw[1:], newNo
			newNo++
		case strings.HasPrefix(raw, "-"):
			kind, text, no = '-', raw[1:], oldNo
			oldNo++
		default:
			kind, text, no = ' ', strings.TrimPrefix(raw, " "), newNo
			newNo++
		}

		marker := string(kind)
		var style xui.Style
		switch kind {
		case '+':
			style = addSt
		case '-':
			style = delSt
		default:
			style = th.Foreground
			style.Dim = true
			marker = " "
		}

		// Fixed-width gutter: [old] [marker] text. Keeping the marker in its
		// own padded cell means the +/- column is the same for every line, so
		// the eye can scan changes without re-finding the alignment.
		numText := ""
		if no > 0 {
			numText = fmt.Sprintf("%4d", no)
		}
		spans := []components.Span{
			{Text: numText + "  ", Style: hunkSt},
			{Text: marker + " ", Style: style},
			{Text: text, Style: style},
		}
		seenContent = true
		out = append(out, components.WrapSpans(spans, width, method)...)
	}
	return out
}

// isDiffPrologue reports whether line is the tool's human summary ahead of a
// diff body, rather than a unified-diff line. A real diff line always starts
// with '+', '-', ' ', or '@@'; prose therefore starts with anything else.
func isDiffPrologue(line string) bool {
	if line == "" {
		return false
	}
	switch line[0] {
	case '+', '-', ' ', '@', '\\':
		return false
	}
	return true
}

// parseHunkStart extracts the old and new starting line numbers from an
// "@@ -a,b +c,d @@" header. Unparseable headers leave the counters untouched.
func parseHunkStart(header string) (oldStart, newStart int) {
	for f := range strings.FieldsSeq(header) {
		switch {
		case strings.HasPrefix(f, "-"):
			oldStart = leadingInt(f[1:])
		case strings.HasPrefix(f, "+"):
			newStart = leadingInt(f[1:])
		}
	}
	return oldStart, newStart
}

// leadingInt parses the leading digits of s, stopping at the first non-digit.
func leadingInt(s string) int {
	n := 0
	for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
		if s[i] < '0' || s[i] > '9' {
			break
		}
		n = n*10 + int(s[i]-'0')
	}
	return n
}
package block_test

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/block"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/status"
)

const sampleDiff = `--- a/internal/foo.go
+++ b/internal/foo.go
@@ -1,5 +1,6 @@
 package foo
+
+// Added documents the func.
 func Bar() {}
@@ -20,3 +21,4 @@
 func Baz() {}
+    return 1
-    return 0
`

func draw(t *testing.T, w *block.DiffBlock, width int) string {
	t.Helper()
	s := w.Draw(components.DrawContext{Max: components.Size{Width: width, Height: 40}})
	return components.SurfaceText(s)
}

func TestDiffBlockStatCountsChanges(t *testing.T) {
	d := &block.DiffBlock{Path: "internal/foo.go", Diff: sampleDiff}
	added, removed := d.Stat()
	assert.Equal(t, 3, added, "three + lines")
	assert.Equal(t, 1, removed, "one - line")
}

func TestDiffBlockStatIgnoresHeaders(t *testing.T) {
	// A tool that emits a brand-new file ("Created new file.") has no diff
	// body, so the stat must be 0/0 rather than counting the header lines.
	d := &block.DiffBlock{Path: "new.go", Diff: "@file new.go#ABCD\n\nCreated new file."}
	added, removed := d.Stat()
	assert.Equal(t, 0, added)
	assert.Equal(t, 0, removed)
}

func TestDiffBlockCopyTextIncludesStatAndBody(t *testing.T) {
	d := &block.DiffBlock{Path: "a.go", Diff: sampleDiff}
	text := d.CopyText()
	assert.Contains(t, text, "a.go")
	assert.Contains(t, text, "+3 -1")
	assert.Contains(t, text, "+// Added documents the func.")
}

func TestDiffBlockDrawsHeaderAndBody(t *testing.T) {
	d := &block.DiffBlock{
		Path:     "internal/foo.go",
		Diff:     sampleDiff,
		Status:   status.ToolDone,
		Expanded: true,
		Theme:    components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	got := draw(t, d, 60)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "internal/foo.go")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "+3 -1", "the header shows the change count")
	// SurfaceText trims trailing whitespace, so assert on the meaningful
	// content of each line rather than exact padding.
	assert.Contains(t, got, "+ // Added documents the func.", "an added line is rendered")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "-     return 0", "a removed line is rendered")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "21    func Baz() {}", "a context line keeps its line number")
	// File headers are dropped: the path is already in the card header.
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "--- a/")
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "+++ b/")
	// A separator rules the boundary between hunks.
	assert.Contains(t, got, "·")
}

func TestDiffBlockCollapsedHidesBody(t *testing.T) {
	d := &block.DiffBlock{Path: "internal/foo.go", Diff: sampleDiff, Theme: components.DefaultTheme()}
	got := draw(t, d, 60)
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "+// Added documents the func.", "collapsed hides the body")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "internal/foo.go", "the header stays visible")
}

func TestDiffBlockFailedEditShowsError(t *testing.T) {
	d := &block.DiffBlock{
		Path:   "internal/foo.go",
		Error:  "old_str not found in internal/foo.go",
		Status: status.ToolError,
		Theme:  components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	require.True(t, d.HasBody(), "a failed edit has a body: the error")
	got := draw(t, d, 60)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "Error:")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "old_str not found")
}

func TestDiffBlockNewFileShowsNoStat(t *testing.T) {
	d := &block.DiffBlock{
		Path:     "brand/new.go",
		Diff:     "@file brand/new.go#ABCD\n\nCreated new file.",
		Status:   status.ToolDone,
		Expanded: true,
		Theme:    components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	got := draw(t, d, 60)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "brand/new.go")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "Created new file.", "the creation note is still readable")
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "+0 -0", "no bogus stat on a created file")
}

func TestToolBlockResultStat(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name   string
		status status.ToolStatus
		output string
		want   string
	}{
		{"running shows nothing", status.ToolRunning, "partial", ""},
		{"error shows nothing", status.ToolError, "boom", ""},
		{"empty output", status.ToolDone, "", ""},
		{"whitespace only", status.ToolDone, "\n\n  \n", ""},
		{"one line", status.ToolDone, "a.go", "(1 line)"},
		{"many lines", status.ToolDone, "a\nb\n\nc", "(3 lines)"},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			b := &block.ToolBlock{
				Name:     "grep",
				Detail:   "Paths",
				Output:   tc.output,
				Status:   tc.status,
				Expanded: true,
				Theme:    components.DefaultTheme(),
			}
			got := components.SurfaceText(b.Draw(components.DrawContext{Max: components.Size{Width: 60, Height: 40}}))
			assert.Contains(t, got, "grep")
			if tc.want == "" {
				assert.NotContains(t, got, "(1 line)")
				assert.NotContains(t, got, "lines)")
			} else {
				assert.Contains(t, got, tc.want, "the header reports the result volume")
			}
		})
	}
}

// A body with no @@ header (a brand-new file) must still number from 1: without
// that the first row has no line number and every later row is off by one.
func TestDiffBlockNumbersNewFileFromOne(t *testing.T) {
	d := &block.DiffBlock{
		Path:     "brand/new.go",
		Diff:     "Created brand/new.go (3 lines).\n\n+package main\n+\n+func main() {}",
		Status:   status.ToolDone,
		Expanded: true,
		Theme:    components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	got := draw(t, d, 60)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "Created brand/new.go (3 lines).", "the summary line is shown")
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "1  +package main", "no phantom unnumbered first row")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "1  + package main", "the first added line is numbered 1")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "3  + func main() {}", "numbering continues to the last line")
}

// The tool's summary prose must not be swallowed as a diff context line, and
// the blank line separating it from the body must not draw a row at all.
func TestDiffBlockSkipsSummaryAndBlankLines(t *testing.T) {
	d := &block.DiffBlock{
		Path:     "a.go",
		Diff:     "Updated a.go.\n\n@@ -1,1 +1,2 @@\n keep\n+added",
		Status:   status.ToolDone,
		Expanded: true,
		Theme:    components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	got := draw(t, d, 60)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "Updated a.go.")
	// No separator before the first hunk: there is nothing above it to separate.
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "·", "no leading hunk separator")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "+ added")
}

// A second hunk does get a separator, so the two change regions read apart.
func TestDiffBlockSeparatesHunks(t *testing.T) {
	d := &block.DiffBlock{
		Path: "a.go",
		Diff: "@@ -1,2 +1,2 @@\n one\n-two\n+TWO\n" +
			"@@ -40,2 +40,3 @@\n forty\n+forty one",
		Status:   status.ToolDone,
		Expanded: true,
		Theme:    components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	got := draw(t, d, 60)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "·", "a separator sits between hunks")
}
package block

import (
	"fmt"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"github.com/pulseaiclub/xui"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/chrome"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/status"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/util"
)

// ReadBlock renders a read / grep row as a card in the same shape as DiffBlock:
//
//	✓ read haiku.txt (5 lines)
//
//	     1  cold bytes on the wire
//	     2  a green cursor waits alone
//
// The `@file path` line the tools emit is dropped — the path is already the card
// header, so repeating it costs a row on a narrow terminal.
type ReadBlock struct {
	// Path is the display path shown in the header.
	Path string
	// Body is the tool output with its `@file path` header line removed.
	Body string
	// Status drives the glyph and header style.
	Status status.ToolStatus
	// Error is the failure text, shown when the call failed.
	Error string
	// Expanded controls whether the body is drawn.
	Expanded bool
	// Name is the tool name ("read" / "grep"); it is what the header verbs from.
	Name string
	// Detail is the arg-derived phrase from DetailFromArgs (grep's carries the
	// pattern and scope). It is preferred over Path for the header target.
	Detail  string
	Theme   components.Theme
	Spinner *status.Spinner
	// OnToggle is called when the user expands/collapses.
	OnToggle func(expanded bool)

	titleH int // title row count; body clicks don't toggle (allow selection)
}

func (readBlock *ReadBlock) theme() components.Theme {
	if readBlock.Theme.Success.Fg.Kind == 0 && readBlock.Theme.Foreground.Fg.Kind == 0 {
		return components.DefaultTheme()
	}
	return readBlock.Theme
}

// HasBody reports whether the row has anything to show beyond its header.
func (readBlock *ReadBlock) HasBody() bool {
	return strings.TrimSpace(readBlock.Body) != "" || strings.TrimSpace(readBlock.Error) != ""
}

// Handle toggles expansion on Enter/space or a left-click on the title row.
func (readBlock *ReadBlock) Handle(ctx *components.EventContext, ev xui.Event) {
	if !readBlock.HasBody() {
		return
	}
	switch e := ev.(type) {
	case xui.KeyEvent:
		if e.Code == xui.KeyEnter || (e.Code == xui.KeyRune && e.Rune == ' ') {
			readBlock.toggle(ctx)
		}
	case xui.MouseEvent:
		if e.Action == xui.MousePress && e.Button == xui.MouseLeft && e.Y >= 0 && e.Y < readBlock.titleH {
			readBlock.toggle(ctx)
		}
	}
}

func (readBlock *ReadBlock) toggle(ctx *components.EventContext) {
	readBlock.Expanded = !readBlock.Expanded
	if readBlock.OnToggle != nil {
		readBlock.OnToggle(readBlock.Expanded)
	}
	ctx.ConsumeAndRedraw()
}

// CopyText returns the path, the line count, and the body.
func (readBlock *ReadBlock) CopyText() string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "%s", readBlock.displayPath())
	if n := readBlock.LineCount(); n > 0 {
		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, " (%d lines)", n)
	}
	if body := strings.TrimRight(readBlock.Body, "\n"); body != "" {
		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "\n%s", body)
	}
	return sb.String()
}

// LineCount counts the non-blank body lines.
func (readBlock *ReadBlock) LineCount() int {
	n := 0
	for ln := range strings.SplitSeq(readBlock.Body, "\n") {
		if strings.TrimSpace(ln) != "" {
			n++
		}
	}
	return n
}

// displayPath returns the plain path for the row, used by CopyText. The header
// uses headerTarget instead, which also folds in grep's pattern phrase.
func (readBlock *ReadBlock) displayPath() string {
	path := strings.TrimSpace(readBlock.Path)
	path = strings.TrimPrefix(path, "@file ")
	if base, _, ok := strings.Cut(path, "#"); ok {
		path = strings.TrimSpace(base)
	}
	if path == "" {
		return "file"
	}
	return path
}

// Draw renders the "✓ read path (N lines)" header and, when expanded, the body.
func (readBlock *ReadBlock) Draw(ctx components.DrawContext) components.Surface {
	th := readBlock.theme()
	w := ctx.Max.Width
	if w <= 0 {
		w = 40
	}

	titleWrapped := components.WrapSpans(readBlock.titleSpans(th), w, ctx.Method)
	readBlock.titleH = len(titleWrapped)

	var bodyLines []components.RichLine
	if readBlock.HasBody() {
		bodyW := w
		if bodyW > 2 {
			bodyW -= 2
		}
		// A failure is the one thing the user must see without expanding.
		showBody := readBlock.Expanded || strings.TrimSpace(readBlock.Error) != ""
		if showBody {
			if errText := strings.TrimSpace(readBlock.Error); errText != "" {
				bodyLines = append(bodyLines, components.WrapSpans([]components.Span{
					{Text: "Error: " + errText, Style: th.Destructive},
				}, bodyW, ctx.Method)...)
			}
			bodyLines = append(bodyLines, readBodyLines(readBlock.Body, th, bodyW, ctx.Method)...)
		}
	}

	h := len(titleWrapped) + len(bodyLines)
	h = max(h, 1)
	s := components.NewSurface(w, h, readBlock)
	y := 0
	for _, line := range titleWrapped {
		components.PaintSpans(&s, 0, y, line, ctx.Method)
		y++
	}
	for _, line := range bodyLines {
		components.PaintSpans(&s, 2, y, line, ctx.Method)
		y++
	}
	return s
}

// titleSpans builds the "✓ read path (N lines) ↓" header. For grep the detail is
// already a phrase ("grep \"cursor\" in ."), so the name is not repeated and the
// path is left out — the path lives inside every match line anyway.
func (readBlock *ReadBlock) titleSpans(th components.Theme) []components.Span {
	icon, iconSt := chrome.ToolIcon(readBlock.Status, th, readBlock.Spinner)
	spans := []components.Span{{Text: icon + " ", Style: iconSt}}

	// Always lead with the verb ("read" / "grep") then the target, so read and
	// grep rows read the same way and neither is a bare path.
	spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: readBlock.readerName() + " ", Style: th.ToolName})
	if target := readBlock.headerTarget(); target != "" && target != "file" {
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: target, Style: th.ToolName})
	}
	if n := readBlock.LineCount(); n > 0 {
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: fmt.Sprintf(" (%d lines)", n), Style: th.Muted})
	}
	if suf := chrome.StatusSuffix(readBlock.Status); suf != "" {
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: suf, Style: th.Muted})
	}
	if readBlock.HasBody() {
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: chrome.ExpandArrow(readBlock.Expanded), Style: th.Muted})
	}
	return spans
}

// headerTarget returns the text that identifies the row after the verb. A grep
// run carries an arg-derived phrase ("grep \"cursor\" in .") which is more
// informative than a path, so it is used with its own leading verb stripped —
// the header already prints one. Read carries a bare path.
func (readBlock *ReadBlock) headerTarget() string {
	verb := strings.ToLower(readBlock.readerName())
	for _, d := range []string{readBlock.Detail, readBlock.Path} {
		d = strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(d, "@file "))
		if d == "" || d == "file" {
			continue
		}
		if i := strings.Index(d, " "); i > 0 && strings.EqualFold(d[:i], verb) {
			d = strings.TrimSpace(d[i+1:])
		}
		if d != "" {
			return d
		}
	}
	return ""
}

// readerName names the tool when no target identifies the row.
func (readBlock *ReadBlock) readerName() string {
	if readBlock.Name != "" {
		return readBlock.Name
	}
	return "read"
}

// readBodyLines renders the tool output with a line-number gutter. The read tool
// already prints "  12|text"; grep prints "path:>>  12|text". Both are normalized
// to the same right-aligned gutter so read and grep rows look identical.
func readBodyLines(body string, th components.Theme, width int, method xui.WidthMethod) []components.RichLine {
	if width < 1 {
		width = 1
	}
	numSt := th.Muted
	textSt := th.Foreground
	textSt.Dim = true

	var out []components.RichLine
	for raw := range strings.SplitSeq(util.ReplaceAll(body, "\r", ""), "\n") {
		if strings.TrimSpace(raw) == "" {
			continue
		}
		no, rest := splitLineNumber(raw)
		numText := ""
		if no > 0 {
			numText = fmt.Sprintf("%6d ", no)
		}
		spans := []components.Span{
			{Text: numText, Style: numSt},
			{Text: rest, Style: textSt},
		}
		out = append(out, components.WrapSpans(spans, width, method)...)
	}
	return out
}

// splitLineNumber pulls a leading "  12|" or "path:>>  12|" gutter off a
// tool-output line, returning the number (0 when absent) and the remaining text.
func splitLineNumber(line string) (int, string) {
	rest := line
	// Drop a "path:" or "path:>> " prefix that grep prepends.
	if i := strings.LastIndex(rest, "|"); i >= 0 {
		head, tail := rest[:i], rest[i+1:]
		trimmed := strings.TrimLeft(head, " ")
		// The head may itself be "path:>>" — keep only its trailing digits.
		if j := strings.LastIndexAny(trimmed, ":>"); j >= 0 {
			trimmed = trimmed[j+1:]
		}
		trimmed = strings.TrimLeft(trimmed, " >")
		if n, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(trimmed)); err == nil {
			return n, tail
		}
	}
	return 0, rest
}
package block_test

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/block"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/status"
)

const readOutput = "@file haiku.txt\n     1\tcold bytes on the wire\n     2\ta green cursor waits alone\n     3\tthe build passes at last"

// strip drops the tool's leading "@file path" line, the same way the Mapper's
// stripReadHeader does before handing the body to ReadBlock.
func strip(body string) string {
	lines := strings.Split(body, "\n")
	for i, ln := range lines {
		if strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(ln), "@file ") {
			return strings.TrimLeft(
				strings.Join(append(append([]string(nil), lines[:i]...), lines[i+1:]...), "\n"),
				"\n",
			)
		}
	}
	return body
}

func readCard(t *testing.T, w *block.ReadBlock) string {
	t.Helper()
	return components.SurfaceText(w.Draw(components.DrawContext{Max: components.Size{Width: 74, Height: 40}}))
}

func TestReadBlockHeaderNamesToolAndPath(t *testing.T) {
	d := &block.ReadBlock{
		Name: "read", Path: "haiku.txt", Body: strip(readOutput),
		Status: status.ToolDone, Expanded: true, Theme: components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	got := readCard(t, d)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "read haiku.txt (3 lines)", "the header matches the edit-card shape")
	// The @file line is the tool's, not the card's: it must not double up.
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "@file", "no duplicated @file header inside the card")
}

func TestReadBlockGrepHeaderKeepsPattern(t *testing.T) {
	d := &block.ReadBlock{
		Name: "grep", Detail: `grep "cursor" in .`, Body: "a green cursor waits alone",
		Status: status.ToolDone, Expanded: true, Theme: components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	got := readCard(t, d)
	assert.Contains(t, got, `grep "cursor" in . (1 lines)`)
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "grep grep", "the header prints one verb, not two")
}

func TestReadBlockStripsGrepLinePrefix(t *testing.T) {
	// grep emits "path:>>  12|text"; ReadBlock normalizes it to the same gutter
	// read uses, so both row types look identical.
	d := &block.ReadBlock{
		Name: "grep", Detail: `grep "cursor" in .`, Body: "haiku.txt:>>\t 2|a green cursor waits alone",
		Status: status.ToolDone, Expanded: true, Theme: components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	got := readCard(t, d)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "a green cursor waits alone")
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "haiku.txt:>>", "the path:>> prefix is stripped")
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "2|", "the | separator is stripped")
}

func TestReadBlockFailedShowsError(t *testing.T) {
	d := &block.ReadBlock{
		Name: "read", Path: "missing.go", Error: "file not found",
		Status: status.ToolError, Theme: components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	require.True(t, d.HasBody(), "a failed read has a body: the error")
	assert.Contains(t, readCard(t, d), "Error:")
}

func TestReadBlockCopyText(t *testing.T) {
	d := &block.ReadBlock{Name: "read", Path: "haiku.txt", Body: strip(readOutput)}
	text := d.CopyText()
	assert.Contains(t, text, "haiku.txt (3 lines)")
	assert.Contains(t, text, "cold bytes on the wire")
}

func TestReadBlockLineCountIgnoresBlanks(t *testing.T) {
	d := &block.ReadBlock{Name: "read", Body: "a\n\n\nb\n"}
	assert.Equal(t, 2, d.LineCount(), "blank lines are not content")
}

func TestLastRunningChildPrefersInFlight(t *testing.T) {
	got := block.LastRunningChild([]block.ChildTool{
		{Name: "read", Detail: "haiku.txt", Status: status.ToolDone},
		{Name: "grep", Detail: "cursor in .", Status: status.ToolDone},
		{Name: "edit", Detail: "main.go", Status: status.ToolRunning},
		{Name: "read", Detail: "main.go", Status: status.ToolQueued},
	})
	assert.Equal(t, "edit · main.go", got, "the running tool wins over the queued one")

func TestLastRunningChildFallsBackToMostRecent(t *testing.T) {
	got := block.LastRunningChild([]block.ChildTool{
		{Name: "read", Detail: "haiku.txt", Status: status.ToolDone},
		{Name: "grep", Detail: "cursor in .", Status: status.ToolDone},

	assert.Equal(t, "grep · cursor in .", got,
		"a finished sub-agent still shows what it last did")
}

	assert.Empty(t, block.LastRunningChild([]block.ChildTool{{Name: "  ", Status: status.ToolRunning}}),
