package block

import (
	"fmt"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"

	"github.com/pulseaiclub/xui"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/chrome"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/todo"
)

// ChecklistBlock renders a project TODO.md as a live progress row.
//
//	☑ TODO.md 3 done, 2 open ▼
//	  ▸ Patch the parser
//	    still fails on a missing trailing newline
//	  ◦ Update the tests
//	  ✓ Read the current writer
//
// This is the a1 counterpart to Claude Code's TaskListV2. The difference is
// deliberate: there is no todo tool behind this. The agent writes a markdown
// file it already has tools for, and this row reads it — no schema, no
// persistence, no model cooperation needed for the row to exist.
type ChecklistBlock struct {
	// Path is the file the checklist was read from, shown in the header.
	Path  string
	Items []todo.Item
	// Expanded shows the item list; the counts always show.
	Expanded bool
	Theme    components.Theme
	// StaleFor counts file-editing tool rows since the checklist last moved.
	// Non-zero renders a staleness warning, because a checklist the agent
	// stopped updating is worse than no checklist.
	StaleFor int
	// MaxRows caps how many items render. Zero means the default.
	MaxRows  int
	OnToggle func(expanded bool)

	titleH int
}

// defaultChecklistRows matches the reference budget: keep the list legible
// without eating the transcript.
const defaultChecklistRows = 10

func (c *ChecklistBlock) theme() components.Theme {
	if c.Theme.Success.Fg.Kind == 0 && c.Theme.Foreground.Fg.Kind == 0 {
		return components.DefaultTheme()
	}
	return c.Theme
}

// HasBody reports whether there is anything beyond the header to show.
func (c *ChecklistBlock) HasBody() bool { return len(c.Items) > 0 }

func (c *ChecklistBlock) maxRows() int {
	if c.MaxRows > 0 {
		return c.MaxRows
	}
	return defaultChecklistRows
}

// Counts returns the done, open, and in-progress task counts. Boxes only:
// detail lines are attached notes, not claims about state.
func (c *ChecklistBlock) Counts() (done, open, inProgress int) { return c.tasks() }

// tasks counts the boxed items; details are attached, not counted.
func (c *ChecklistBlock) tasks() (done, open, inProgress int) {
	for _, it := range c.Items {
		if it.Detail {
			continue
		}
		switch {
		case it.Done:
			done++
		case it.InProgress:
			inProgress++
		default:
			open++
		}
	}
	return done, open, inProgress
}

// CopyText returns the counts and the item list, preserving each line's
// original shape — a detail line copies back as an unboxed bullet, because
// writing "- [ ]" over it would turn a note into a task the agent never claimed.
func (c *ChecklistBlock) CopyText() string {
	done, open, _ := c.tasks()
	var sb strings.Builder
	fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "%s (%d done, %d open)\n", c.Path, done, open)
	for _, it := range c.Items {
		prefix := strings.Repeat(" ", it.Indent)
		if it.Detail {
			fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "%s- %s\n", prefix, it.Text)
			continue
		}
		box := "- [ ]"
		switch {
		case it.Done:
			box = "- [x]"
		case it.InProgress:
			box = "- [~]"
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "%s%s %s\n", prefix, box, it.Text)
	}
	return sb.String()
}

// visibleItems selects which items render, in the reference's priority order:
// in-progress first, then open, then done — work still ahead of you outranks
// completed history, so the row is useful mid-run rather than a changelog.
// Details follow their parent task, and a task cut by the row cap takes its
// details with it rather than leaving them floating over an unrelated row.
func (c *ChecklistBlock) visibleItems() (shown []todo.Item, hidden int) {
	type entry struct {
		task    todo.Item
		details []todo.Item
	}
	var live, open, done []*entry
	var current *entry

	for _, it := range c.Items {
		if it.Detail {
			if current == nil {
				// A detail before any task has nothing to attach to.
				continue
			}
			current.details = append(current.details, it)
			continue
		}
		current = &entry{task: it}
		switch {
		case it.InProgress:
			live = append(live, current)
		case it.Done:
			done = append(done, current)
		default:
			open = append(open, current)
		}
	}

	ordered := make([]*entry, 0, len(live)+len(open)+len(done))
	ordered = append(ordered, live...)
	ordered = append(ordered, open...)
	ordered = append(ordered, done...)
	if len(ordered) > c.maxRows() {
		hidden = len(ordered) - c.maxRows()
		ordered = ordered[:c.maxRows()]
	}
	for _, e := range ordered {
		shown = append(shown, e.task)
		shown = append(shown, e.details...)
	}
	return shown, hidden
}

// Draw renders the header, the item list, and the staleness warning.
func (c *ChecklistBlock) Draw(ctx components.DrawContext) components.Surface {
	th := c.theme()
	w := ctx.Max.Width
	if w <= 0 {
		w = 40
	}

	titleLines := components.WrapSpans(c.titleSpans(th), w, ctx.Method)
	c.titleH = len(titleLines)

	var body []components.RichLine
	if c.Expanded && c.HasBody() {
		bodyW := w
		if bodyW > 2 {
			bodyW -= 2
		}
		shown, hidden := c.visibleItems()
		for _, it := range shown {
			body = append(body, components.WrapSpans(c.itemSpans(it, th), bodyW, ctx.Method)...)
		}
		if hidden > 0 {
			body = append(body, components.WrapSpans([]components.Span{
				{Text: fmt.Sprintf("… +%d more", hidden), Style: th.Muted},
			}, bodyW, ctx.Method)...)
		}
		if c.StaleFor > 0 {
			body = append(body, components.WrapSpans([]components.Span{
				{Text: fmt.Sprintf("⚠ %d file changes since this list moved", c.StaleFor), Style: th.Warning},
			}, bodyW, ctx.Method)...)
		}
	}

	h := len(titleLines) + len(body)
	h = max(h, 1)
	s := components.NewSurface(w, h, c)
	y := 0
	for _, line := range titleLines {
		components.PaintSpans(&s, 0, y, line, ctx.Method)
		y++
	}
	for _, line := range body {
		components.PaintSpans(&s, 2, y, line, ctx.Method)
		y++
	}
	return s
}

// Handle toggles expansion on Enter/space or a click on the title row.
func (c *ChecklistBlock) Handle(ctx *components.EventContext, ev xui.Event) {
	if !c.HasBody() {
		return
	}
	switch e := ev.(type) {
	case xui.KeyEvent:
		if e.Code == xui.KeyEnter || (e.Code == xui.KeyRune && e.Rune == ' ') {
			c.toggle(ctx)
		}
	case xui.MouseEvent:
		if e.Action == xui.MousePress && e.Button == xui.MouseLeft && e.Y >= 0 && e.Y < c.titleH {
			c.toggle(ctx)
		}
	}
}

func (c *ChecklistBlock) toggle(ctx *components.EventContext) {
	c.Expanded = !c.Expanded
	if c.OnToggle != nil {
		c.OnToggle(c.Expanded)
	}
	ctx.ConsumeAndRedraw()
}

// titleSpans builds "☑ TODO.md 2 done, 2 open ▼". The counts are the glanceable
// part, so they are always present even when the list is collapsed.
func (c *ChecklistBlock) titleSpans(th components.Theme) []components.Span {
	done, open, inProgress := c.tasks()
	spans := []components.Span{{Text: "☑ ", Style: th.Success}}
	spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: c.headerName(), Style: th.ToolName})
	spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: " ", Style: th.Muted})

	var stats []components.BylineItem
	if done > 0 {
		stats = append(stats, components.BylineItem{Text: fmt.Sprintf("%d done", done), Style: th.Success})
	}
	// An in-flight item is the answer to "what is it doing right now", which is
	// the first question during a run. It was counted but never printed.
	if inProgress > 0 {
		stats = append(stats, components.BylineItem{
			Text:  fmt.Sprintf("%d in progress", inProgress),
			Style: th.ToolName,
		})
	}
	if open > 0 {
		stats = append(stats, components.BylineItem{Text: fmt.Sprintf("%d open", open), Style: th.Muted})
	}
	spans = append(spans, components.BylineSpans(stats, th.Muted)...)

	if c.HasBody() {
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: chrome.ExpandArrow(c.Expanded), Style: th.Muted})
	}
	return spans
}

// headerName is the file's base name, not the path it was read from. The editor
// hands the block a joined path, and printing "/home/user/project/TODO.md" spent
// most of a narrow terminal's row on a directory the user is already in.
func (c *ChecklistBlock) headerName() string {
	return filepath.Base(strings.TrimSpace(c.Path))
}

// itemSpans renders one row with the reference's boxes: ✓ done, ◦ open, ▸ the
// in-flight item.
func (c *ChecklistBlock) itemSpans(it todo.Item, th components.Theme) []components.Span {
	if it.Detail {
		// A note, not a task: no box, so it can never be misread as something
		// the agent claimed to have done.
		return []components.Span{
			{Text: strings.Repeat(" ", it.Indent+2) + it.Text, Style: c.textStyle(it, th)},
		}
	}
	box := "◦ "
	switch {
	case it.Done:
		box = "✓ "
	case it.InProgress:
		box = "▸ "
	}
	return []components.Span{
		{Text: strings.Repeat(" ", it.Indent) + box, Style: c.boxStyle(it, th)},
		{Text: it.Text, Style: c.textStyle(it, th)},
	}
}

func (c *ChecklistBlock) boxStyle(it todo.Item, th components.Theme) xui.Style {
	switch {
	case it.Done:
		return th.Success
	case it.InProgress:
		return th.ToolName
	default:
		return th.Muted
	}
}

func (c *ChecklistBlock) textStyle(it todo.Item, th components.Theme) xui.Style {
	base := th.Foreground
	if it.Done || it.Detail {
		base.Dim = true
	}
	return base
}
package block_test

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/pulseaiclub/xui"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/block"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/todo"
)

func checklistCard(t *testing.T, c *block.ChecklistBlock) string {
	t.Helper()
	return components.SurfaceText(c.Draw(components.DrawContext{
		Max: components.Size{Width: 74, Height: 40},
	}))
}

func checklistItems() []todo.Item {
	return []todo.Item{
		{Text: "Read the current writer", Done: true},
		{Text: "handles escaped quotes", Indent: 2, Detail: true},
		{Text: "Patch the parser", InProgress: true},
		{Text: "Update the tests"},
		{Text: "Update the docs"},
	}
}

// drawChecklist renders a checklist row into text so these tests can assert on
// what the terminal shows. The DiffBlock-typed draw helper does not generalize.
func drawChecklist(c *block.ChecklistBlock, width int) string {
	s := c.Draw(components.DrawContext{Max: components.Size{Width: width, Height: 60}})
	return components.SurfaceText(s)
}

func TestChecklistBlockHeaderCounts(t *testing.T) {
	c := &block.ChecklistBlock{Path: "TODO.md", Items: checklistItems(), Theme: components.DefaultTheme()}
	got := checklistCard(t, c)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "☑ TODO.md")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "1 done")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "2 open", "the in-progress task is neither done nor open")
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "1 open", "details are not counted")
}

func TestChecklistBlockDetailsDoNotCount(t *testing.T) {
	c := &block.ChecklistBlock{
		Path: "TODO.md",
		Items: []todo.Item{
			{Text: "a", Done: true},
			{Text: "note one", Indent: 2, Detail: true},
			{Text: "note two", Indent: 2, Detail: true},
		},
		Theme: components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	got := checklistCard(t, c)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "1 done")
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "open", "two details did not become two open tasks")
}

func TestChecklistBlockCollapsedShowsOnlyHeader(t *testing.T) {
	c := &block.ChecklistBlock{Path: "TODO.md", Items: checklistItems(), Theme: components.DefaultTheme()}
	got := checklistCard(t, c)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "☑ TODO.md")
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "Patch the parser", "collapsed hides the items")
}

func TestChecklistBlockExpandedListsItems(t *testing.T) {
	c := &block.ChecklistBlock{
		Path: "TODO.md", Items: checklistItems(), Expanded: true, Theme: components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	got := checklistCard(t, c)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "✓ Read the current writer")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "▸ Patch the parser", "the in-flight item gets its own box")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "◦ Update the tests")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "handles escaped quotes", "details render under their parent")
}

func TestChecklistBlockInProgressIsListedFirst(t *testing.T) {
	c := &block.ChecklistBlock{
		Path: "TODO.md", Items: checklistItems(), Expanded: true, Theme: components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	got := checklistCard(t, c)
	lines := splitLines(got)
	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(lines), 2)
	// lines[0] is the header; the first item row is lines[1]. The reference's
	// ordering puts work still ahead of you above completed history.
	assert.Contains(t, lines[0], "☑ TODO.md")
	assert.Contains(t, lines[1], "Patch the parser", "in-progress sorts to the top")
	assert.Contains(t, lines[2], "Update the tests", "then open tasks")
}

func TestChecklistBlockRowCapAndHiddenCount(t *testing.T) {
	items := make([]todo.Item, 0, 12)
	for i := range 12 {
		items = append(items, todo.Item{Text: "task", Done: i%3 == 0})
	}
	c := &block.ChecklistBlock{
		Path: "TODO.md", Items: items, Expanded: true, Theme: components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	got := checklistCard(t, c)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "… +2 more", "the capped remainder is reported, not silently dropped")
	assert.Equal(t, 10, countChecklistRows(got), "at most MaxRows items render")
}

func TestChecklistBlockMaxRowsRespected(t *testing.T) {
	c := &block.ChecklistBlock{
		Path: "TODO.md", Items: checklistItems(), Expanded: true, MaxRows: 2,
		Theme: components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	got := checklistCard(t, c)
	assert.Equal(t, 2, countChecklistRows(got), "MaxRows items render")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "… +2 more", "the remainder counts tasks, not rows")
}

func TestChecklistBlockStalenessWarning(t *testing.T) {
	c := &block.ChecklistBlock{
		Path: "TODO.md", Items: checklistItems(), Expanded: true, StaleFor: 7,
		Theme: components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	assert.Contains(t, checklistCard(t, c), "⚠ 7 file changes since this list moved")
}

func TestChecklistBlockCopyText(t *testing.T) {
	c := &block.ChecklistBlock{Path: "TODO.md", Items: checklistItems()}
	got := c.CopyText()
	assert.Contains(t, got, "TODO.md (1 done, 2 open)")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "- [x] Read the current writer")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "- [~] Patch the parser")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "- [ ] Update the tests")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "  - handles escaped quotes", "indent survives into copy text")
}

func TestChecklistBlockToggle(t *testing.T) {
	c := &block.ChecklistBlock{Path: "TODO.md", Items: checklistItems(), Theme: components.DefaultTheme()}
	assert.False(t, c.Expanded)
	c.Handle(&components.EventContext{}, xui.KeyEvent{Press: true, Code: xui.KeyEnter})
	assert.True(t, c.Expanded)
	c.Handle(&components.EventContext{}, xui.KeyEvent{Press: true, Code: xui.KeyEnter})
	assert.False(t, c.Expanded)
}

func TestChecklistBlockEmptyHasNoBody(t *testing.T) {
	c := &block.ChecklistBlock{Path: "TODO.md", Theme: components.DefaultTheme()}
	assert.False(t, c.HasBody(), "an uncreated file is not a row")
	assert.Equal(t, "TODO.md (0 done, 0 open)\n", c.CopyText())
}

func splitLines(s string) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, ln := range strings.Split(s, "\n") {
		if strings.TrimSpace(ln) != "" {
			out = append(out, ln)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// countChecklistRows counts item rows: a box glyph, or the "+N more" trailer.
func countChecklistRows(s string) int {
	n := 0
	for _, ln := range splitLines(s) {
		if strings.Contains(ln, "☑") {
			continue
		}
		if strings.Contains(ln, "✓ ") || strings.Contains(ln, "◦ ") || strings.Contains(ln, "▸ ") {
			n++
		}
	}
	return n
}

// The editor hands the block a joined path; printing it whole spent most of a
// narrow terminal's row on a directory the user is already in.
func TestChecklistBlockHeaderUsesBaseName(t *testing.T) {
	c := &block.ChecklistBlock{
		Path:  "/home/solis/Documentos/Code/phi/TODO.md",
		Items: checklistItems(),
		Theme: components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	got := drawChecklist(c, 60)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "☑ TODO.md")
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "/home/solis", "the directory is not printed")
}

// The in-progress item answers "what is it doing right now", which is the first
// question during a run. It was counted but the header never showed it.
func TestChecklistBlockHeaderShowsInProgress(t *testing.T) {
	c := &block.ChecklistBlock{
		Path: "TODO.md",
		Items: []todo.Item{
			{Text: "done one", Done: true},
			{Text: "live one", InProgress: true},
			{Text: "open one"},
			{Text: "a note under it", Detail: true},
		},
		Theme: components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	got := drawChecklist(c, 80)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "1 done")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "1 in progress")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "1 open")
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "note", "details are not counted as open")
}
package block

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"github.com/pulseaiclub/xui"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/chrome"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/status"
)

// ReadGroupBlock is the collapsed form of a run of read-only calls.
//
//	🔍 Read 12 files, searched for 3 patterns ▼
//	  ├── ✓ read haiku.txt
//	  ├── ✓ grep "cursor" in .
//	  ╰── ✓ read main.go
//
// Claude Code folds consecutive reads/greps into one row reading "Read 12 files,
// searched for 3 patterns". a1 needs it more than the reference does: adding
// the read/grep cards earlier made each row large, so a 15-file exploration was
// 15 large cards. The counts keep the glanceable value; the expansion keeps
// every individual card reachable.
type ReadGroupBlock struct {
	// Detail is the already-composed summary, e.g. "Read 3 files, searched for
	// 2 patterns". Built by the session layer from the group's counts.
	Detail string
	// Hint is the most recent member's target, shown beside the counts so the
	// row says what it happened to be looking at last.
	Hint string
	// Status drives the header glyph.
	Status status.ToolStatus
	// Expanded shows the member rows.
	Expanded bool
	// Members returns the member rows, resolved at draw time so a live group
	// picks up results that arrived after this widget was built.
	Members  func() []ChildTool
	Theme    components.Theme
	Spinner  *status.Spinner
	OnToggle func(expanded bool)

	titleH int
}

func (g *ReadGroupBlock) theme() components.Theme {
	if g.Theme.Success.Fg.Kind == 0 && g.Theme.Foreground.Fg.Kind == 0 {
		return components.DefaultTheme()
	}
	return g.Theme
}

// HasBody reports whether the group has member rows to show.
func (g *ReadGroupBlock) HasBody() bool {
	return g.Members != nil && len(g.Members()) > 0
}

// CopyText returns the summary and every member's label.
func (g *ReadGroupBlock) CopyText() string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	sb.WriteString(g.Detail)
	if g.Hint != "" {
		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, " · %s", g.Hint)
	}
	if !g.HasBody() {
		return sb.String()
	}
	members := g.Members()
	sb.WriteString("\n")
	for i, m := range members {
		last := i == len(members)-1
		gate := "├── "
		if last {
			gate = "╰── "
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "%s%s %s\n", gate, m.Name, m.Detail)
	}
	return sb.String()
}

// Handle toggles expansion on Enter/space or a click on the title row.
func (g *ReadGroupBlock) Handle(ctx *components.EventContext, ev xui.Event) {
	if !g.HasBody() {
		return
	}
	switch e := ev.(type) {
	case xui.KeyEvent:
		if e.Code == xui.KeyEnter || (e.Code == xui.KeyRune && e.Rune == ' ') {
			g.toggle(ctx)
		}
	case xui.MouseEvent:
		if e.Action == xui.MousePress && e.Button == xui.MouseLeft && e.Y >= 0 && e.Y < g.titleH {
			g.toggle(ctx)
		}
	}
}

func (g *ReadGroupBlock) toggle(ctx *components.EventContext) {
	g.Expanded = !g.Expanded
	if g.OnToggle != nil {
		g.OnToggle(g.Expanded)
	}
	ctx.ConsumeAndRedraw()
}

// titleSpans builds the summary header. The verb tenses flip with liveness the
// way the reference's do: "Reading" while in flight, "Read" once resolved.
func (g *ReadGroupBlock) titleSpans(th components.Theme) []components.Span {
	icon, iconSt := chrome.ToolIcon(g.Status, th, g.Spinner)
	spans := []components.Span{{Text: icon + " ", Style: iconSt}}

	// The session layer composes the summary in the resolved tense; only the
	// in-flight form has to be re-derived here.
	detail := g.Detail
	if g.Status == status.ToolRunning {
		detail = tenseFlip(detail)
	}
	if detail != "" {
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: detail, Style: th.ToolName})
	}
	if hint := strings.TrimSpace(g.Hint); hint != "" && g.Status == status.ToolRunning {
		// Only while running: a resolved row's last target is history, and the
		// expanded members already carry every path.
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: " " + hint, Style: th.Muted})
	}
	if suf := chrome.StatusSuffix(g.Status); suf != "" {
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: suf, Style: th.Muted})
	}
	if g.HasBody() {
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: chrome.ExpandArrow(g.Expanded), Style: th.Muted})
	}
	return spans
}

// tenseFlip converts a resolved summary to its in-flight form.
func tenseFlip(s string) string {
	repl := strings.NewReplacer("Read ", "Reading ", "searched ", "searching ", "listed ", "listing ")
	return repl.Replace(s)
}

// Draw renders the summary header and, when expanded, one row per member.
func (g *ReadGroupBlock) Draw(ctx components.DrawContext) components.Surface {
	th := g.theme()
	w := ctx.Max.Width
	if w <= 0 {
		w = 40
	}

	titleLines := components.WrapSpans(g.titleSpans(th), w, ctx.Method)
	g.titleH = len(titleLines)

	var body []components.RichLine
	if g.Expanded && g.HasBody() {
		bodyW := w
		if bodyW > 2 {
			bodyW -= 2
		}
		members := g.Members()
		for i, m := range members {
			body = append(body, components.WrapSpans(g.memberSpans(m, i == len(members)-1, th), bodyW, ctx.Method)...)
		}
	}

	h := len(titleLines) + len(body)
	h = max(h, 1)
	s := components.NewSurface(w, h, g)
	y := 0
	for _, line := range titleLines {
		components.PaintSpans(&s, 0, y, line, ctx.Method)
		y++
	}
	for _, line := range body {
		components.PaintSpans(&s, 2, y, line, ctx.Method)
		y++
	}
	return s
}

// memberSpans renders one member row with tree gates, matching the sub-agent
// tree so the two expandable row types look alike.
func (g *ReadGroupBlock) memberSpans(m ChildTool, last bool, th components.Theme) []components.Span {
	gate := "├── "
	if last {
		gate = "╰── "
	}
	icon, iconSt := chrome.ToolIcon(m.Status, th, g.Spinner)
	spans := []components.Span{
		{Text: gate, Style: th.Muted},
		{Text: icon + " ", Style: iconSt},
		{Text: m.Name, Style: th.ToolName},
	}
	// A member with a summary shows it ahead of its detail: for a fetch, "200 OK
	// · 12 KB · 0.4s" is the answer and the url is the provenance, which is the
	// opposite priority to a read row where the path *is* the answer.
	if m.Summary != "" {
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: " " + m.Summary, Style: th.Muted})
		return spans
	}
	if m.Detail != "" {
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: " " + m.Detail, Style: th.Muted})
	}
	return spans
}
package block_test

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/pulseaiclub/xui"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/block"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/status"
)

func groupMembers() []block.ChildTool {
	return []block.ChildTool{
		{Name: "read", Detail: "haiku.txt", Status: status.ToolDone},
		{Name: "grep", Detail: `"cursor" in .`, Status: status.ToolDone},
		{Name: "read", Detail: "main.go", Status: status.ToolDone},
	}
}

func newGroup() *block.ReadGroupBlock {
	return &block.ReadGroupBlock{
		Detail:  "Read 2 files, searched for 1 pattern",
		Status:  status.ToolDone,
		Members: groupMembers,
		Theme:   components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
}

func TestReadGroupSummaryHeader(t *testing.T) {
	got := components.SurfaceText(newGroup().Draw(components.DrawContext{
		Max: components.Size{Width: 74, Height: 20},
	}))
	assert.Contains(t, got, "Read 2 files, searched for 1 pattern")
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "haiku.txt", "members stay behind the summary")
}

func TestReadGroupExpandedListsMembers(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGroup()
	g.Expanded = true
	got := components.SurfaceText(g.Draw(components.DrawContext{Max: components.Size{Width: 74, Height: 20}}))
	assert.Contains(t, got, "✓ read haiku.txt")
	assert.Contains(t, got, `✓ grep "cursor" in .`)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "✓ read main.go")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "├── ", "tree gates match the sub-agent rows")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "╰── ", "the last member gets the closing gate")
}

func TestReadGroupRunningUsesPresentTense(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGroup()
	g.Status = status.ToolRunning
	g.Hint = "main.go"
	got := components.SurfaceText(g.Draw(components.DrawContext{Max: components.Size{Width: 74, Height: 20}}))
	assert.Contains(t, got, "Reading 2 files", "in-flight tense")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "searching for 1 pattern")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "main.go", "the current target shows while running")
}

func TestReadGroupResolvedHidesHint(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGroup()
	g.Hint = "main.go"
	got := components.SurfaceText(g.Draw(components.DrawContext{Max: components.Size{Width: 74, Height: 20}}))
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "main.go",
		"a resolved row's last target is history; the expansion carries every path")
}

func TestReadGroupCopyText(t *testing.T) {
	got := newGroup().CopyText()
	assert.Contains(t, got, "Read 2 files, searched for 1 pattern")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "├── read haiku.txt")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "╰── read main.go")
}

func TestReadGroupToggle(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGroup()
	assert.False(t, g.Expanded)
	g.Handle(&components.EventContext{}, xui.KeyEvent{Press: true, Code: xui.KeyEnter})
	assert.True(t, g.Expanded)
	g.Handle(&components.EventContext{}, xui.KeyEvent{Press: true, Code: xui.KeyEnter})
	assert.False(t, g.Expanded)
}

func TestReadGroupNoMembersIsNotExpandable(t *testing.T) {
	g := &block.ReadGroupBlock{
		Detail: "Read 2 files", Status: status.ToolDone,
		Members: func() []block.ChildTool { return nil },
		Theme:   components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	assert.False(t, g.HasBody())
	require.Equal(t, "Read 2 files", g.CopyText())
}
package block

import (
	"strings"

	"github.com/pulseaiclub/xui"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/chrome"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/status"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/text"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/tree"
)

// ChildTool is one nested tool row under an AgentBlock (sub-agent tree).
type ChildTool struct {
	Name   string
	Detail string
	Status status.ToolStatus
	// Summary is the tool's one-line outcome, shown after Detail in a nested
	// row. Used by read groups, where a fetch member carries its status and
	// size rather than showing a bare url.
	Summary string
}

// LastRunningChild picks the child tool to name in an AgentBlock header.
//
// The SubagentStore appends children in completion order, so there is no
// ordering to trust for "which one is still running" — scanning is the honest
// answer. A running or queued child wins; otherwise the most recent child is
// returned, so a finished sub-agent still shows what it last did rather than
// going blank.
func LastRunningChild(children []ChildTool) string {
	label := func(c ChildTool) string {
		name := strings.TrimSpace(c.Name)
		if name == "" {
			return ""
		}
		if d := strings.TrimSpace(c.Detail); d != "" {
			return components.Byline(name, d)
		}
		return name
	}
	var latest string
	for _, c := range children {
		switch c.Status {
		case status.ToolRunning, status.ToolQueued:
			if l := label(c); l != "" {
				return l
			}
		case status.ToolDone, status.ToolError, status.ToolCancelled, status.ToolRejected:
			if l := label(c); l != "" {
				latest = l
			}
		}
	}
	return latest
}

// AgentBlock renders agent_spawn / agent_wait with an optional
// nested tool tree and a terminal markdown summary (not raw JSON).
type AgentBlock struct {
	Name     string
	Detail   string
	Status   status.ToolStatus
	Children []ChildTool
	// Activity names the child tool currently running, so the header shows
	// what a sub-agent is doing without expanding the tree. Claude Code calls
	// this lastToolInfo on AgentProgressLine.
	Activity string
	Summary  string // markdown; shown only when set
	Error    string
	Expanded bool
	Theme    components.Theme
	Spinner  *status.Spinner
	OnToggle func(expanded bool)

	titleH int
}

func (a *AgentBlock) theme() components.Theme {
	if a.Theme.Success.Fg.Kind == 0 && a.Theme.Foreground.Fg.Kind == 0 {
		return components.DefaultTheme()
	}
	return a.Theme
}

func (a *AgentBlock) hasBody() bool {
	return len(a.Children) > 0 || strings.TrimSpace(a.Summary) != "" || strings.TrimSpace(a.Error) != ""
}

// Handle toggles expansion on Enter/space or a left-click on the title row.
func (a *AgentBlock) Handle(ctx *components.EventContext, ev xui.Event) {
	if !a.hasBody() {
		return
	}
	switch e := ev.(type) {
	case xui.KeyEvent:
		if e.Code == xui.KeyEnter || (e.Code == xui.KeyRune && e.Rune == ' ') {
			a.Expanded = !a.Expanded
			if a.OnToggle != nil {
				a.OnToggle(a.Expanded)
			}
			ctx.ConsumeAndRedraw()
		}
	case xui.MouseEvent:
		if e.Action == xui.MousePress && e.Button == xui.MouseLeft && e.Y >= 0 && e.Y < a.titleH {
			a.Expanded = !a.Expanded
			if a.OnToggle != nil {
				a.OnToggle(a.Expanded)
			}
			ctx.ConsumeAndRedraw()
		}
	}
}

// CopyText returns name, detail, child lines, and summary.
func (a *AgentBlock) CopyText() string {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString(a.Name)
	if a.Detail != "" {
		b.WriteByte(' ')
		b.WriteString(a.Detail)
	}
	st := tree.DefaultStyle()
	for i, c := range a.Children {
		b.WriteByte('\n')
		b.WriteString(tree.PrefixForSiblings(len(a.Children), i, st))
		b.WriteString(chrome.ChildIcon(c.Status))
		b.WriteByte(' ')
		b.WriteString(c.Name)
		if c.Detail != "" {
			b.WriteByte(' ')
			b.WriteString(c.Detail)
		}
	}
	if sum := strings.TrimSpace(a.Summary); sum != "" {
		b.WriteByte('\n')
		b.WriteString(sum)
	}
	if err := strings.TrimSpace(a.Error); err != "" {
		b.WriteByte('\n')
		b.WriteString("Error: ")
		b.WriteString(err)
	}
	return b.String()
}

// Draw renders the agent title (icon + name + detail), the nested tool tree,
// and the markdown summary / error body when expanded.
func (a *AgentBlock) Draw(ctx components.DrawContext) components.Surface {
	th := a.theme()
	w := ctx.Max.Width
	if w <= 0 {
		w = 40
	}

	icon, iconSt := chrome.ToolIcon(a.Status, th, a.Spinner)
	spans := []components.Span{
		{Text: icon + " ", Style: iconSt},
		{Text: a.Name, Style: th.ToolName},
	}
	// The tree rows already name each child tool, but only when expanded. The
	// header is where the operator looks while a run is in flight, so the live
	// child goes there too.
	if a.Activity != "" && a.Status == status.ToolRunning {
		if d := strings.TrimSpace(a.Detail); d != "" {
			spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: " " + d, Style: th.Muted})
		}
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: " ", Style: th.Muted})
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: "→ " + a.Activity, Style: th.Muted})
	} else if a.Detail != "" {
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: " " + a.Detail, Style: th.Muted})
	}
	if suf := chrome.StatusSuffix(a.Status); suf != "" {
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: suf, Style: th.Muted})
	}
	if a.hasBody() {
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: chrome.ExpandArrow(a.Expanded), Style: th.Muted})
	}

	titleLines := components.WrapSpans(spans, w, ctx.Method)
	a.titleH = len(titleLines)

	var treeLines []components.RichLine
	var footLines []components.RichLine
	if a.Expanded && a.hasBody() {
		bodyW := w
		if bodyW > 2 {
			bodyW -= 2
		}
		st := tree.DefaultStyle()
		n := len(a.Children)
		for i, c := range a.Children {
			prefix := tree.PrefixForSiblings(n, i, st)
			cIcon, cSt := chrome.ToolIcon(c.Status, th, a.Spinner)
			row := []components.Span{
				{Text: prefix, Style: th.Muted},
				{Text: cIcon + " ", Style: cSt},
				{Text: c.Name, Style: th.ToolName},
			}
			if c.Detail != "" {
				row = append(row, components.Span{Text: " " + c.Detail, Style: th.Muted})
			}
			treeLines = append(treeLines, components.WrapSpans(row, w, ctx.Method)...)
		}
		if err := strings.TrimSpace(a.Error); err != "" {
			footLines = append(footLines, components.WrapSpans([]components.Span{
				{Text: "Error: " + err, Style: th.Destructive},
			}, bodyW, ctx.Method)...)
		}
		if sum := strings.TrimSpace(a.Summary); sum != "" {
			md := text.RenderMarkdown(sum, th)
			footLines = append(footLines, components.WrapSpans(md, bodyW, ctx.Method)...)
		}
	}

	h := len(titleLines) + len(treeLines) + len(footLines)
	h = max(h, 1)
	s := components.NewSurface(w, h, a)
	y := 0
	for _, line := range titleLines {
		components.PaintSpans(&s, 0, y, line, ctx.Method)
		y++
	}
	for _, line := range treeLines {
		components.PaintSpans(&s, 0, y, line, ctx.Method)
		y++
	}
	for _, line := range footLines {
		components.PaintSpans(&s, 2, y, line, ctx.Method)
		y++
	}
	return s
}
package block

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"github.com/pulseaiclub/xui"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/chrome"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/status"
)

// ToolBlock renders a generic tool_use row: status glyph, name,
// detail, and optional expandable output body.
type ToolBlock struct {
	Name   string
	Detail string
	// Summary is the tool's one-line outcome ("200 OK · 42.1 KB · 1.2s"), shown
	// after Detail once the call resolves. Distinct from Detail, which is the
	// call's identity for the whole run.
	Summary  string
	Output   string
	Error    string
	Status   status.ToolStatus
	Expanded bool
	Theme    components.Theme
	Spinner  *status.Spinner
	OnToggle func(expanded bool)

	titleH int
}

func (toolBlock *ToolBlock) theme() components.Theme {
	if toolBlock.Theme.Success.Fg.Kind == 0 && toolBlock.Theme.Foreground.Fg.Kind == 0 {
		return components.DefaultTheme()
	}
	return toolBlock.Theme
}

func (toolBlock *ToolBlock) hasBody() bool {
	return strings.TrimSpace(toolBlock.Output) != "" || strings.TrimSpace(toolBlock.Error) != ""
}

// Handle toggles expansion on Enter/space or a left-click on the title row.
func (toolBlock *ToolBlock) Handle(ctx *components.EventContext, ev xui.Event) {
	if !toolBlock.hasBody() {
		return
	}
	switch e := ev.(type) {
	case xui.KeyEvent:
		if e.Code == xui.KeyEnter || (e.Code == xui.KeyRune && e.Rune == ' ') {
			toolBlock.Expanded = !toolBlock.Expanded
			if toolBlock.OnToggle != nil {
				toolBlock.OnToggle(toolBlock.Expanded)
			}
			ctx.ConsumeAndRedraw()
		}
	case xui.MouseEvent:
		if e.Action == xui.MousePress && e.Button == xui.MouseLeft && e.Y >= 0 && e.Y < toolBlock.titleH {
			toolBlock.Expanded = !toolBlock.Expanded
			if toolBlock.OnToggle != nil {
				toolBlock.OnToggle(toolBlock.Expanded)
			}
			ctx.ConsumeAndRedraw()
		}
	}
}

// CopyText returns name, detail, and body.
func (toolBlock *ToolBlock) CopyText() string {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString(toolBlock.Name)
	if toolBlock.Detail != "" {
		b.WriteByte(' ')
		b.WriteString(toolBlock.Detail)
	}
	if out := strings.TrimSpace(toolBlock.Output); out != "" {
		b.WriteByte('\n')
		b.WriteString(out)
	}
	if err := strings.TrimSpace(toolBlock.Error); err != "" {
		b.WriteByte('\n')
		b.WriteString("Error: ")
		b.WriteString(err)
	}
	return b.String()
}

// resultStat summarizes how much came back from a finished tool, so the row
// reports its outcome without expanding. Empty while running, on failure, or
// when there is no output.
func (toolBlock *ToolBlock) resultStat() string {
	if toolBlock.Status != status.ToolDone {
		return ""
	}
	n := 0
	for ln := range strings.SplitSeq(toolBlock.Output, "\n") {
		if strings.TrimSpace(ln) != "" {
			n++
		}
	}
	switch n {
	case 0:
		return ""
	case 1:
		return "(1 line)"
	default:
		return fmt.Sprintf("(%d lines)", n)
	}
}

// Draw renders the tool status glyph, name, detail, and optional output body.
func (toolBlock *ToolBlock) Draw(ctx components.DrawContext) components.Surface {
	th := toolBlock.theme()
	w := ctx.Max.Width
	if w <= 0 {
		w = 40
	}

	icon, iconSt := chrome.ToolIcon(toolBlock.Status, th, toolBlock.Spinner)
	spans := []components.Span{
		{Text: icon + " ", Style: iconSt},
		{Text: toolBlock.Name, Style: th.ToolName},
	}
	if toolBlock.Detail != "" {
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: " " + toolBlock.Detail, Style: th.Muted})
	}
	if suf := chrome.StatusSuffix(toolBlock.Status); suf != "" {
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: suf, Style: th.Muted})
	}
	// The tool's own summary wins over the generic line count: "200 OK · 42.1 KB
	// · 1.2s" says something, "(412 lines)" does not. The fallback stays for the
	// tools that set no summary.
	if toolBlock.Summary != "" {
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: " " + toolBlock.Summary, Style: th.Muted})
	} else if stat := toolBlock.resultStat(); stat != "" {
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: " " + stat, Style: th.Muted})
	}
	if toolBlock.hasBody() {
		spans = append(spans, components.Span{Text: chrome.ExpandArrow(toolBlock.Expanded), Style: th.Muted})
	}

	titleLines := components.WrapSpans(spans, w, ctx.Method)
	toolBlock.titleH = len(titleLines)

	var bodyLines []components.RichLine
	if toolBlock.Expanded && toolBlock.hasBody() {
		bodyW := w
		if bodyW > 2 {
			bodyW -= 2
		}
		if err := strings.TrimSpace(toolBlock.Error); err != "" {
			bodyLines = append(bodyLines, components.WrapSpans([]components.Span{
				{Text: "Error: " + err, Style: th.Destructive},
			}, bodyW, ctx.Method)...)
		}
		if out := strings.TrimSpace(toolBlock.Output); out != "" {
			fg := th.Foreground
			fg.Dim = true
			bodyLines = append(bodyLines, components.WrapSpans([]components.Span{
				{Text: out, Style: fg},
			}, bodyW, ctx.Method)...)
		}
	}

	h := len(titleLines) + len(bodyLines)
	h = max(h, 1)
	s := components.NewSurface(w, h, toolBlock)
	y := 0
	for _, line := range titleLines {
		components.PaintSpans(&s, 0, y, line, ctx.Method)
		y++
	}
	for _, line := range bodyLines {
		components.PaintSpans(&s, 2, y, line, ctx.Method)
		y++
	}
	return s
}
package block

import (
	"github.com/pulseaiclub/xui"

	components "github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components"
)

// UserBlock renders a user prompt with success left rule + italic.
type UserBlock struct {
	Text  string
	Theme components.Theme
	// ItemID is the session item id this prompt came from. The transcript
	// cursor uses it to name a message for re-editing, so it has to survive
	// being a row rather than a raw message.
	ItemID string
}

// ItemID returns the session item id, or "" when the block was not built from
// a projected item (tests, the welcome screen).
func (userBlock *UserBlock) ItemIDString() string {
	if userBlock == nil {
		return ""
	}
	return userBlock.ItemID
}

func (userBlock *UserBlock) theme() components.Theme {
	if userBlock.Theme.Success.Fg.Kind == 0 && userBlock.Theme.Foreground.Fg.Kind == 0 {
		return components.DefaultTheme()
	}
	return userBlock.Theme
}

// Handle is a no-op; the user prompt is not interactive.
func (*UserBlock) Handle(_ *components.EventContext, _ xui.Event) {}

// CopyText returns the prompt body (without the left rule).
func (userBlock *UserBlock) CopyText() string { return userBlock.Text }

// Draw renders the prompt text with a success left rule and italic body.
func (userBlock *UserBlock) Draw(ctx components.DrawContext) components.Surface {
	th := userBlock.theme()
	w := ctx.Max.Width
	if w <= 0 {
		w = 40
	}
	body := th.Foreground
	body.Italic = true
	rule := th.IdentityOrSuccess()
	innerW := w - 2
	innerW = max(innerW, 1)
	lines := components.WrapSpans([]components.Span{{Text: userBlock.Text, Style: body}}, innerW, ctx.Method)
	h := len(lines)
	h = max(h, 1)
	s := components.NewSurface(w, h, userBlock)
	for y, line := range lines {
		// ▎ tiles full cell height; "|" leaves gaps between wrapped rows.
		s.SetCell(0, y, xui.Cell{Char: "▎", Width: 1, Style: rule})
		components.PaintSpans(&s, 2, y, line, ctx.Method)
	}
	return s
}
package block_test

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/block"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/status"
)

// bashText renders a bash row the way the terminal sees it, so these tests
// assert on visible output rather than on widget internals.
func bashText(b *block.BashBlock, width int) string {
	s := b.Draw(components.DrawContext{Max: components.Size{Width: width, Height: 60}})
	return components.SurfaceText(s)
}

func TestBashBlockCollapsedShowsTailNotWholeOutput(t *testing.T) {
	var out strings.Builder
	for i := 1; i <= 40; i++ {
		fmt.Fprintf(&out, "line %02d\n", i)
	}
	b := &block.BashBlock{
		Command: "go test ./...",
		Output:  out.String(),
		Status:  status.ToolDone,
		Theme:   components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	require.False(t, b.Expanded, "starts collapsed")

	got := bashText(b, 80)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "go test ./...", "the command is always shown")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "line 40", "the newest line is visible collapsed")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "… +32 more lines", "the hidden count is reported")
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "line 01", "the oldest line is not shown collapsed")
}

func TestBashBlockCollapsedShortOutputHasNoTrailer(t *testing.T) {
	b := &block.BashBlock{
		Command: "ls",
		Output:  "parser.go\nrun.go\n",
		Status:  status.ToolDone,
		Theme:   components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	got := bashText(b, 80)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "parser.go")
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "more lines", "a row within budget needs no trailer")
}

func TestBashBlockErrorIsNotTruncatedWhenCollapsed(t *testing.T) {
	var out strings.Builder
	for i := 1; i <= 30; i++ {
		fmt.Fprintf(&out, "err %02d\n", i)
	}
	b := &block.BashBlock{
		Command: "make",
		Output:  out.String(),
		Status:  status.ToolError,
		Theme:   components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	got := bashText(b, 80)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "err 01", "a failed command shows from the top when collapsed")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "err 30", "…and through the end")
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "more lines", "no trailer on the full error body")
}

func TestBashBlockExpandedBeatsCollapsedTail(t *testing.T) {
	var out strings.Builder
	for i := 1; i <= 20; i++ {
		fmt.Fprintf(&out, "line %02d\n", i)
	}
	b := &block.BashBlock{
		Command:  "go build ./...",
		Output:   out.String(),
		Status:   status.ToolDone,
		Expanded: true,
		Theme:    components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	got := bashText(b, 80)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "line 01", "expanded shows the first line")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "line 20", "expanded shows the last line")
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "more lines", "no trailer when expanded")
}

// A wrapped line costs several surface rows, so the tail must be measured on the
// rendered rows: one very long output line collapsed to a preview stays bounded.
func TestBashBlockTailCountsWrappedLines(t *testing.T) {
	b := &block.BashBlock{
		Command: "cat big.log",
		Output:  strings.Repeat("x", 600) + "\n" + "tail line\n",
		Status:  status.ToolDone,
		Theme:   components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	got := bashText(b, 40)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "tail line", "the newest line survives")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "more lines", "a wrapped flood is still counted and reported")
}

// The tool's own truncation notice must survive into the collapsed view, since
// it is the line that says where the full log went.
func TestBashBlockCollapsedKeepsToolTailNotice(t *testing.T) {
	b := &block.BashBlock{
		Command: "go test ./...",
		Output:  "…\n\n[Showing lines 993-1000 of 1000. Full output: /tmp/a1-bash-abc.log]",
		Status:  status.ToolDone,
		Theme:   components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	got := bashText(b, 80)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "Showing lines 993-1000 of 1000", "the dump link stays visible collapsed")
}

// Running bash with partial output: the user must watch progress live.
func TestRunningBashShowsLiveOutput(t *testing.T) {
	b := &block.BashBlock{Command: "go test ./...", Output: "ok\n", Status: status.ToolRunning, Theme: components.DefaultTheme()}
	got := bashText(b, 80)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "ok")
}

// Empty output, still running: nothing to tail, row must not panic or draw gaps.
func TestRunningBashNoOutput(t *testing.T) {
	b := &block.BashBlock{Command: "sleep 5", Status: status.ToolRunning, Theme: components.DefaultTheme()}
	got := bashText(b, 40)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "sleep 5")
}

// Output that is exactly the budget: no trailer, full display.
func TestExactBudgetNoTrailer(t *testing.T) {
	var out strings.Builder
	for i := 1; i <= 8; i++ {
		fmt.Fprintf(&out, "line %d\n", i)
	}
	b := &block.BashBlock{Command: "x", Output: out.String(), Status: status.ToolDone, Theme: components.DefaultTheme()}
	got := bashText(b, 80)
	assert.Contains(t, got, "line 1")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "line 8")
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "more lines")
}

// One line over budget: trailer says exactly 1.
func TestOneOverBudget(t *testing.T) {
	var out strings.Builder
	for i := 1; i <= 9; i++ {
		fmt.Fprintf(&out, "line %d\n", i)
	}
	b := &block.BashBlock{Command: "x", Output: out.String(), Status: status.ToolDone, Theme: components.DefaultTheme()}
	got := bashText(b, 80)
	assert.NotContains(t, got, "line 1 ")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "line 9")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "… +1 more lines")
}
package branchlist

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/listpicker"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/util/gitx"
)

func TestItemsAnchorsCurrentThenRecentThenLocalThenRemote(t *testing.T) {
	branches := []gitx.Branch{
		{Name: "main", Current: true},
		{Name: "fix/agent-wait", Subject: "wip"},
		{Name: "feature/old"},
		{Name: "origin/main", Remote: true},
	}

	items := Items(branches, []string{"feature/old", "main"})

	assert.Equal(t, []string{"main", "feature/old", "fix/agent-wait", "origin/main"}, primaries(items),
		"current anchors the list, then recent, then local by commit date, remotes last")
	assert.Len(t, items, 4, "no branch is listed twice")
}

func TestItemsIgnoresRecentNamesThatNoLongerExist(t *testing.T) {
	branches := []gitx.Branch{{Name: "main", Current: true}}

	items := Items(branches, []string{"deleted-branch", "main"})

	assert.Equal(t, []string{"main"}, primaries(items))
}

func TestRowsAreNameAndLastCommitOnly(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		branch  gitx.Branch
		leading string
		detail  string
	}{
		{
			name: "current branch",
			branch: gitx.Branch{
				Name: "main", Current: true, Upstream: "origin/main",
				Ahead: 2, Behind: 3, Committed: "3 hours ago", Subject: "chore: bump",
			},
			leading: "●",
			detail:  "chore: bump",
		},
		{
			name:   "diverged branch keeps the counts out of the row",
			branch: gitx.Branch{Name: "fix/y", Upstream: "origin/fix/y", Ahead: 2, Behind: 3, Subject: "wip"},
			detail: "wip",
		},
		{
			name:   "deleted upstream keeps the badge out of the row",
			branch: gitx.Branch{Name: "stale", Upstream: "origin/stale", Gone: true, Subject: "old"},
			detail: "old",
		},
		{
			name:   "remote branch",
			branch: gitx.Branch{Name: "origin/main", Remote: true, Subject: "chore: bump"},
			detail: "chore: bump",
		},
		{
			name:   "no commits yet",
			branch: gitx.Branch{Name: "empty"},
			detail: "",
		},
	}

	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			item := Items([]gitx.Branch{tc.branch}, nil)[0]
			assert.Equal(t, tc.branch.LocalName(), item.ID,
				"accepting a remote row checks out its local branch")
			assert.Equal(t, tc.branch.Name, item.Primary)
			assert.Equal(t, tc.leading, item.Leading)
			assert.Equal(t, tc.detail, item.Detail)
			assert.Empty(t, item.Badge, "two columns means no badge column")
			assert.Contains(t, item.Keywords, tc.branch.Name)
		})
	}
}

func TestRemoteRowAcceptsTheTrackingBranch(t *testing.T) {
	item := Items([]gitx.Branch{{Name: "origin/fix/one", Remote: true, Subject: "wip"}}, nil)[0]

	assert.Equal(t, "fix/one", item.ID)
	assert.Equal(t, "origin/fix/one", item.Primary, "the row still says where it lives")
}

func TestConfigKeepsBranchNamesReadable(t *testing.T) {
	cfg := Config()
	assert.Equal(t, "Branches", cfg.Title)
	assert.GreaterOrEqual(t, cfg.PrimaryWidth, len("fix/agent-wait-timeout"))
	assert.Contains(t, cfg.Hint, "switch")
}

// primaries is the display order; IDs collapse a remote row onto its local
// tracking branch, so they are asserted separately.
func primaries(items []listpicker.Item) []string {
	out := make([]string, 0, len(items))
	for _, item := range items {
		out = append(out, item.Primary)
	}
	return out
}
// Package branchlist maps gitx.Branch rows into listpicker items.
// A row is two columns — branch name, last commit — plus a dot for the branch
// HEAD is on. Ordering is the product decision here: where you are, where you
// came from, the local rest, then remotes.
package branchlist

import (
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/chrome"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/components/listpicker"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/util/gitx"
)

// branchColumn leaves room for the commit subject on an 80-column terminal.
// Longer names elide; typing three characters filters them back into view.
const branchColumn = 30

// Config returns chrome copy for the branch picker.
func Config() listpicker.ShowConfig {
	return listpicker.ShowConfig{
		Title:        "Branches",
		FilterHint:   "filter branches…",
		Empty:        "No branches yet — commit something first",
		EmptyFilter:  "No branches match %q",
		Hint:         chrome.ListHint("switch"),
		LeadingWidth: 2,
		PrimaryWidth: branchColumn,
	}
}

// Items orders branches for display and maps each one to a row.
// recent holds branch names in most-recently-checked-out order; names not in
// branches are ignored.
func Items(branches []gitx.Branch, recent []string) []listpicker.Item {
	byName := make(map[string]int, len(branches))
	for i, b := range branches {
		byName[b.Name] = i
	}
	out := make([]listpicker.Item, 0, len(branches))
	seen := make(map[string]bool, len(branches))
	add := func(b gitx.Branch) {
		if seen[b.Name] {
			return
		}
		seen[b.Name] = true
		out = append(out, row(b))
	}
	for _, b := range branches {
		if b.Current {
			add(b)
		}
	}
	for _, name := range recent {
		if i, ok := byName[name]; ok {
			add(branches[i])
		}
	}
	for _, b := range branches {
		if !b.Remote {
			add(b)
		}
	}
	for _, b := range branches {
		if b.Remote {
			add(b)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func row(b gitx.Branch) listpicker.Item {
	return listpicker.Item{
		// Accepting a remote row means checking out the local branch that tracks
		// it: git switch refuses a remote-tracking ref outright, and origin/feat
		// is what `git switch feat` is for.
		ID:       b.LocalName(),
		Leading:  currentMarker(b),
		Primary:  b.Name,
		Detail:   b.Subject,
		Keywords: b.Name + " " + b.Subject,
	}
}

// currentMarker keeps the one thing the list cannot be read without: which
// branch HEAD is on. Upstream state, ahead/behind counts, and badges stay out of
// the row — the list is for picking, not for auditing.
func currentMarker(b gitx.Branch) string {
	if b.Current {
		return "●"
	}
	return ""
}

func TestChatInputBorderLabels(t *testing.T) {
	c := &ChatInput{
		MinBodyRows: 3,
		TopLeftLabel: layout.BorderLabel{
			Text:  "nostromo—1—skill",
			Style: xui.Style{Fg: xui.RGBColor(0x5f, 0xc2, 0xc2)},
		},
		TopRightLabel: layout.BorderLabel{
			Text:  "high",
			Style: xui.Style{Fg: xui.IndexedColor(250)},
		},
		BottomLeftLabel: layout.BorderLabel{
			Text:  "↑1.2k ↓800 Σ2.0k 5% of 128k",
			Style: xui.Style{Fg: xui.RGBColor(0x7d, 0xc3, 0xff)},
		},
		BottomRightLabel: layout.BorderLabel{
			Text:  "~/Desktop/../examples/hello",
			Style: xui.Style{Fg: xui.IndexedColor(250)},
		},
		UseBlockCursor: true,
	}
	s := c.Draw(components.DrawContext{Max: components.Size{Width: 60, Height: 10}})
	assert.Equal(t, 60, s.Size.Width)
	assert.Equal(t, 5, s.Size.Height)
	// Corners
	assert.Equal(t, "╭", s.Buffer[0].Char)
	assert.Equal(t, "╮", s.Buffer[59].Char)
	bottom := 4 * 60
	assert.Equal(t, "╰", s.Buffer[bottom].Char)
	assert.Equal(t, "╯", s.Buffer[bottom+59].Char)
	top := rowString(s, 0)
	assert.Contains(t, top, "nostromo")
	assert.Contains(t, top, "high")
	bot := rowString(s, 4)
	assert.Contains(t, bot, "5% of 128k")
	assert.Contains(t, bot, "examples")
	require.NotNil(t, s.Cursor, "expected cursor")
}

func TestChatInputTyping(t *testing.T) {
	c := &ChatInput{MinBodyRows: 3}
	ctx := &components.EventContext{}
	c.Handle(ctx, xui.KeyEvent{Code: xui.KeyRune, Rune: 'h', Press: true})
	c.Handle(ctx, xui.KeyEvent{Code: xui.KeyRune, Rune: 'i', Press: true})
	assert.Equal(t, "hi", c.Value)
	assert.Equal(t, 2, c.Cursor)
	submitted := ""
	c.OnSubmit = func(s string) { submitted = s }
	c.Handle(ctx, xui.KeyEvent{Code: xui.KeyEnter, Press: true})
	assert.Equal(t, "hi", submitted)
}

func TestChatInputCtrlUClearsAll(t *testing.T) {
	c := &ChatInput{MinBodyRows: 3, Value: "hello\nworld", Cursor: 5}
	ctx := &components.EventContext{}
	changed := 0
	c.OnChange = func(string) { changed++ }
	c.Handle(ctx, xui.KeyEvent{Code: xui.KeyRune, Rune: 'u', Mods: xui.ModCtrl, Press: true})
	require.Empty(t, c.Value)
	require.Zero(t, c.Cursor)
	require.Equal(t, 1, changed)
	require.True(t, ctx.Consume)
	// A plain 'u' still types.
	c.Handle(ctx, xui.KeyEvent{Code: xui.KeyRune, Rune: 'u', Press: true})
	require.Equal(t, "u", c.Value)
}

func TestChatInputCtrlAEJumpLineBounds(t *testing.T) {
	c := &ChatInput{MinBodyRows: 3, Value: "hello world", Cursor: 5}
	ctx := &components.EventContext{}

	c.Handle(ctx, xui.KeyEvent{Code: xui.KeyRune, Rune: 'a', Mods: xui.ModCtrl, Press: true})

	require.True(t, ctx.Consume)
}

func TestChatInputMentionOpenDefersNav(t *testing.T) {
	c := &ChatInput{MinBodyRows: 3, Value: "@a\nb", Cursor: 2, MentionOpen: true}
	ctx := &components.EventContext{}
	c.Handle(ctx, xui.KeyEvent{Code: xui.KeyDown, Press: true})
	require.False(t, ctx.Consume, "Down should bubble when MentionOpen")
	require.Equal(t, 2, c.Cursor, "cursor should stay put")
	submitted := false
	c.OnSubmit = func(string) { submitted = true }
	ctx = &components.EventContext{}
	c.Handle(ctx, xui.KeyEvent{Code: xui.KeyEnter, Press: true})
	require.False(t, ctx.Consume, "Enter should bubble to picker when MentionOpen")
	require.False(t, submitted, "Enter should bubble to picker when MentionOpen")
}

		c.Handle(ctx, xui.KeyEvent{Code: xui.KeyEnter, Mods: mods, Press: true})

	}

func TestChatInputGrowsUntilMax(t *testing.T) {
	c := &ChatInput{MinBodyRows: 3, MaxBodyRows: 5, PaddingX: 1}

	require.Equal(t, 6, c.PreferredHeight(w, method), "4 lines preferred height")
	c.Value = "one\ntwo\nthree\nfour\nfive\nsix\nseven"
	require.Equal(t, 7, c.PreferredHeight(w, method), "over max preferred height (max body 5 + borders)")
	s := c.Draw(components.DrawContext{Max: components.Size{Width: w, Height: 20}, Method: method})
	require.Equal(t, 7, s.Size.Height, "draw height")
}

func TestChatInputCJKPasteNoContinuationReverse(t *testing.T) {
	c := &ChatInput{
		MinBodyRows:    3,
		MaxBodyRows:    8,
		PaddingX:       1,
		UseBlockCursor: true,
		CursorStyle:    xui.Style{Reverse: true},
	}
	ctx := &components.EventContext{}
	c.Handle(ctx, xui.PasteEvent{Text: "已修复中文粘贴"})
	s := c.Draw(components.DrawContext{Max: components.Size{Width: 40, Height: 10}, Method: xui.WidthUnicode})
	require.NotNil(t, s.Cursor, "expected cursor")
	cy := s.Cursor.Y
	revPrimaries := 0
	for x := 0; x < s.Size.Width; {
		cell := s.Buffer[cy*s.Size.Width+x]
		step := int(cell.Width)
		step = max(step, 1)
		if xui.StringWidth(cell.Char, xui.WidthUnicode) == 2 && cell.Width != 2 {
			require.FailNowf(t, "CJK width mismatch", "CJK %q stored with width %d at col %d", cell.Char, cell.Width, x)
		}
		if cell.Style.Reverse {
			revPrimaries++
		}
		x += step
	}
	require.Equal(t, 1, revPrimaries, "expected 1 reverse primary (block cursor)")
}

func TestChatInputPendingSkills(t *testing.T) {
	c := &ChatInput{
		MinBodyRows:   3,
		PendingSkills: []string{"building-plugins"},
		Theme:         components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	method := xui.WidthUnicode
	require.Equal(t, 6, c.PreferredHeight(60, method), "preferred height with pending skill")
	s := c.Draw(components.DrawContext{Max: components.Size{Width: 60, Height: 10}, Method: method})
	require.Equal(t, 6, s.Size.Height, "draw height")
	require.Equal(t, "╭", s.Buffer[0].Char, "skills must be inside the border")
	inner := rowString(s, 1)
	require.Contains(t, inner, "Skills:")
	require.Contains(t, inner, "building-plugins")
	underlined := false
	row := 1 * s.Size.Width
	for x := 0; x < s.Size.Width; x++ {
		if s.Buffer[row+x].Style.Underline {
			underlined = true
			break
		}
	}
	require.True(t, underlined, "expected underlined skill name")
	// Cursor sits on the editor line below the skills chip.
	require.NotNil(t, s.Cursor, "expected cursor below skills")
	require.Equal(t, 2, s.Cursor.Y, "cursor below skills")

	// Backspace on empty input pops the pending skill.
	ctx := &components.EventContext{}
	c.Handle(ctx, xui.KeyEvent{Code: xui.KeyBackspace, Press: true})
	require.Empty(t, c.PendingSkills, "expected pending skills cleared")
	require.Equal(t, 5, c.PreferredHeight(60, method), "preferred height after clear")
}

func TestChatInputAddPendingSkillDedup(t *testing.T) {
	c := &ChatInput{}
	c.AddPendingSkill("building-plugins")
	c.AddPendingSkill("building-plugins")
	c.AddPendingSkill("example-skill")
	require.Len(t, c.PendingSkills, 2)
	require.True(t, c.PopPendingSkill())
	require.Equal(t, "building-plugins", c.PendingSkills[0])
}

func rowString(s components.Surface, y int) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	for x := 0; x < s.Size.Width; x++ {
		ch := s.Buffer[y*s.Size.Width+x].Char
		if ch == "" {
			ch = " "
		}
		b.WriteString(ch)
	}
	return b.String()
}

func TestChatInputCJKBlockCursorKeepsWidth(t *testing.T) {
	c := &ChatInput{
		MinBodyRows:    3,
		PaddingX:       1,
		Value:          "中",
		Cursor:         0,
		UseBlockCursor: true,
		CursorStyle:    xui.Style{Reverse: true},
	}
	s := c.Draw(components.DrawContext{Max: components.Size{Width: 40, Height: 10}, Method: xui.WidthUnicode})
	require.NotNil(t, s.Cursor, "expected cursor")
	cx, cy := s.Cursor.X, s.Cursor.Y
	cell := s.Buffer[cy*s.Size.Width+cx]
	require.Equal(t, "中", cell.Char)
	require.EqualValues(t, 2, cell.Width)
}

func TestCursorAfterCJKPasteAtTextEnd(t *testing.T) {
	sample := "13个技能 你把这个 skills挪动过去"
	c := &ChatInput{MinBodyRows: 3, PaddingX: 1, UseBlockCursor: false}
	c.Handle(&components.EventContext{}, xui.PasteEvent{Text: sample})
	w := 80
	s := c.Draw(components.DrawContext{Max: components.Size{Width: w, Height: 10}, Method: xui.WidthUnicode})
	require.NotNil(t, s.Cursor, "nil cursor")
	cy := s.Cursor.Y
	var lastContentEnd int
	for x := 0; x < w; {
		cell := s.Buffer[cy*w+x]
		step := int(cell.Width)
		step = max(step, 1)
		if !cell.Trail && cell.Char != "" && cell.Char != " " && cell.Char != "│" {
			lastContentEnd = x + step
		}
		x += step
	}
	require.Equal(t, lastContentEnd, s.Cursor.X, "cursorX")
	// Insertion caret must not sit on the last CJK primary (IME would overlay it).
	cell := s.Buffer[cy*w+s.Cursor.X]
	require.NotEqual(t, 2, xui.StringWidth(cell.Char, xui.WidthUnicode), "cursor on wide glyph %q", cell.Char)
}

func TestActiveMention(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name   string
		value  string
		cursor int
		ok     bool
		query  string
		start  int
	}{
		{"empty", "", 0, false, "", 0},
		{"at alone", "@", 1, true, "", 0},
		{"at query", "@man", 4, true, "man", 0},
		{"mid query", "@manager", 4, true, "man", 0},
		{"after space", "see @go", 7, true, "go", 4},
		{"email", "a@b.com", 7, false, "", 0},
		{"after newline", "hi\n@x", 5, true, "x", 3},
		{"after paren", "(@file", 6, true, "file", 1},
		{"space ends", "@a b", 2, true, "a", 0},
		{"cursor before at", "@a", 0, false, "", 0},
		{"closed by space at cursor", "look @path ", 11, false, "", 0},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			q, start, end, ok := ActiveMention(tt.value, tt.cursor)
			require.Equal(t, tt.ok, ok, "q=%q", q)
			if !ok {
				return
			}
			require.Equal(t, tt.query, q, "query")
			require.Equal(t, tt.start, start, "start")
			require.Equal(t, tt.cursor, end, "end")
		})
	}
}

func TestReplaceRange(t *testing.T) {
	c := &ChatInput{Value: "see @man", Cursor: 8}
	c.ReplaceRange(4, 8, "@internal/session/manager.go")
	require.Equal(t, "see @internal/session/manager.go", c.Value)
	require.Equal(t, len(c.Value), c.Cursor)
}

func TestActiveQuestion(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name   string
		value  string
		cursor int
		ok     bool
		query  string
	}{
		{"empty", "", 0, false, ""},
		{"question alone", "?", 1, true, ""},
		{"prefix", "?ctrl", 5, true, "ctrl"},
		{"cursor at start", "?help", 0, false, ""},
		{"after space", "?help me", 8, false, ""},
		{"not at start", "hi?", 3, false, ""},
		{"slash", "/sessions", 9, false, ""},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			q, start, end, ok := ActiveQuestion(tt.value, tt.cursor)
			require.Equal(t, tt.ok, ok, "ok")
			if !ok {
				return
			}
			assert.Equal(t, tt.query, q, "query")
			assert.Equal(t, 0, start, "start")
			assert.Equal(t, tt.cursor, end, "end")
			assert.True(t, strings.HasPrefix(tt.value, "?"), "expected ? prefix")
		})
	}
}

func TestRefLabel(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name string
		ref  Ref
		want string
	}{
		{"single line", Ref{Path: "main.go", Start: 12, End: 12}, "main.go:12"},
		{"range", Ref{Path: "main.go", Start: 12, End: 18}, "main.go:12-18"},
		{"zero start clamps to one", Ref{Path: "main.go", Start: 0, End: 0}, "main.go:1"},
		{"backwards range collapses", Ref{Path: "main.go", Start: 9, End: 4}, "main.go:9"},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			assert.Equal(t, tc.want, tc.ref.Label())
		})
	}
}

func TestRefBlock(t *testing.T) {
	withLang := Ref{Path: "main.go", Start: 12, End: 13, Lang: "go", Text: "a := 1\nb := 2"}
	assert.Equal(t, "main.go:12-13\n```go\na := 1\nb := 2\n```", withLang.Block())

	bare := Ref{Path: "main.go", Start: 12, End: 12, Text: "x"}
	assert.Equal(t, "main.go:12\n```\nx\n```", bare.Block())

	// A selection that already ends with a newline must not gain a blank line.
	trailing := Ref{Path: "main.go", Start: 1, End: 1, Text: "x\n"}
	assert.Equal(t, "main.go:1\n```\nx\n```", trailing.Block())
}

func TestChatInputAddPendingRefRejectsAndDedups(t *testing.T) {
	c := &ChatInput{}
	c.AddPendingRef(Ref{Start: 1, End: 2, Text: "x"})
	c.AddPendingRef(Ref{Path: "main.go", Start: 1, End: 2})
	require.Empty(t, c.PendingRefs, "empty path or text carries nothing")

	ref := Ref{Path: "main.go", Start: 3, End: 4, Text: "x"}
	c.AddPendingRef(ref)
	c.AddPendingRef(ref)
	c.AddPendingRef(Ref{Path: "main.go", Start: 3, End: 5, Text: "x"})
	assert.Len(t, c.PendingRefs, 2)
}

func TestChatInputPendingRefsRow(t *testing.T) {
	c := &ChatInput{
		MinBodyRows:   3,
		PendingRefs:   []Ref{{Path: "main.go", Start: 12, End: 18, Lang: "go", Text: "x"}},
		PendingSkills: []string{"building-plugins"},
		Theme:         components.DefaultTheme(),
	}
	method := xui.WidthUnicode
	require.Equal(t, 7, c.PreferredHeight(60, method), "preferred height with a ref and a skill")

	s := c.Draw(components.DrawContext{Max: components.Size{Width: 60, Height: 10}, Method: method})
	require.Equal(t, 7, s.Size.Height, "draw height")
	// Refs paint before skills so the pending rows stay contiguous.
	require.Contains(t, rowString(s, 1), "Refs:")
	require.Contains(t, rowString(s, 1), "main.go:12-18")
	require.Contains(t, rowString(s, 2), "Skills:")
	require.NotNil(t, s.Cursor, "expected cursor below the pending rows")
	require.Equal(t, 3, s.Cursor.Y, "cursor below refs and skills")
}

func TestChatInputPopAndClearPendingRefs(t *testing.T) {
	c := &ChatInput{MinBodyRows: 3}
	base := c.PreferredHeight(40, xui.WidthUnicode)
	c.AddPendingRef(Ref{Path: "main.go", Start: 1, End: 2, Text: "x"})
	require.Equal(t, base+1, c.PreferredHeight(40, xui.WidthUnicode), "one row per pending refs")

	notified := 0
	c.OnPendingRefsChange = func([]Ref) { notified++ }
	require.True(t, c.PopPendingRef())
	require.False(t, c.PopPendingRef(), "nothing left to pop")
	require.Equal(t, 1, notified)
	require.Equal(t, base, c.PreferredHeight(40, xui.WidthUnicode))

	c.AddPendingRef(Ref{Path: "main.go", Start: 1, End: 2, Text: "x"})
	c.ClearPendingRefs()
	require.Empty(t, c.PendingRefs)
	require.Equal(t, 3, notified, "add and clear notify once each")
	c.ClearPendingRefs()
	require.Equal(t, 3, notified, "clearing an empty list stays silent")
}

func TestChatInputBackspacePopsPendingRef(t *testing.T) {
	c := &ChatInput{MinBodyRows: 3}
	c.AddPendingRef(Ref{Path: "main.go", Start: 1, End: 2, Text: "x"})
	c.Handle(&components.EventContext{}, xui.KeyEvent{Press: true, Code: xui.KeyBackspace})
	require.Empty(t, c.PendingRefs)
}
