// ConfigDoc is the JSON/YAML representation of the config editor document.
type ConfigDoc struct {
	Path           string             `yaml:"-"                         json:"path,omitempty"`
	Models         []ModelDoc         `yaml:"models"                    json:"models"`
	SkillPath      *string            `yaml:"skill_path,omitempty"      json:"skillPath,omitempty"`
	Permissions    *PermDoc           `yaml:"permissions,omitempty"     json:"permissions,omitempty"`
	Agents         *AgentsDoc         `yaml:"agents,omitempty"          json:"agents,omitempty"`
	SemanticSearch *SemanticSearchDoc `yaml:"semantic_search,omitempty" json:"semanticSearch,omitempty"`
	Judge          *JudgeDoc          `yaml:"judge,omitempty"           json:"judge,omitempty"`
	Browser        *BrowserDoc        `yaml:"browser,omitempty"         json:"browser,omitempty"`
	UI             *UIDoc             `yaml:"ui,omitempty"              json:"ui,omitempty"`
}

// ModelDoc describes a single model entry.
type ModelDoc struct {
	Name          string `yaml:"name"                     json:"name"`
	APIKey        string `yaml:"api_key"                  json:"apiKey"`
	BaseURL       string `yaml:"base_url"                 json:"baseUrl"`
	ContextWindow *int   `yaml:"context_window,omitempty" json:"contextWindow,omitempty"`
	ImageEnabled  *bool  `yaml:"image_enabled,omitempty"  json:"imageEnabled,omitempty"`
	API           string `yaml:"api,omitempty"            json:"api,omitempty"`
	ThinkEnabled  *bool  `yaml:"think_enabled,omitempty"  json:"thinkEnabled,omitempty"`
	ThinkLevel    string `yaml:"think_level,omitempty"    json:"thinkLevel,omitempty"`
	Default       bool   `yaml:"default,omitempty"        json:"default,omitempty"`
}

// PermDoc describes permissions settings.
type PermDoc struct {
	Mode                *string  `yaml:"mode,omitempty"                  json:"mode,omitempty"`
	WorkspaceOnlyWrites *bool    `yaml:"workspace_only_writes,omitempty" json:"workspaceOnlyWrites,omitempty"`
	AskTimeoutSec       *int     `yaml:"ask_timeout_sec,omitempty"       json:"askTimeoutSec,omitempty"`
	DangerouslyAllowAll *bool    `yaml:"dangerously_allow_all,omitempty" json:"dangerouslyAllowAll,omitempty"`
	Bash                *BashDoc `yaml:"bash,omitempty"                  json:"bash,omitempty"`
}

// BashDoc describes bash permission settings.
type BashDoc struct {
	Default *string  `yaml:"default,omitempty" json:"default,omitempty"`
	Allow   []string `yaml:"allow"             json:"allow,omitempty"`
	Deny    []string `yaml:"deny"              json:"deny,omitempty"`
}

// AgentsDoc describes agent settings.
type AgentsDoc struct {
	Enabled *bool            `yaml:"enabled,omitempty" json:"enabled,omitempty"`
	Models  *AgentsModelsDoc `yaml:"models,omitempty"  json:"models,omitempty"`
}

// AgentsModelsDoc describes model assignments for agent roles.
type AgentsModelsDoc struct {
	Explore string `yaml:"explore" json:"explore,omitempty"`
	Review  string `yaml:"review"  json:"review,omitempty"`
	Worker  string `yaml:"worker"  json:"worker,omitempty"`
}

// SemanticSearchDoc describes semantic search settings.
type SemanticSearchDoc struct {
	Enabled        bool   `yaml:"enabled"         json:"enabled"`
	OllamaBaseURL  string `yaml:"ollama_base_url" json:"ollamaBaseUrl"`
	EmbeddingModel string `yaml:"embedding_model" json:"embeddingModel"`
}

// JudgeDoc describes judge settings.
type JudgeDoc struct {
	Model         string `yaml:"model"           json:"model"`
	OllamaBaseURL string `yaml:"ollama_base_url" json:"ollamaBaseUrl"`
}

// BrowserDoc describes browser settings.
type BrowserDoc struct {
	Profiles []string `yaml:"profiles" json:"profiles"`
}

// UIDoc describes terminal UI presentation settings.
type UIDoc struct {
	// AutoExpandToolOutput is a pointer so an absent key round-trips as absent
	// (the resolver defaults it to true) rather than as an explicit false.
	AutoExpandToolOutput *bool `yaml:"auto_expand_tool_output" json:"autoExpandToolOutput"`
}

// ModelListRequest is the request body for /api/models.
type ModelListRequest struct {
	BaseURL string `json:"baseUrl"`
	APIKey  string `json:"apiKey"`
	Model   string `json:"model"`
	API     string `json:"api"`
}

type modelListItem struct {
	ID          string `json:"id"`
	Name        string `json:"name"`
	DisplayName string `json:"display_name"`
}

type modelListResponse struct {
	Data   []modelListItem `json:"data"`
	Models []modelListItem `json:"models"`
}

const (
	defaultOpenAIBaseURL  = "https://api.openai.com/v1"
	KiloGatewayBaseURL    = "https://api.kilo.ai/api/gateway"
	anthropicAPIVersion   = "2023-06-01"
	modelListRequestLimit = 15 * time.Second
	modelListBodyLimit    = int64(4 << 20)
)

// Handler bundles the config file path with shared config-server helpers.
type Handler struct {
	ConfigPath string
	configHTML []byte
}

//go:embed config.html
var embeddedConfigHTML []byte

// loadConfigHTML returns the editor document. The copy embedded in the binary
// wins so an installed binary works from any directory; locating it on disk was
// the only mechanism before embed and would silently 500 outside a source tree.
func loadConfigHTML() ([]byte, error) {
	if len(embeddedConfigHTML) > 0 {
		return embeddedConfigHTML, nil
	}
	path, err := locateConfigHTML()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return os.ReadFile(path)
}

func (h *Handler) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if (r.URL.Path == "/api/config" || r.URL.Path == "/api/models" || r.URL.Path == "/api/stats") &&
		!isLoopbackHost(r.Host) {
		writeConfigErr(w, http.StatusForbidden, errors.New("request origin is not allowed"))
		return
	}

	switch r.URL.Path {
	case "/":
		html, err := h.loadHTML()
		if err != nil {
			writeConfigErr(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err)
			return
		}
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/html; charset=utf-8")
		_, _ = w.Write(html)
	case "/api/config":
		h.handleConfig(w, r)
	case "/api/models":
		h.handleModels(w, r)
	case "/api/stats":
		h.handleStats(w, r)
	default:
		http.NotFound(w, r)
	}
}

func (h *Handler) loadHTML() ([]byte, error) {
	if len(h.configHTML) > 0 {
		return h.configHTML, nil
	}
	html, err := loadConfigHTML()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	h.configHTML = html
	return html, nil
}

func (h *Handler) handleConfig(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	switch r.Method {
	case http.MethodGet:
		doc, err := readConfigDoc(h.ConfigPath)
		if err != nil {
			writeConfigErr(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err)
			return
		}
		doc.Path = h.ConfigPath
		writeConfigJSON(w, doc)
	case http.MethodPost:
		if status, err := validateLocalJSONRequest(r); err != nil {
			writeConfigErr(w, status, err)
			return
		}
		var doc ConfigDoc
		if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&doc); err != nil {
			writeConfigErr(w, http.StatusBadRequest, fmt.Errorf("bad request: %w", err))
			return
		}
		if err := validateConfigDoc(&doc); err != nil {
			writeConfigErr(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err)
			return
		}
		if err := writeConfigDoc(h.ConfigPath, &doc); err != nil {
			writeConfigErr(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err)
			return
		}
		writeConfigJSON(w, map[string]string{"status": "saved"})
	default:
		http.Error(w, "method not allowed", http.StatusMethodNotAllowed)
	}
}

// handleModels fetches model IDs through the local config server so the page
// does not need cross-origin access to a provider API.
func (*Handler) handleModels(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if r.Method != http.MethodPost {
		http.Error(w, "method not allowed", http.StatusMethodNotAllowed)
		return
	}
	if status, err := validateLocalJSONRequest(r); err != nil {
		writeConfigErr(w, status, err)
		return
	}

	var input ModelListRequest
	if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&input); err != nil {
		writeConfigErr(w, http.StatusBadRequest, fmt.Errorf("bad request: %w", err))
		return
	}

	baseURL := strings.TrimSpace(input.BaseURL)
	apiKey := strings.TrimSpace(input.APIKey)
	anthropic := isAnthropicAPI(input.API, baseURL, input.Model)
	if baseURL == "" {
		if anthropic {
			baseURL = "https://api.anthropic.com"
		} else {
			baseURL = defaultOpenAIBaseURL
		}
	}
	endpoint, err := modelListEndpoint(baseURL, anthropic)
	if err != nil {
		writeConfigErr(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err)
		return
	}

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), modelListRequestLimit)
	defer cancel()
	request, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, endpoint, http.NoBody)
	if err != nil {
		writeConfigErr(w, http.StatusBadRequest, fmt.Errorf("build model list request: %w", err))
		return
	}
	request.Header.Set("Accept", "application/json")
	if anthropic {
		request.Header.Set("X-Api-Key", apiKey)
		request.Header.Set("Anthropic-Version", anthropicAPIVersion)
	} else {
		request.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+apiKey)
	}

	response, err := modelListHTTPClient().Do(request)
	if err != nil {
		writeConfigErr(w, http.StatusBadGateway, fmt.Errorf("fetch model list: %w", err))
		return
	}
	defer response.Body.Close()

	body, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(response.Body, modelListBodyLimit+1))
	if err != nil {
		writeConfigErr(w, http.StatusBadGateway, fmt.Errorf("read model list: %w", err))
		return
	}
	if int64(len(body)) > modelListBodyLimit {
		writeConfigErr(w, http.StatusBadGateway, errors.New("model list response is too large"))
		return
	}
	if response.StatusCode < http.StatusOK || response.StatusCode >= http.StatusMultipleChoices {
		message := strings.TrimSpace(string(body))
		if len(message) > 500 {
			message = message[:500]
		}
		if message == "" {
			message = response.Status
		}
		writeConfigErr(w, http.StatusBadGateway, fmt.Errorf("model list request failed: %s", message))
		return
	}

	var payload modelListResponse
	if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &payload); err != nil {
		writeConfigErr(w, http.StatusBadGateway, fmt.Errorf("decode model list: %w", err))
		return
	}
	models := collectModelIDs(append(payload.Data, payload.Models...))
	sort.Strings(models)
	writeConfigJSON(w, struct {
		Models []string `json:"models"`
	}{Models: models})
}

func (*Handler) handleStats(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if r.Method != http.MethodGet {
		http.Error(w, "method not allowed", http.StatusMethodNotAllowed)
		return
	}
	if !isLoopbackHost(r.Host) {
		writeConfigErr(w, http.StatusForbidden, errors.New("request origin is not allowed"))
		return
	}

	rec := telemetry.GlobalRecorder()
	snapshot := telemetry.Snapshot{}
	if rec != nil {
		snapshot = rec.Snapshot()
	}
	writeConfigJSON(w, snapshot)
}

func modelListHTTPClient() *http.Client {
	client := *util.DefaultHTTPClient()
	client.CheckRedirect = func(req *http.Request, via []*http.Request) error {
		if len(via) >= 10 {
			return errors.New("stopped after 10 redirects")
		}
		origin := via[0].URL
		if !strings.EqualFold(req.URL.Scheme, origin.Scheme) ||
			!strings.EqualFold(req.URL.Host, origin.Host) {
			return errors.New("model list redirect changed origin")
		}
		return nil
	}
	return &client
}

func isAnthropicAPI(api, baseURL, model string) bool {
	switch strings.TrimSpace(api) {
	case "Anthropic":
		return true
	case "OpenAI", "OpenAIResponses", "Gemini":
		return false
	}
	return strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(baseURL), "anthropic") ||
		strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(model)), "claude")
}

func modelListEndpoint(baseURL string, anthropic bool) (string, error) {
	u, err := url.Parse(strings.TrimSpace(baseURL))
	if err != nil || u.Scheme == "" || u.Host == "" {
		return "", errors.New("base URL must be an absolute HTTP(S) URL")
	}
	if u.Scheme != "http" && u.Scheme != "https" {
		return "", errors.New("base URL must use http or https")
	}

	path := strings.TrimRight(u.Path, "/")
	if !strings.HasSuffix(path, "/models") {
		if anthropic && !strings.HasSuffix(path, "/v1") {
			path += "/v1"
		}
		path += "/models"
	}
	u.Path = path
	u.RawPath = ""
	u.RawQuery = ""
	u.Fragment = ""
	return u.String(), nil
}

func collectModelIDs(items []modelListItem) []string {
	seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(items))
	models := make([]string, 0, len(items))
	for _, item := range items {
		id := strings.TrimSpace(item.ID)
		if id == "" {
			id = strings.TrimSpace(item.Name)
		}
		if id == "" {
			id = strings.TrimSpace(item.DisplayName)
		}
		if id == "" {
			continue
		}
		if _, ok := seen[id]; ok {
			continue
		}
		seen[id] = struct{}{}
		models = append(models, id)
	}
	return models
}

func validateLocalJSONRequest(r *http.Request) (int, error) {
	mediaType, _, err := mime.ParseMediaType(r.Header.Get("Content-Type"))
	if err != nil || mediaType != "application/json" {
		return http.StatusUnsupportedMediaType, errors.New("content type must be application/json")
	}
	origin := r.Header.Get("Origin")
	originURL, err := url.Parse(origin)
	if err != nil || origin == "" || originURL.Scheme == "" || originURL.Host == "" ||
		originURL.User != nil || originURL.Path != "" || originURL.RawQuery != "" || originURL.Fragment != "" {
		return http.StatusForbidden, errors.New("request origin is not allowed")
	}

	expectedScheme := "http"
	if r.TLS != nil {
		expectedScheme = "https"
	}
	if !strings.EqualFold(originURL.Scheme, expectedScheme) || !strings.EqualFold(originURL.Host, r.Host) {
		return http.StatusForbidden, errors.New("request origin is not allowed")
	}
	return 0, nil
}

func isLoopbackHost(rawHost string) bool {
	u, err := url.Parse("http://" + rawHost)
	if err != nil || u.Host != rawHost || u.User != nil || u.Path != "" {
		return false
	}
	hostname := u.Hostname()
	if strings.EqualFold(hostname, "localhost") {
		return true
	}
	ip := net.ParseIP(hostname)
	return ip != nil && ip.IsLoopback()
}

func readConfigDoc(path string) (*ConfigDoc, error) {
	doc := &ConfigDoc{}
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
			return doc, nil
		}
		return nil, err
	}
	if err := yaml.Unmarshal(data, doc); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return doc, nil
}

func validateConfigDoc(doc *ConfigDoc) error {
	if len(doc.Models) == 0 {
		return errors.New("at least one model is required")
	}
	hasDefault := false
	for i := range doc.Models {
		m := &doc.Models[i]
		if m.Name == "" {
			return fmt.Errorf("model %d has no name", i+1)
		}
		if !m.Default {
			continue
		}
		if hasDefault {
			return errors.New("only one model may be marked default")
		}
		hasDefault = true
		if m.APIKey == "" {
			return fmt.Errorf("default model %q is missing api_key", m.Name)
		}
	}
	if !hasDefault {
		doc.Models[0].Default = true
		if doc.Models[0].APIKey == "" {
			return fmt.Errorf("default model %q is missing api_key", doc.Models[0].Name)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

func writeConfigDoc(path string, doc *ConfigDoc) error {
	data, err := yaml.Marshal(doc)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if cur, err := os.ReadFile(path); err == nil {
		//nolint:gosec // G306: config backup stays user-readable
		if err := os.WriteFile(path+".bak", cur, 0o644); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("backup config: %w", err)
		}
	}
	return os.WriteFile(path, data, 0o644) //nolint:gosec // G306: config.yaml is meant to be user-readable
}

func writeConfigJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, v any) {
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	if err := json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v); err != nil {
		http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusInternalServerError)
	}
}

func writeConfigErr(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, err error) {
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	w.WriteHeader(status)
	_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(map[string]string{"error": err.Error()})
}

// Start launches the config editor webserver and returns the listener address
// plus a stop function. The caller owns the goroutine lifetime.
func Start(ctx context.Context, configPath string) (string, func(), error) {
	if ctx == nil {
		ctx = context.Background()
	}

	page, err := loadConfigHTML()
	if err != nil {
		return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("read config html: %w", err)
	}

	ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
	if err != nil {
		return "", nil, err
	}
	addr := ln.Addr().(*net.TCPAddr)
	pageURL := fmt.Sprintf("http://127.0.0.1:%d/", addr.Port)

	srv := &http.Server{
		Handler:           &Handler{ConfigPath: configPath, configHTML: page},
		ReadHeaderTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
	}

	errc := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() { errc <- srv.Serve(ln) }()

	stopped := make(chan struct{})
	stop := func() {
		_ = srv.Close()
		<-stopped
	}

	go func() {
		defer close(stopped)
		select {
		case err := <-errc:
			if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, http.ErrServerClosed) {
				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "config server error: %v\n", err)
			}
		case <-ctx.Done():
			_ = srv.Shutdown(context.Background())
		}
	}()

	return pageURL, stop, nil
}

func locateConfigHTML() (string, error) {
	start, err := os.Getwd()
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("get working directory: %w", err)
	}
	dir := start
	for {
		for _, rel := range []string{"config.html", filepath.Join("internal", "configserver", "config.html")} {
			candidate := filepath.Join(dir, rel)
			if info, err := os.Stat(candidate); err == nil && !info.IsDir() {
				return candidate, nil
			}
		}
		parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
		if parent == dir {
			break
		}
		dir = parent
	}
	return "", fmt.Errorf("config.html not found from %s", start)
}

// OpenBrowser best-effort opens url in the default browser.
func OpenBrowser(ctx context.Context, url string) {
	if ctx == nil {
		ctx = context.Background()
	}
	var cmd *exec.Cmd
	switch runtime.GOOS {
	case "darwin":
		cmd = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "open", url)
	case "linux":
		cmd = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "xdg-open", url)
	default:
		return
	}
	_ = cmd.Start()
}
package webserver

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/session"
)

// promptRequest is the body posted by the chat composer. SessionID selects the
// conversation ("" starts a new one); Prompt is the user text.
type promptRequest struct {
	SessionID string `json:"sessionId"`
	Prompt    string `json:"prompt"`
}

// askRequest answers a permission prompt raised mid-turn.
type askRequest struct {
	ID       string `json:"id"`
	Approved bool   `json:"approved"`
	Feedback string `json:"feedback"`
}

// cancelRequest names the session whose in-flight turn should stop.
type cancelRequest struct {
	SessionID string `json:"sessionId"`
}

// handlePage serves the single-document web UI.
func (s *Server) handlePage(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/html; charset=utf-8")
	w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-store")
	_, _ = w.Write(s.page)
}

// handleListSessions renders the sidebar session list as an htmx fragment.
func (s *Server) handleListSessions(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
	if !s.requireProject(w) {
		return
	}
	sessions, err := s.listSessions()
	if err != nil {
		writeStatus(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "list sessions: "+err.Error())
		return
	}
	renderFragment(w, sessionListFragment(sessions, s.pinStore().list()))
}

// handleTranscript renders a stored session's messages as an htmx fragment so
// switching sessions in the sidebar repaints the main pane.
func (s *Server) handleTranscript(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if !s.requireProject(w) {
		return
	}
	id := strings.TrimSpace(r.URL.Query().Get("id"))
	if id == "" {
		writeStatus(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "session id is required")
		return
	}
	snap, err := s.transcript(id)
	if err != nil {
		writeStatus(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())
		return
	}
	renderFragment(w, transcriptFragment(snap))
}

// handleSessionMeta returns one session's display title. The chat topbar shows
// a human label rather than the id, and the id is only minted server-side at the
// first prompt — before the sidebar has a row to read one from.
func (s *Server) handleSessionMeta(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if !s.requireProject(w) {
		return
	}
	id := strings.TrimSpace(r.URL.Query().Get("id"))
	if id == "" {
		writeStatus(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "session id is required")
		return
	}
	title, err := s.sessionTitle(id)
	if err != nil {
		writeStatus(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"id": id, "title": title})
}

// decodeBody reads the request body into v, accepting either JSON (the shape
// curl and fetch send) or form encoding (what htmx.ajax sends when called with
// values:). Saving one content-type branch in the client would mean the browser
// only ever sees one of the two, and both are part of this API's contract.
func decodeBody(r *http.Request, v any) error {
	ct := r.Header.Get("Content-Type")
	if strings.Contains(ct, "application/x-www-form-urlencoded") {
		if err := r.ParseForm(); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("bad form: %w", err)
		}
		form := formTarget(v)
		if form == nil {
			return errors.New("form decoding is not supported for this type")
		}
		return form(r.PostForm)
	}
	if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(v); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("bad request: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}

// formTarget returns the bound setter for a supported request type, so a new
// handler opts in to form support explicitly rather than silently ignoring
// posted fields.
func formTarget(v any) func(map[string][]string) error {
	switch t := v.(type) {
	case *promptRequest:
		return func(f map[string][]string) error {
			t.SessionID = firstFormValue(f, "sessionId")
			t.Prompt = firstFormValue(f, "prompt")
			return nil
		}
	case *askRequest:
		return func(f map[string][]string) error {
			t.ID = firstFormValue(f, "id")
			t.Approved = firstFormValue(f, "approved") == "true"
			t.Feedback = firstFormValue(f, "feedback")
			return nil
		}
	case *cancelRequest:
		return func(f map[string][]string) error {
			t.SessionID = firstFormValue(f, "sessionId")
			return nil
		}
	case *modeRequest:
		return func(f map[string][]string) error {
			t.Mode = firstFormValue(f, "mode")
			return nil
		}
	case *pinRequest:
		return func(f map[string][]string) error {
			t.SessionID = firstFormValue(f, "sessionId")
			return nil
		}
	}
	return nil
}

func firstFormValue(f map[string][]string, key string) string {
	if v, ok := f[key]; ok && len(v) > 0 {
		return v[0]
	}
	return ""
}

// handlePrompt starts one agent turn. The HTTP call returns as soon as the turn
// is scheduled so the browser is never holding an open connection while the
// model thinks; results stream over the SSE endpoint.
func (s *Server) handlePrompt(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if !s.requireProject(w) {
		return
	}
	var req promptRequest
	if err := decodeBody(r, &req); err != nil {
		writeStatus(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
		return
	}
	if strings.TrimSpace(req.Prompt) == "" {
		writeStatus(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "prompt is empty")
		return
	}

	le, err := s.liveFor(strings.TrimSpace(req.SessionID))
	if err != nil {
		writeStatus(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())
		return
	}
	sessionID := le.engine.SessionID()

	// Serialize turns: a second prompt waits for the first instead of
	// interleaving two streams into one transcript.
	//
	// The turn context is deliberately detached from r.Context(): this handler
	// returns 202 as soon as the turn is scheduled, so a request-scoped context
	// would be cancelled by the response write itself. It lives until the turn
	// finishes or /api/cancel cancels it.
	le.turn.Lock()
	//nolint:gosec // G118: the turn must outlive this request; /api/cancel stops it
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	le.cancel = cancel
	go func(prompt string) {
		defer le.turn.Unlock()
		defer cancel()
		s.runTurn(withSession(ctx, sessionID), le, prompt)
	}(req.Prompt)

	writeJSON(w, http.StatusAccepted, map[string]string{"sessionId": sessionID})
}

// runTurn drives one engine.Loop and projects its events onto the SSE hub.
func (s *Server) runTurn(ctx context.Context, le *liveEngine, prompt string) {
	sessionID := sessionFromContext(ctx)
	s.events().publish(sessionID, serverEvent{Kind: eventStatus, Status: &statusPayload{Text: "thinking…"}})

	var runErr error
	for ev, err := range le.engine.Loop(ctx, prompt, loopOpts()) {
		if err != nil {
			runErr = err
			break
		}
		s.projectEvent(sessionID, ev)
	}
	if runErr != nil {
		s.events().publish(sessionID, serverEvent{
			Kind:   eventStatus,
			Status: &statusPayload{Text: "error: " + runErr.Error()},
			Failed: true,
		})
		return
	}
	s.events().publish(sessionID, serverEvent{Kind: eventStatus, Status: &statusPayload{Text: "done"}})
	s.events().publish(sessionID, serverEvent{Kind: eventDone})
}

// projectEvent maps one session.Event onto the wire event kinds.
func (s *Server) projectEvent(sessionID string, ev session.Event) {
	switch e := ev.(type) {
	case session.AssistantMessageUpdate:
		var delta deltaPayload
		for _, b := range e.Message.Content {
			switch b.Type {
			case session.BlockText:
				delta.Text += b.Text
			case session.BlockThinking:
				delta.Reasoning += b.Text
			}
		}
		// The engine re-emits the whole accumulated message on every stream
		// chunk (including tool-call chunks that carry no text at all), so an
		// empty delta is noise the browser would only re-render over.
		if delta.Text == "" && delta.Reasoning == "" {
			return
		}
		s.events().publish(sessionID, serverEvent{Kind: eventDelta, Delta: &delta})
	case session.ToolData:
		run := toolEventPayload(e.Run)
		s.events().publish(sessionID, serverEvent{Kind: eventTool, Tool: &run})
	case session.CompactionStarted:
		s.events().
			publish(sessionID, serverEvent{Kind: eventStatus, Status: &statusPayload{Text: "compacting context…"}})
	case session.CompactionComplete:
		text := "compacted context"
		if e.Failed {
			text = "compaction failed"
		} else if e.TokensBefore > 0 {
			text = fmt.Sprintf("compacted context (%d tokens)", e.TokensBefore)
		}
		s.events().publish(sessionID, serverEvent{Kind: eventStatus, Status: &statusPayload{Text: text}})
	}
}

// handleCancel cancels the in-flight turn for a session.
func (s *Server) handleCancel(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var req cancelRequest
	if err := decodeBody(r, &req); err != nil {
		writeStatus(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
		return
	}
	s.mu.Lock()
	le, ok := s.engines[req.SessionID]
	if ok && le.cancel != nil {
		le.cancel()
	}
	s.mu.Unlock()
	if !ok {
		writeStatus(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session is not running")
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"status": "cancelled"})
}

// handleAsk answers an outstanding permission prompt.
func (s *Server) handleAsk(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var body askRequest
	if err := decodeBody(r, &body); err != nil {
		writeStatus(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
		return
	}
	if body.ID == "" {
		writeStatus(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "id is required")
		return
	}
	s.mu.Lock()
	ch, ok := s.pending[body.ID]
	s.mu.Unlock()
	if !ok {
		writeStatus(w, http.StatusNotFound, "no pending permission prompt with that id")
		return
	}
	select {
	case ch <- permissionAskResult(body.Approved, body.Feedback):
	default:
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"status": "ok"})
}

// handleEvents streams SSE for the browser. One stream serves every live
// session; each event carries its session id so a page can follow several
// conversations and stay subscribed across sidebar switches.
func (s *Server) handleEvents(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	flusher, ok := w.(http.Flusher)
	if !ok {
		writeStatus(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "streaming unsupported")
		return
	}
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
	w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
	w.Header().Set("Connection", "keep-alive")
	w.Header().Set("X-Accel-Buffering", "no")

	ch, release := s.events().subscribe()
	defer release()

	flusher.Flush()
	keepalive := time.NewTicker(20 * time.Second)
	defer keepalive.Stop()
	for {
		select {
		case <-r.Context().Done():
			return
		case <-keepalive.C:
			_, _ = w.Write([]byte(": keepalive\n\n"))
			flusher.Flush()
		case ev, ok := <-ch:
			if !ok {
				return
			}
			if err := writeSSE(w, ev); err != nil {
				return
			}
			flusher.Flush()
		}
	}
}

// writeSSE encodes one event as a named SSE message with a JSON data payload.
func writeSSE(w http.ResponseWriter, ev serverEvent) error {
	data, err := json.Marshal(ev)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	_, err = fmt.Fprintf(w, "event: %s\ndata: %s\n\n", ev.Kind, data)
	return err
}

// transcript loads a stored session and projects it for rendering.
func (s *Server) transcript(id string) (session.Snapshot, error) {
	le, err := s.liveFor(id)
	if err != nil {
		return session.Snapshot{}, err
	}
	return session.ReplaySnapshot(le.engine.Session().PathEntries(), le.engine.ToolDetail), nil
}

// ---- request / response helpers ----

func writeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, v any) {
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	w.WriteHeader(status)
	_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v)
}

func writeStatus(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, msg string) {
	writeJSON(w, status, map[string]string{"error": msg})
}
package webserver

import (
	"sync"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/session"
)

// serverEvent is one item pushed to a browser over the SSE channel. Kind picks
// which payload field is populated, so the wire shape stays flat and the
// frontend switch has no ambiguity between omitted vs zero values.
type serverEvent struct {
	Kind eventKind `json:"kind"`

	// SessionID tags the conversation the event belongs to. The browser keeps a
	// bubble per session so a page showing more than one conversation (or a
	// session created mid-stream) still routes text to the right place.
	SessionID string `json:"sessionId"`

	// Delta is assistant text or reasoning streamed for the in-flight turn.
	Delta *deltaPayload `json:"delta,omitempty"`

	// Tool is a tool run update (queued → in-progress → done/error).
	Tool *toolPayload `json:"tool,omitempty"`

	// Ask is an outstanding permission prompt. Answered through POST /api/ask.
	Ask *askPayload `json:"ask,omitempty"`

	// Status is a one-line lifecycle note ("thinking…", "compacting…", "done").
	Status *statusPayload `json:"status,omitempty"`

	// Failed marks the turn as ended with an error.
	Failed bool `json:"failed,omitempty"`
}

type eventKind string

const (
	eventSession eventKind = "session"
	eventDelta   eventKind = "delta"
	eventTool    eventKind = "tool"
	eventAsk     eventKind = "ask"
	eventStatus  eventKind = "status"
	eventDone    eventKind = "done"
)

// deltaPayload carries streamed assistant text. Text and Reasoning are the two
// visible streams; the client keeps each turn's authoritative copy and
// re-renders, because the engine emits accumulated (not incremental) text.
type deltaPayload struct {
	Text      string `json:"text"`
	Reasoning string `json:"reasoning"`
}

// toolPayload mirrors the fields of session.ToolRun the web UI renders. It
// exists so the wire names are pinned by this package rather than by whatever
// Go happens to export on the shared TUI type. Status is pre-stringified for
// the same reason.
type toolPayload struct {
	ToolUseID string `json:"toolUseId"`
	Name      string `json:"name"`
	Status    string `json:"status"`
	Detail    string `json:"detail,omitempty"`
	Output    string `json:"output,omitempty"`
	Error     string `json:"error,omitempty"`
}

func toolEventPayload(run session.ToolRun) toolPayload {
	return toolPayload{
		ToolUseID: run.ToolUseID,
		Name:      run.Name,
		Status:    run.Status.String(),
		Detail:    run.Detail,
		Output:    run.Output,
		Error:     run.Error,
	}
}

// askPayload is a permission prompt rendered in the browser.
type askPayload struct {
	ID     string `json:"id"`
	Tool   string `json:"tool"`
	Reason string `json:"reason"`
}

// statusPayload is a transient lifecycle line for the status pill.
type statusPayload struct {
	Text string `json:"text"`
}

// hub fans live events out to every connected browser. One stream serves the
// whole process: events are tagged with their session id and the client filters,
// which keeps a tab's subscription alive across session switches.
//
// There is deliberately no replay buffer. A client that attaches mid-turn (or
// reconnects after a drop) re-reads the transcript from the session store, which
// is the authoritative record, then follows the live stream from there.
type hub struct {
	mu  sync.Mutex
	sub map[chan serverEvent]struct{}
}

func newHub() *hub {
	return &hub{sub: map[chan serverEvent]struct{}{}}
}

// subscribe registers a channel for live events. The returned func must be
// called to release it.
func (h *hub) subscribe() (chan serverEvent, func()) {
	ch := make(chan serverEvent, 64)
	h.mu.Lock()
	if h.sub == nil {
		h.sub = map[chan serverEvent]struct{}{}
	}
	h.sub[ch] = struct{}{}
	h.mu.Unlock()
	return ch, func() {
		h.mu.Lock()
		delete(h.sub, ch)
		h.mu.Unlock()
	}
}

// publish delivers an event to every subscriber. Delivery is non-blocking: a
// stalled browser tab must not throttle the agent loop, so a subscriber that
// cannot keep up is detached instead of back-pressuring the turn.
func (h *hub) publish(sessionID string, ev serverEvent) {
	if ev.SessionID == "" {
		ev.SessionID = sessionID
	}
	h.mu.Lock()
	defer h.mu.Unlock()
	for ch := range h.sub {
		select {
		case ch <- ev:
		default:
			delete(h.sub, ch)
		}
	}
}
package webserver

import (
	"net/http"
	"strings"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/permission"
)

// modeRequest carries the requested permission mode. "cycle" advances to the
// next mode, which is how the switcher pill behaves on click.
type modeRequest struct {
	Mode string `json:"mode"`
}

// modeResponse is the switcher's state: the active mode plus every mode with
// its label and summary, so the client renders one static menu rather than
// hard-coding names that could drift from the Go constants.
type modeResponse struct {
	Mode    string      `json:"mode"`
	Label   string      `json:"label"`
	Summary string      `json:"summary"`
	Modes   []modeEntry `json:"modes"`
}

type modeEntry struct {
	Mode    string `json:"mode"`
	Label   string `json:"label"`
	Summary string `json:"summary"`
	Active  bool   `json:"active"`
}

// handleGetMode reports the live permission mode.
func (s *Server) handleGetMode(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, s.modeView())
}

// handleSetMode switches the permission mode and rebuilds the gate for every
// live engine. An unknown mode is rejected, so a typo can never silently land
// on interactive (which would green-light what the user just restricted).
func (s *Server) handleSetMode(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var req modeRequest
	if err := decodeBody(r, &req); err != nil {
		writeStatus(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
		return
	}
	modes := s.modeStore()

	mode := strings.TrimSpace(req.Mode)
	if mode == "cycle" {
		if err := s.setPermissionMode(modes.cycle()); err != nil {
			writeStatus(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())
			return
		}
		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, s.modeView())
		return
	}

	if err := s.setPermissionMode(permission.Mode(mode)); err != nil {
		writeStatus(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, s.modeView())
}

// modeView renders the switcher's current state.
func (s *Server) modeView() modeResponse {
	current := s.modeStore().mode()
	out := modeResponse{
		Mode:    string(current),
		Label:   modeLabel[current],
		Summary: modeSummary[current],
		Modes:   make([]modeEntry, 0, len(webPermissionModes)),
	}
	for _, m := range webPermissionModes {
		out.Modes = append(out.Modes, modeEntry{
			Mode:    string(m),
			Label:   modeLabel[m],
			Summary: modeSummary[m],
			Active:  m == current,
		})
	}
	return out
}

// pinRequest toggles a session's pin. A session with no turns has nothing to
// pin yet, so the id alone is enough.
type pinRequest struct {
	SessionID string `json:"sessionId"`
}

// pinResponse is the pin state after a toggle.
type pinResponse struct {
	SessionID string   `json:"sessionId"`
	Pinned    bool     `json:"pinned"`
	Pins      []string `json:"pins"`
}

// handleGetPins lists pinned session ids.
func (s *Server) handleGetPins(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
	pins := s.pinStore().list()
	if pins == nil {
		pins = []string{}
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, pinResponse{Pins: pins})
}

// handleTogglePin pins or unpins a session and reports the new state.
func (s *Server) handleTogglePin(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var req pinRequest
	if err := decodeBody(r, &req); err != nil {
		writeStatus(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
		return
	}
	id := strings.TrimSpace(req.SessionID)
	if id == "" {
		writeStatus(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "session id is required")
		return
	}
	pinned, err := s.pinStore().toggle(id)
	if err != nil {
		writeStatus(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, pinResponse{SessionID: id, Pinned: pinned, Pins: s.pinStore().list()})
}
package webserver

import (
	"fmt"
	"sync"
	"sync/atomic"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/agent"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/permission"
)

// webPermissionModes are the modes the switcher offers, in cycle order. They
// mirror controller.CyclePermissionMode so the two surfaces cannot drift: a user
// who switches to read-only in the browser gets what the terminal would give.
var webPermissionModes = permission.AllModes

// modeLabel is the switcher's short name for each mode.
var modeLabel = map[permission.Mode]string{
	permission.ModeInteractive:    "ask",
	permission.ModeReadonly:       "read-only",
	permission.ModeAutopilot:      "autopilot",
	permission.ModeHeadlessStrict: "strict",
	permission.ModeYolo:           "yolo",
}

// modeSummary explains what a mode does, so the name never has to be decoded
// from the policy tables. The yolo line is the warning, and it is blunt on
// purpose: a user scanning a dropdown needs to know what they are picking
// before they pick it, not after.
var modeSummary = map[permission.Mode]string{
	permission.ModeInteractive:    "prompts before anything risky",
	permission.ModeReadonly:       "reads and searches only, no writes or bash",
	permission.ModeAutopilot:      "allowlisted tools run without asking",
	permission.ModeHeadlessStrict: "anything needing approval is denied",
	permission.ModeYolo:           "no prompts at all — dangerous, denied tools stay denied",
}

// modeState is the live permission mode for the process. It is process-wide
// rather than per-session (like the TUI's controller): two tabs open on the same
// conversation must agree about whether a command will ship.
type modeState struct {
	// current holds a permission.Mode.
	current atomic.Value

	mu    sync.Mutex
	gates map[permission.Mode]permission.Gate
}

// loadGate returns the cached gate for mode, if one has been built.
func (m *modeState) loadGate(mode permission.Mode) (permission.Gate, bool) {
	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()
	g, ok := m.gates[mode]
	return g, ok && g != nil
}

// storeGate caches a gate for mode.
func (m *modeState) storeGate(mode permission.Mode, g permission.Gate) {
	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()
	if m.gates == nil {
		m.gates = map[permission.Mode]permission.Gate{}
	}
	m.gates[mode] = g
}

// newModeState returns a modeState in interactive.
func newModeState() *modeState {
	m := &modeState{}
	m.current.Store(permission.ModeInteractive)
	return m
}

// mode returns the active mode, defaulting to interactive for a fresh server.
func (m *modeState) mode() permission.Mode {
	if m == nil {
		return permission.ModeInteractive
	}
	if v, ok := m.current.Load().(permission.Mode); ok && v != "" {
		return v
	}
	return permission.ModeInteractive
}

// setMode validates and installs mode, reporting the previous one. An unknown
// mode is rejected rather than silently treated as interactive, which would
// quietly green-light tools the user believes are restricted.
func (m *modeState) setMode(mode permission.Mode) (permission.Mode, error) {
	if _, ok := modeSummary[mode]; !ok {
		return m.mode(), fmt.Errorf("web: unknown permission mode %q", mode)
	}
	prev := m.mode()
	m.current.Store(mode)
	return prev, nil
}

// cycle advances to the next mode and returns it.
func (m *modeState) cycle() permission.Mode {
	modes := webPermissionModes
	idx := 0
	for i, md := range modes {
		if md == m.mode() {
			idx = (i + 1) % len(modes)
			break
		}
	}
	m.current.Store(modes[idx])
	return modes[idx]
}

// policy returns a copy of the project policy with the current mode applied, so
// the gate the server hands to engines reflects the switcher rather than
// whatever the config file said.
func (m *modeState) policy(base permission.Policy) permission.Policy {
	p := base
	p.Mode = m.mode()
	if p.Mode == "" {
		p.Mode = permission.ModeInteractive
	}
	return p
}

// rebuildGate constructs a StaticGate for the current mode over the project
// policy, preserving APPA trajectory state from the previous gate so the label
// L=(R,t) survives a mode switch instead of resetting to Trusted.
func (m *modeState) rebuildGate(
	base permission.Policy,
	workspace string,
	prev permission.Gate,
) (permission.Gate, error) {
	var trajectory *permission.TrajectoryState
	if sg, ok := prev.(*permission.StaticGate); ok {
		trajectory = sg.Trajectory()
	}
	g, err := permission.NewGate(m.policy(base), workspace)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if trajectory != nil {
		g.SetTrajectory(trajectory)
	}
	return g, nil
}

// applyToEngines installs gate on every live engine. Engines created later pick
// it up in engineOptions, so this only has to touch the ones already running.
func (s *Server) applyToEngines(gate permission.Gate) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	engines := make([]*agent.Engine, 0, len(s.engines))
	for _, le := range s.engines {
		if le.engine != nil {
			engines = append(engines, le.engine)
		}
	}
	s.mu.Unlock()
	for _, e := range engines {
		e.SetPermission(gate, s.ask)
	}
}
package webserver

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"sync"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/session"
)

// pinnedSessions is the web surface's session-pin list: a JSON file under the
// project session directory, so pins travel with the workspace and the GUI never
// writes to the config file the CLI and TUI read. Writes replace the whole list
// (a pin toggle is a read-modify-write under the mutex, never a partial edit).
type pinnedSessions struct {
	mu   sync.Mutex
	path string
}

// pinnedFile is the on-disk shape. Sessions is the ordered pin list, newest
// pin first.
type pinnedFile struct {
	Sessions []string `json:"sessions"`
}

func newPinnedSessions(dir string) *pinnedSessions {
	return &pinnedSessions{path: filepath.Join(dir, "pins.json")}
}

// list returns the pinned session ids in order.
func (p *pinnedSessions) list() []string {
	p.mu.Lock()
	defer p.mu.Unlock()
	return p.read()
}

// toggle adds id to the pin list or removes it, reporting whether it is now
// pinned. An empty directory or an unreadable file reads as "nothing pinned".
func (p *pinnedSessions) toggle(id string) (pinned bool, err error) {
	p.mu.Lock()
	defer p.mu.Unlock()
	if p.path == "" {
		return false, errors.New("web: pin store is not configured")
	}
	current := p.read()
	out := make([]string, 0, len(current)+1)
	found := false
	for _, s := range current {
		if s == id {
			found = true
			continue
		}
		out = append(out, s)
	}
	if !found {
		out = append([]string{id}, out...)
	}
	if err := p.write(out); err != nil {
		return !found, err
	}
	return !found, nil
}

// read locks nothing: callers hold p.mu.
func (p *pinnedSessions) read() []string {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(p.path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil
	}
	var f pinnedFile
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &f); err != nil {
		// A corrupt pin file is cosmetic: an empty list degrades to "no pins",
		// which is what the sidebar renders for a fresh workspace anyway.
		return nil
	}
	out := make([]string, 0, len(f.Sessions))
	for _, s := range f.Sessions {
		if s = strings.TrimSpace(s); s != "" {
			out = append(out, s)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// write locks nothing: callers hold p.mu. It creates the parent directory so a
// first pin on a project that has never had a session works.
func (p *pinnedSessions) write(ids []string) error {
	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(p.path), 0o755); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("web: create pin dir: %w", err)
	}
	data, err := json.Marshal(pinnedFile{Sessions: ids})
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("web: encode pins: %w", err)
	}
	// 0600: pins are user-local state, not project config other users read.
	if err := os.WriteFile(p.path, data, 0o600); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("web: write pins: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}

// sessionTitle resolves a session id to its sidebar label: the first user
// message, trimmed. It falls back to the id's short form for a session whose
// file is unreadable or has no user text, so the topbar never shows a bare
// 32-char hex string.
func (s *Server) sessionTitle(id string) (string, error) {
	if s.proj == nil {
		return "", errors.New("web: project is not configured")
	}
	sessions, err := s.listSessions()
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("web: list sessions: %w", err)
	}
	for _, m := range sessions {
		if m.ID == id {
			if t := strings.TrimSpace(m.Preview); t != "" {
				return t, nil
			}
			break
		}
	}
	return shortSessionID(id), nil
}

// shortSessionID renders an id as a stable, readable fallback label.
func shortSessionID(id string) string {
	if len(id) > 12 {
		return id[:12] + "…"
	}
	return id
}

// sessionTitleFromMeta maps a listing row to its display label.
func sessionTitleFromMeta(m session.SessionMeta) string {
	if t := strings.TrimSpace(m.Preview); t != "" {
		return t
	}
	return shortSessionID(m.ID)
}
package webserver

import (
	_ "embed"
	"fmt"
	"html"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"regexp"
	"strings"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/session"
)

//go:embed chat.html
var page []byte

// Inline span matchers. They run after html.EscapeString, so the patterns only
// ever match already-escaped text and cannot reintroduce raw HTML.
var (
	inlineCodeRe = regexp.MustCompile("`([^`]+)`")
	bold         = regexp.MustCompile(`\*\*([^*]+)\*\*`)
	italic       = regexp.MustCompile(`\*([^*]+)\*`)
)

// inlineCode renders `code` spans, escaping the delimiter content again so a
// backtick pair inside escaped text still shows literally.
func inlineCode(s string) string {
	return inlineCodeRe.ReplaceAllString(s,
		`<code>$1</code>`)
}

// renderFragment writes an htmx fragment: raw HTML, never JSON, because the
// browser swaps it straight into the DOM.
func renderFragment(w http.ResponseWriter, html string) {
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/html; charset=utf-8")
	_, _ = io.WriteString(w, html)
}

// sessionListFragment renders the sidebar's session rows, pinned first, then
// newest first inside each group.
func sessionListFragment(sessions []session.SessionMeta, pins []string) string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	if len(sessions) == 0 {
		// No Tailwind utilities here: this fragment is swapped in by htmx after
		// load, and the Tailwind browser build only scans the classes present
		// in the initial document, so utility classes would silently no-op.
		sb.WriteString(`<p class="sessions-empty">No sessions yet. Start a new chat.</p>`)
		return sb.String()
	}
	pinned := pinnedSet(pins)
	for _, s := range orderByPin(sessions, pinned) {
		title := html.EscapeString(sessionTitleFromMeta(s))
		fmt.Fprintf(&sb,
			`<button type="button" class="session-row%[1]s" data-session-id="%[2]s" data-title="%[3]s">`+
				`<span class="session-pin" aria-hidden="true">%[4]s</span>`+
				`<span class="session-title">%[3]s</span>`+
				`<span class="session-meta">%[5]s · %[6]s</span>`+
				`</button>`,
			pinClass(pinned[s.ID]),
			html.EscapeString(s.ID),
			title,
			pinGlyph(pinned[s.ID]),
			html.EscapeString(formatMtime(s)),
			html.EscapeString(s.ID),
		)
	}
	return sb.String()
}

// pinnedSet indexes the pin list for cheap membership tests.
func pinnedSet(pins []string) map[string]bool {
	out := make(map[string]bool, len(pins))
	for _, p := range pins {
		out[p] = true
	}
	return out
}

// orderByPin puts pinned sessions first, preserving the input order (newest
// first) inside each group.
func orderByPin(sessions []session.SessionMeta, pinned map[string]bool) []session.SessionMeta {
	out := make([]session.SessionMeta, 0, len(sessions))
	for _, s := range sessions {
		if pinned[s.ID] {
			out = append(out, s)
		}
	}
	for _, s := range sessions {
		if !pinned[s.ID] {
			out = append(out, s)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func pinClass(pinned bool) string {
	if pinned {
		return " session-pinned"
	}
	return ""
}

// pinGlyph is the row's pin marker: filled for pinned, hollow otherwise.
func pinGlyph(pinned bool) string {
	if pinned {
		return "&#9733;"
	}
	return "&#9734;"
}

// transcriptFragment renders a stored transcript: user text, assistant text and
// thinking, tool runs, and compaction markers. An empty session renders the
// same start page the client draws, so switching to an unused session and
// clicking "New chat" look identical.
func transcriptFragment(snap session.Snapshot) string {
	if len(snap.Messages) == 0 {
		return emptyStateFragment()
	}
	var sb strings.Builder
	for _, m := range snap.Messages {
		switch m.Role {
		case session.RoleUser:
			fmt.Fprintf(&sb, `<div class="bubble bubble-user">%s</div>`, renderMarkdown(m.Text))
		case session.RoleAssistant:
			sb.WriteString(assistantBubble(m))
		case session.RoleCompaction:
			text := "Compacted context"
			if m.TokensBefore > 0 {
				text = fmt.Sprintf("Compacted context (%d tokens)", m.TokensBefore)
			}
			fmt.Fprintf(&sb, `<div class="bubble bubble-system">%s</div>`, html.EscapeString(text))
		}
	}
	sb.WriteString(toolsFragment(snap))
	return sb.String()
}

// emptyStateFragment is the landing state for a session with no messages. The
// ids match the client-side start page so both paths light up the same rules.
func emptyStateFragment() string {
	return `<div class="empty-state" id="start-page">` +
		`<h1>What can I do for you?</h1>` +
		`<p>Ask anything about this workspace.</p>` +
		`</div>`
}

// assistantBubble renders one assistant message: optional thinking disclosure,
// text blocks in order, then the tool runs it issued.
func assistantBubble(m session.Message) string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	sb.WriteString(`<div class="bubble bubble-assistant">`)
	var think, text strings.Builder
	for _, b := range m.Content {
		switch b.Type {
		case session.BlockThinking:
			think.WriteString(b.Text)
		case session.BlockText:
			text.WriteString(b.Text)
		case session.BlockToolUse:
			text.WriteString("\n\n→ ")
			text.WriteString(b.Name)
		}
	}
	if t := strings.TrimSpace(think.String()); t != "" {
		// Reasoning is free prose with its own line breaks; preformatted text
		// preserves them, whereas the markdown renderer would collapse each
		// line into its own paragraph.
		fmt.Fprintf(
			&sb,
			`<details class="thinking"><summary>Thinking</summary><div class="thinking-body">%s</div></details>`,
			html.EscapeString(t),
		)
	}
	if t := strings.TrimSpace(text.String()); t != "" {
		sb.WriteString(renderMarkdown(t))
	}
	if m.Usage.Reported() {
		usage := fmt.Sprintf("%d in · %d out", m.Usage.PromptTokens, m.Usage.CompletionTokens)
		if m.Usage.TPS > 0 {
			usage += fmt.Sprintf(" · %.0f tok/s", m.Usage.TPS)
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, `<div class="usage">%s</div>`, usage)
	}
	sb.WriteString(`</div>`)
	return sb.String()
}

// toolsFragment renders the tool rows of a snapshot below the transcript so
// they read as a trace of what the agent ran.
func toolsFragment(snap session.Snapshot) string {
	if len(snap.Tools) == 0 {
		return ""
	}
	var sb strings.Builder
	sb.WriteString(`<div class="tool-trace">`)
	for _, run := range snap.Tools {
		status := html.EscapeString(run.Status.String())
		fmt.Fprintf(&sb,
			`<div class="tool-row tool-%s" data-tool-id="%s">`+
				`<span class="tool-name">%s</span>`+
				`<span class="tool-status">%s</span>`+
				`<span class="tool-detail">%s</span>`+
				`</div>`,
			status,
			html.EscapeString(run.ToolUseID),
			html.EscapeString(run.Name),
			status,
			html.EscapeString(toolDetailText(run)),
		)
	}
	sb.WriteString(`</div>`)
	return sb.String()
}

// toolDetailText picks the most informative one-liner for a tool row.
func toolDetailText(run session.ToolRun) string {
	if run.Detail != "" {
		return run.Detail
	}
	if run.Error != "" {
		return run.Error
	}
	out := strings.TrimSpace(run.Output)
	if len(out) > 160 {
		return out[:160] + "…"
	}
	return out
}

// formatMtime renders a session's timestamp as a short label. SessionMeta
// carries the file's string timestamp; fall back to the mtime when the header
// did not parse one.
func formatMtime(s session.SessionMeta) string {
	if ts := strings.TrimSpace(s.Timestamp); ts != "" {
		return ts
	}
	return s.Mtime.Format("2006-01-02 15:04")
}

// loadPage reads the embedded web UI document. It is compiled into the
// binary, so no file is resolved at runtime and the server cannot fail to
// find its own page on another machine.
func loadPage() ([]byte, error) {
	return page, nil
}

// renderMarkdown is a deliberately small markdown subset renderer: fenced code,
// inline code, bold, italic, and paragraphs. The transcript is machine-generated
// text and code, so pulling in a full markdown dependency would dwarf the
// payload this UI needs.
func renderMarkdown(src string) string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	var code strings.Builder
	inCode := false

	lines := strings.Split(src, "\n")
	for i, line := range lines {
		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
		switch {
		case strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "```"):
			if !inCode {
				inCode = true
				code.Reset()
				continue
			}
			inCode = false
			fmt.Fprintf(&sb, `<pre><code>%s</code></pre>`, html.EscapeString(code.String()))
			continue
		case inCode:
			code.WriteString(line)
			if i+1 < len(lines) {
				code.WriteString("\n")
			}
			continue
		case trimmed == "":
			continue
		}
		sb.WriteString("<p>")
		sb.WriteString(inlineMarkdown(trimmed))
		sb.WriteString("</p>")
	}
	if inCode {
		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, `<pre><code>%s</code></pre>`, html.EscapeString(code.String()))
	}
	return sb.String()
}

// inlineMarkdown escapes then re-applies `code`, **bold**, and *italic* spans.
func inlineMarkdown(s string) string {
	s = html.EscapeString(s)
	s = bold.ReplaceAllString(s, "<strong>$1</strong>")
	s = italic.ReplaceAllString(s, "<em>$1</em>")
	return inlineCode(s)
}
package webserver

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/session"
)

// The transcript renders agent output, which is untrusted text. Nothing that
// passes through renderMarkdown may emit raw markup.
func TestRenderMarkdownEscapesHTML(t *testing.T) {
	out := renderMarkdown(`<script>alert(1)</script> & <b>bold</b> "quoted"`)
	assert.NotContains(t, out, "<script>")
	assert.NotContains(t, out, "<b>")
	assert.Contains(t, out, "&lt;script&gt;")
	assert.Contains(t, out, "&amp;")
}

func TestRenderMarkdownKeepsCodeFences(t *testing.T) {
	out := renderMarkdown("before\n\n```go\nfmt.Println(\"x\")\n```\n\nafter")
	assert.Contains(t, out, "<pre><code>")
	assert.Contains(t, out, "fmt.Println")
	// The fence body must be escaped, so a code block cannot smuggle tags.
	// html.EscapeString renders quotes as numeric entities.
	assert.Contains(t, out, "&#34;x&#34;")
	assert.NotContains(t, out, "\"x\"")
}

func TestRenderMarkdownInlineSpans(t *testing.T) {
	out := renderMarkdown("use `read` for **bold** and *italic* text")
	assert.Contains(t, out, "<code>read</code>")
	assert.Contains(t, out, "<strong>bold</strong>")
	assert.Contains(t, out, "<em>italic</em>")
}

func TestRenderMarkdownUnterminatedFenceStillRenders(t *testing.T) {
	// A stream that cuts off mid-fence must not lose the code it received.
	out := renderMarkdown("```\npartial code")
	assert.Contains(t, out, "partial code")
	assert.Contains(t, out, "<pre><code>")
}

func TestTranscriptFragmentEscapesUserText(t *testing.T) {
	snap := session.Snapshot{Messages: []session.Message{{
		Role: session.RoleUser,
		Text: `</div><script>alert("xss")</script>`,
	}}}
	out := transcriptFragment(snap)
	assert.NotContains(t, out, "<script>")
	assert.NotContains(t, out, "</div><script>")
	assert.Contains(t, out, "&lt;script&gt;")
}

func TestTranscriptFragmentMarksCompaction(t *testing.T) {
	snap := session.Snapshot{Messages: []session.Message{{
		Role:         session.RoleCompaction,
		TokensBefore: 4200,
	}}}
	out := transcriptFragment(snap)
	assert.Contains(t, out, "Compacted context (4200 tokens)")
}

func TestTranscriptFragmentUsageOmitsZeroTPS(t *testing.T) {
	snap := session.Snapshot{Messages: []session.Message{{
		Role:    session.RoleAssistant,
		Content: []session.ContentBlock{{Type: session.BlockText, Text: "answer"}},
		Usage:   session.TokenUsage{PromptTokens: 10, CompletionTokens: 4},
	}}}
	out := transcriptFragment(snap)
	assert.Contains(t, out, "10 in · 4 out")
	assert.NotContains(t, out, "tok/s", "a zero TPS must not print a meaningless rate")
}

func TestTranscriptFragmentEmptySessionShowsStartPage(t *testing.T) {
	out := transcriptFragment(session.Snapshot{})
	assert.Contains(t, out, `id="start-page"`, "an empty session must match the client-side start page")
	assert.Contains(t, out, "What can I do for you?")
}

func TestSessionListFragmentEscapesPreview(t *testing.T) {
	sessions := []session.SessionMeta{{
		ID:        "abc",
		Preview:   `<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>`,
		Timestamp: "2026-10-09T10-00-00",
	}}
	out := sessionListFragment(sessions, nil)
	assert.NotContains(t, out, "<img")
	assert.Contains(t, out, "&lt;img")
	assert.Contains(t, out, `data-session-id="abc"`)
	// The row carries its own title so the topbar can show a name once the
	// server mints the id (before the sidebar has a row to read one from).
	assert.Contains(t, out, `data-title="&lt;img`)
}

func TestSessionListFragmentEmptyState(t *testing.T) {
	out := sessionListFragment(nil, nil)
	assert.Contains(t, out, "sessions-empty")
	// No Tailwind utilities: this fragment is swapped in by htmx after load,
	// and the Tailwind browser build only scans the initial document.
	assert.NotContains(t, out, `class="px-`)
	assert.NotContains(t, out, `class="text-sm`)
}

func TestSessionListFragmentPinsFloatToTop(t *testing.T) {
	sessions := []session.SessionMeta{
		{ID: "newest", Preview: "newest", Mtime: time.Unix(300, 0)},
		{ID: "middle", Preview: "middle", Mtime: time.Unix(200, 0)},
		{ID: "oldest", Preview: "oldest", Mtime: time.Unix(100, 0)},
	}
	out := sessionListFragment(sessions, []string{"oldest"})
	firstIdx := strings.Index(out, `data-session-id="oldest"`)
	require.Positive(t, firstIdx, "the pinned session must be present")
	assert.Less(t, firstIdx, strings.Index(out, `data-session-id="newest"`),
		"a pinned session sorts above the newest unpinned one")
	assert.Contains(t, out, "session-pinned")
	// The pin glyph is a filled star only for the pinned row.
	assert.Equal(t, 1, strings.Count(out, "&#9733;"))
	assert.Equal(t, 2, strings.Count(out, "&#9734;"))
}

func TestOrderByPinPreservesInputOrderWithinGroups(t *testing.T) {
	sessions := []session.SessionMeta{
		{ID: "a"}, {ID: "b"}, {ID: "c"}, {ID: "d"},
	}
	got := orderByPin(sessions, pinnedSet([]string{"d", "b"}))
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"b", "d", "a", "c"}, ids(got),
		"pinned order follows the pin list; the rest keep their input order")
}

func ids(sessions []session.SessionMeta) []string {
	out := make([]string, 0, len(sessions))
	for _, s := range sessions {
		out = append(out, s.ID)
	}
	return out
}

func TestToolDetailTextPrefersDetailThenError(t *testing.T) {
	long := strings.Repeat("y", 400)
	assert.Equal(t, "ls -1", toolDetailText(session.ToolRun{Detail: "ls -1", Output: long}))
	assert.Equal(t, "boom", toolDetailText(session.ToolRun{Error: "boom", Output: long}))
	trimmed := toolDetailText(session.ToolRun{Output: long})
	require.True(t, strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "yyy"))
	assert.Contains(t, trimmed, "…", "a long output is truncated with an ellipsis")
	assert.LessOrEqual(t, len(trimmed), 160+len("…"), "a long output must be truncated to one line")
}
// Package webserver serves the htmx web chat UI for the a1 harness.
//
// It is a separate surface from the TUI: same agent engine, same session store,
// delivered over HTTP. The UI is a single HTML document (embedded) plus a small
// JSON/SSE API, so the binary stays self-contained and needs no build step or
// node toolchain on the user's machine.
//
// Concurrency model: one Engine per session, guarded by a per-session turn
// mutex, so a second prompt on the same session queues behind the first instead
// of interleaving two streams into one transcript.
package webserver

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/agent"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/configserver"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/permission"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/project"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/project/model"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/session"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/tools"
)

// DefaultPort is where `a1 --web` listens.
const DefaultPort = 9001

const (
	readHeaderTimeout = 15 * time.Second
	// askTimeout bounds how long a permission prompt may sit unanswered
	// before the tool call is denied.
	askTimeout = 10 * time.Minute
)

// Server owns the HTTP listener and the live engine sessions.
type Server struct {
	proj     *project.Project
	page     []byte
	http     *http.Server
	hub      *hub
	stopOnce sync.Once

	mu      sync.Mutex
	modes   *modeState
	pins    *pinnedSessions
	engines map[string]*liveEngine
	pending map[string]chan permission.AskResult
}

// liveEngine is one engine plus the turn mutex that serializes prompts on it
// and the cancel func for the in-flight turn.
type liveEngine struct {
	engine *agent.Engine
	turn   sync.Mutex
	cancel context.CancelFunc
}

// Start launches the web server on 127.0.0.1:port and returns the page URL
// plus a stop function. The caller owns the goroutine lifetime; stop is
// idempotent and safe to call from a defer.
func Start(ctx context.Context, proj *project.Project, port int) (string, func(), error) {
	if ctx == nil {
		ctx = context.Background()
	}
	if port <= 0 || port > 65535 {
		return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("web: port %d out of range", port)
	}
	if proj == nil {
		return "", nil, errors.New("web: project is required")
	}
	if err := proj.LoadConfig(); err != nil {
		return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("web: load config: %w", err)
	}

	page, err := loadPage()
	if err != nil {
		return "", nil, err
	}

	ln, err := (&net.ListenConfig{KeepAlive: readHeaderTimeout}).Listen(ctx, "tcp", fmt.Sprintf("127.0.0.1:%d", port))
	if err != nil {
		return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("web: listen on 127.0.0.1:%d: %w", port, err)
	}

	srv := &Server{
		proj:    proj,
		page:    page,
		hub:     newHub(),
		modes:   newModeState(),
		pins:    newPinnedSessions(proj.SessionDir()),
		engines: map[string]*liveEngine{},
		pending: map[string]chan permission.AskResult{},
	}
	srv.http = &http.Server{
		Handler:           srv.routes(),
		ReadHeaderTimeout: readHeaderTimeout,
	}

	errc := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() { errc <- srv.http.Serve(ln) }()

	stopped := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		defer close(stopped)
		select {
		case err := <-errc:
			if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, http.ErrServerClosed) {
				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "web server error: %v\n", err)
			}
		case <-ctx.Done():
			// Shutdown with the caller's context: an interrupt already cancelled
			// it, so a fresh Background would make this graceful drain hang for
			// as long as any in-flight turn takes to finish.
			_ = srv.http.Shutdown(ctx)
		}
	}()

	stop := func() {
		srv.stopOnce.Do(func() { _ = srv.http.Close() })
		<-stopped
	}

	return fmt.Sprintf("http://127.0.0.1:%d/", port), stop, nil
}

// routes wires the page, the session API, the SSE stream, and the config editor.
func (s *Server) routes() http.Handler {
	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /{$}", s.handlePage)
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/events", s.handleEvents)
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/sessions", s.handleListSessions)
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/transcript", s.handleTranscript)
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/session", s.handleSessionMeta)
	mux.HandleFunc("POST /api/prompt", s.handlePrompt)
	mux.HandleFunc("POST /api/cancel", s.handleCancel)
	mux.HandleFunc("POST /api/ask", s.handleAsk)

	// Permission mode switching and session pins.
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/mode", s.handleGetMode)
	mux.HandleFunc("POST /api/mode", s.handleSetMode)
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/pins", s.handleGetPins)
	mux.HandleFunc("POST /api/pin", s.handleTogglePin)

	// The config editor is a second document served from the same origin, so a
	// browser already on the settings page can call back without CORS. Its API
	// paths (/api/config, /api/models, /api/stats) do not collide with the chat
	// API above, and the Handler itself enforces the loopback + JSON-origin
	// checks. Mounting it here means `a1 --web` needs no second server.
	s.configRoutes(mux)
	return mux
}

// configRoutes mounts the config editor's page and API. The configserver
// Handler is reused as-is (same code path as `a1 config`), so the editor can
// never drift from the CLI surface.
func (s *Server) configRoutes(mux *http.ServeMux) {
	cfg := &configserver.Handler{ConfigPath: s.configPath()}

	// The editor document lives at /settings, but configserver.Handler matches
	// on the exact path "/" for its page. Rewrite just that one request so the
	// document is served, and leave every API path untouched: config.html's
	// fetches are root-relative (/api/config) and routed directly below.
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /settings", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		cfg.ServeHTTP(w, editorPageRequest(r))
	})

	for _, route := range []string{"GET /api/config", "GET /api/stats", "POST /api/config"} {
		mux.HandleFunc(route, cfg.ServeHTTP)
	}
	mux.HandleFunc("POST /api/models", cfg.ServeHTTP)
}

// configPath resolves the config file the editor should read and write. It is
// the project's global config file, matching what `a1 config` opens.
func (s *Server) configPath() string {
	if s.proj != nil {
		return s.proj.Global().ConfigFile()
	}
	// A Server built without a project (tests) still answers the API; the
	// Handler treats a non-existent path as an empty document.
	return ""
}

// liveFor returns the engine for a session id, creating it on first use.
// An empty id starts a brand-new persisted session (the "new chat" path).
func (s *Server) liveFor(sessionID string) (*liveEngine, error) {
	// Resolve the gate before taking s.mu: gate() reads the mode store, and a
	// lock ordering mistake here would deadlock every handler at once.
	gate := s.gate()

	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	if le, ok := s.engines[sessionID]; ok {
		return le, nil
	}
	s.initMaps()

	cwd, err := os.Getwd()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("web: getwd: %w", err)
	}
	opts := []agent.SessionOption{
		agent.WithCwd(cwd),
		agent.WithSessionDir(s.proj.SessionDir()),
		agent.WithPersist(true),
	}
	if sessionID != "" {
		opts = append(opts, agent.WithResumeID(sessionID))
	}
	sess, err := agent.NewSession(opts...)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	eng, err := agent.NewEngine(s.proj.Config().Model(), sess, s.engineOptions(gate)...)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	le := &liveEngine{engine: eng}
	s.engines[eng.SessionID()] = le
	return le, nil
}

// engineOptions are the shared options for every web engine: the project-scoped
// permission gate, a browser-backed Ask handler, and the default toolset. The
// gate is passed in rather than fetched, because the caller (liveFor) holds
// s.mu while building the engine.
func (s *Server) engineOptions(gate permission.Gate) []agent.EngineOption {
	cfg := s.proj.Config().Model()
	return []agent.EngineOption{
		agent.WithGate(gate),
		agent.WithAsk(s.ask),
		agent.WithContinueAsk(func(context.Context, int) (bool, error) {
			// No modal exists on the web surface: grant the budget so a turn
			// runs to completion instead of dead-ending at the round cap.
			return true, nil
		}),
		agent.WithTools(tools.DefaultTools()),
		agent.WithHooks(model.HooksFor(cfg.Name)),
	}
}

// initMaps lazily creates the server's registries. Start builds a fully
// initialized Server, but a zero-valued Server (tests, embedding) must not
// panic on first use.
func (s *Server) initMaps() {
	if s.hub == nil {
		s.hub = newHub()
	}
	if s.engines == nil {
		s.engines = map[string]*liveEngine{}
	}
	if s.pending == nil {
		s.pending = map[string]chan permission.AskResult{}
	}
	if s.modes == nil {
		s.modes = newModeState()
	}
	if s.pins == nil {
		s.pins = newPinnedSessions("")
	}
}

// modeStore returns the live mode state, initializing it on first use.
func (s *Server) modeStore() *modeState {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.initMaps()
	return s.modes
}

// pinStore returns the pin list, initializing it on first use. A Server built
// without a project gets an unconfigured store: reads report no pins and writes
// fail with a clear error instead of panicking.
func (s *Server) pinStore() *pinnedSessions {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.initMaps()
	return s.pins
}

// events returns the live hub, initializing it on first use so callers (and
// tests) never have to remember build order.
func (s *Server) events() *hub {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.initMaps()
	return s.hub
}

// policy returns the project's permission policy, falling back to the package
// defaults when the config is not loaded. Start loads it before serving, but a
// hand-built Server (tests, embedding) may not have.
//
// The fallback must be DefaultPolicy, not a zero Policy: the zero value leaves
// BashDefault at Allow, which fails open and lets every command through.
func (s *Server) policy() permission.Policy {
	if s.proj != nil && s.proj.Config() != nil {
		return s.proj.Config().Permissions
	}
	return permission.DefaultPolicy()
}

// gate builds the permission gate for web sessions from the project policy and
// the live permission mode. The gate is cached per mode so switching back and
// forth does not reset the APPA trajectory state every time.
func (s *Server) gate() permission.Gate {
	modes := s.modeStore()
	if cached, ok := modes.loadGate(modes.mode()); ok {
		return cached
	}
	g, err := modes.rebuildGate(s.policy(), s.workspace(), nil)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "web: permission gate fallback: %v\n", err)
		return permission.AllowAll{}
	}
	modes.storeGate(modes.mode(), g)
	return g
}

// workspace returns the project root used for permission confinement.
func (s *Server) workspace() string {
	if s.proj != nil {
		return s.proj.Root()
	}
	return permission.WorkspaceRoot()
}

// setPermissionMode switches the live mode and installs the new gate on every
// running engine, so a change takes effect on the next tool call without
// restarting the session.
func (s *Server) setPermissionMode(mode permission.Mode) error {
	modes := s.modeStore()
	// Validate before mutating anything, so a bad mode leaves the previous gate
	// (and the previous mode) exactly as they were.
	if _, ok := modeSummary[mode]; !ok {
		return fmt.Errorf("web: unknown permission mode %q", mode)
	}
	var prevGate permission.Gate
	if g, ok := modes.loadGate(modes.mode()); ok {
		prevGate = g
	}
	// Publish the mode first: the gate is built from it, so building first
	// would stamp the old mode into the new gate and every decision would fold
	// as if nothing changed.
	prev, err := modes.setMode(mode)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	var gate permission.Gate
	if g, ok := modes.loadGate(mode); ok {
		gate = g
	} else {
		g, err := modes.rebuildGate(s.policy(), s.workspace(), prevGate)
		if err != nil {
			// Roll the mode back: a gate we could not build is not a state to
			// leave the server in.
			_, _ = modes.setMode(prev)
			return fmt.Errorf("web: build gate for %s: %w", mode, err)
		}
		gate = g
		modes.storeGate(mode, gate)
	}
	s.applyToEngines(gate)
	return nil
}

// ask blocks until the browser answers a permission prompt, or the timeout
// elapses (which denies). Feedback from a denial is forwarded to the model.
func (s *Server) ask(ctx context.Context, req permission.Request, reason string) (permission.AskResult, error) {
	id := permission.CallHash(req)
	ch := make(chan permission.AskResult, 1)

	s.mu.Lock()
	s.initMaps()
	s.pending[id] = ch
	s.mu.Unlock()

	// Publish after unlocking so a stalled browser cannot hold the engine mutex.
	// The session id rides on the turn context so the prompt lands on the
	// browser tab that started it.
	s.events().publish(sessionFromContext(ctx), serverEvent{
		Kind: eventAsk,
		Ask:  &askPayload{ID: id, Tool: req.Tool, Reason: reason},
	})

	defer func() {
		s.mu.Lock()
		delete(s.pending, id)
		s.mu.Unlock()
	}()

	timer := time.NewTimer(askTimeout)
	defer timer.Stop()
	select {
	case res := <-ch:
		return res, nil
	case <-timer.C:
		return permission.AskResult{}, errors.New("web: permission prompt timed out")
	case <-ctx.Done():
		return permission.AskResult{}, ctx.Err()
	}
}

// requireProject guards handlers that need the loaded project. It writes the
// error response itself and returns false, so a Server built without a project
// (or a config that failed to load) reports a clean 500 instead of panicking
// on a nil dereference inside the handler.
func (s *Server) requireProject(w http.ResponseWriter) bool {
	if s.proj == nil {
		writeStatus(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "web: project is not configured")
		return false
	}
	return true
}

// listSessions returns persisted sessions for the sidebar.
func (s *Server) listSessions() ([]session.SessionMeta, error) {
	if s.proj == nil {
		return nil, errors.New("web: project is not configured")
	}
	return session.ListSessions(s.proj.SessionDir())
}
