// The session id must ride on the turn context, because the Ask handler runs on
// the engine's goroutine with no other line back to the HTTP request that
// started the turn.
func TestSessionContextRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := t.Context()
	assert.Empty(t, sessionFromContext(ctx))

	ctx = withSession(ctx, "abc123")
	assert.Equal(t, "abc123", sessionFromContext(ctx))
}

func TestDecodeBodyFormMatchesJSON(t *testing.T) {
	jsonReq := promptRequest{}
	require.NoError(t, decodeBody(jsonRequest(t, `{"sessionId":"s1","prompt":"hi"}`), &jsonReq))

	formReq := promptRequest{}
	require.NoError(t, decodeBody(formRequest(t, "sessionId=s1&prompt=hi"), &formReq))

	assert.Equal(t, jsonReq, formReq,
		"htmx posts form-encoded while curl posts JSON; both must decode identically")
}

func TestDecodeBodyFormAskAndCancel(t *testing.T) {
	var ask askRequest
	require.NoError(t, decodeBody(formRequest(t, "id=42&approved=true&feedback=use+bash"), &ask))
	assert.Equal(t, askRequest{ID: "42", Approved: true, Feedback: "use bash"}, ask)

	var cancel cancelRequest
	require.NoError(t, decodeBody(formRequest(t, "sessionId=s9"), &cancel))
	assert.Equal(t, cancelRequest{SessionID: "s9"}, cancel)
}

func TestProjectEventDropsEmptyDelta(t *testing.T) {
	// The engine re-emits the full accumulated message on every stream chunk,
	// including tool-call chunks that carry no text at all. Those must not
	// reach the browser, where they would force a pointless re-render.
	s := &Server{}
	ch, release := s.events().subscribe()
	defer release()

	s.projectEvent("s1", session.AssistantMessageUpdate{Message: session.Message{
		State: session.StateStreaming,
	}})

	select {
	case ev := <-ch:
		t.Fatalf("an empty delta must not be published, got %s", ev.Kind)
	default:
	}
}

func TestProjectEventPublishesAccumulatedText(t *testing.T) {
	s := &Server{}
	ch, release := s.events().subscribe()
	defer release()

	s.projectEvent("s1", session.AssistantMessageUpdate{Message: session.Message{
		State:   session.StateStreaming,
		Content: []session.ContentBlock{{Type: session.BlockText, Text: "hello"}},
	}})

	select {
	case ev := <-ch:
		require.NotNil(t, ev.Delta)
		assert.Equal(t, "hello", ev.Delta.Text)
		assert.Equal(t, "s1", ev.SessionID, "the turn id is stamped onto the event")
	default:
		t.Fatal("expected a delta event")
	}
}

func TestToolEventPayloadUsesStringStatus(t *testing.T) {
	got := toolEventPayload(session.ToolRun{
		ToolUseID: "call_1",
		Name:      "bash",
		Status:    session.ToolInProgress,
		Detail:    "ls -1",
	})
	assert.Equal(t, "call_1", got.ToolUseID)
	assert.Equal(t, "bash", got.Name)
	assert.Equal(t, "in-progress", got.Status,
		"status is pre-stringified so the client needs no enum table")

	raw, err := json.Marshal(serverEvent{Kind: eventTool, Tool: &got})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Contains(t, string(raw), `"status":"in-progress"`)
	assert.Contains(t, string(raw), `"toolUseId":"call_1"`)
}

func TestWireEventJSONTagsAreStable(t *testing.T) {
	raw, err := json.Marshal(serverEvent{
		Kind:      eventDelta,
		SessionID: "s1",
		Delta:     &deltaPayload{Text: "hi", Reasoning: "think"},
	})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	for _, want := range []string{`"kind":"delta"`, `"sessionId":"s1"`, `"text":"hi"`, `"reasoning":"think"`} {
		assert.Contains(t, string(raw), want)
	}
	// Absent payloads must be omitted, so the client can branch on presence
	// without confusing an omitted object with a zero value.
	assert.NotContains(t, string(raw), `"tool"`)
	assert.NotContains(t, string(raw), `"ask"`)
}

func TestHubBroadcastsToEverySubscriber(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHub()
	a, releaseA := h.subscribe()
	defer releaseA()
	b, releaseB := h.subscribe()
	defer releaseB()

	h.publish("s1", serverEvent{Kind: eventStatus, Status: &statusPayload{Text: "thinking…"}})
	for _, ch := range []chan serverEvent{a, b} {
		select {
		case ev := <-ch:
			assert.Equal(t, "s1", ev.SessionID, "publish fills the session id when the event omits it")
			assert.Equal(t, eventStatus, ev.Kind)
		default:
			t.Fatal("subscriber received nothing")
		}
	}
}

func TestHubDropsStalledSubscriber(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHub()
	stalled, release := h.subscribe()
	defer release()

	// Overflow the 64-slot buffer without draining, then publish far past it.
	// The hub must not block the agent loop on a stalled browser tab.
	for range 200 {
		h.publish("s1", serverEvent{Kind: eventDelta, Delta: &deltaPayload{Text: "x"}})
	}
	// Drain the stalled subscriber so the assertion below is about the live
	// one, not about a channel that happens to still hold old events.
	for range len(stalled) {
		<-stalled
	}

	next, releaseNext := h.subscribe()
	defer releaseNext()
	h.publish("s1", serverEvent{Kind: eventDone})
	select {
	case ev := <-next:
		assert.Equal(t, eventDone, ev.Kind, "a healthy subscriber keeps working after a stalled one is dropped")
	default:
		t.Fatal("publish blocked or dropped the healthy subscriber")
	}
}

func TestSettingsRouteServesEditorPage(t *testing.T) {
	s := &Server{}
	mux := s.routes()

	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	mux.ServeHTTP(rec, httptest.NewRequestWithContext(t.Context(), "GET", "/settings", http.NoBody))
	assert.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, rec.Code)
	// The editor document is served, not a redirect or a blank shell.
	assert.Contains(t, rec.Body.String(), `id="langToggle"`)
	assert.Contains(t, rec.Body.String(), "/api/config")
	assert.Contains(t, rec.Body.String(), "a1-config-lang")
}

func TestSettingsRouteDoesNotShadowChatRoutes(t *testing.T) {
	s := &Server{}
	mux := s.routes()

	// Mounting the editor must not claim the chat API paths. A zero-value
	// Server has no project, so /api/sessions answers 500 rather than the
	// editor document — what matters is that it is not the HTML page.
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	mux.ServeHTTP(rec, httptest.NewRequestWithContext(t.Context(), "GET", "/api/sessions", http.NoBody))
	assert.NotEqual(t, http.StatusOK, rec.Code, "a projectless server cannot list sessions")
	assert.NotContains(
		t,
		rec.Body.String(),
		`id="langToggle"`,
		"the editor document must not be served for chat routes",
	)
	assert.Contains(t, rec.Header().Get("Content-Type"), "application/json")
}

func TestConfigAPIRoutesRejectForeignOrigin(t *testing.T) {
	s := &Server{}
	mux := s.routes()

	// configserver's own handler refuses non-loopback hosts; the mount must
	// not strip that guard.
	req := httptest.NewRequestWithContext(t.Context(), http.MethodPost, "/api/config", strings.NewReader("{}"))
	req.Host = "evil.example.com"
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	mux.ServeHTTP(rec, req)
	assert.Equal(t, http.StatusForbidden, rec.Code)
}

func TestPinToggleRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	// Pins live under the project session directory; a temp dir keeps the
	// test's pins out of the real session store.
	dir := t.TempDir()
	s := &Server{pins: newPinnedSessions(dir)}
	mux := s.routes()

	post := func(id string) *httptest.ResponseRecorder {
		req := httptest.NewRequestWithContext(t.Context(), http.MethodPost, "/api/pin",
			strings.NewReader(`{"sessionId":"`+id+`"}`))
		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
		mux.ServeHTTP(rec, req)
		return rec
	}

	rec := post("sess-1")
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, rec.Code)
	var first pinResponse
	require.NoError(t, json.NewDecoder(rec.Body).Decode(&first))
	assert.True(t, first.Pinned)
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"sess-1"}, first.Pins)

	rec = post("sess-1")
	var second pinResponse
	require.NoError(t, json.NewDecoder(rec.Body).Decode(&second))
	assert.False(t, second.Pinned, "a second toggle unpins")

	rec = post("sess-2")
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, rec.Code)
	rec = httptest.NewRecorder()
	mux.ServeHTTP(rec, httptest.NewRequestWithContext(t.Context(), "GET", "/api/pins", http.NoBody))
	var list pinResponse
	require.NoError(t, json.NewDecoder(rec.Body).Decode(&list))
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"sess-2"}, list.Pins, "the newest pin leads the list")
}

// A nested s.mu acquisition wedges the whole server rather than one request:
// the handler holding the mutex never finishes, so every other handler blocks
// behind it and the process stops answering anything at all. liveFor holds s.mu
// while building an engine, so building one must not read the mode store, which
// locks s.mu too.
//
// The test drives a session that actually exists, because liveFor only builds
// (and therefore reaches the gate path) for an id it can resume — the other
// route tests use a zero-valued Server that short-circuits in requireProject,
// which would hide the deadlock entirely.
func TestLiveForDoesNotDeadlockOnLockedState(t *testing.T) {
	proj, err := project.Discover(t.TempDir())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, proj.LoadConfig())

	sessionDir := proj.SessionDir()
	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(sessionDir, 0o755))
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = os.RemoveAll(sessionDir) })

	// A minimal but valid session file: header plus one user turn, which is what
	// WithResumeID requires to accept the id as resumable.
	const sessionID = "a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90"
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(sessionDir, "probe_"+sessionID+".jsonl"), []byte(
		`{"type":"EntrySession","id":"`+sessionID+`","timestamp":"2026-10-09T10-00-00","cwd":"`+t.TempDir()+`"}`+"\n"+
			`{"type":"EntryMessage","id":"m1","parentID":null,"timestamp":"2026-10-09T10:00:01-05:00",`+
			`"message":{"role":"user","content":"hello"}}`+"\n"), 0o600))

	srv := &Server{proj: proj, modes: newModeState(), pins: newPinnedSessions(t.TempDir())}
	// Prime the registries the way Start does, so the zero-value fallback is not
	// what is under test.
	srv.mu.Lock()
	srv.hub = newHub()
	srv.engines = map[string]*liveEngine{}
	srv.pending = map[string]chan permission.AskResult{}
	srv.mu.Unlock()
	mux := srv.routes()

	// One transcript request first: it builds and caches the engine, so the
	// hammering below contends on s.mu the way a real browser does.
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	mux.ServeHTTP(rec, httptest.NewRequestWithContext(t.Context(), "GET",
		"/api/transcript?id="+sessionID, http.NoBody))
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, rec.Code, rec.Body.String())

	stop := make(chan struct{})
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	// Every endpoint that takes s.mu, hammered at once. If any of them nests its
	// acquisition with liveFor, the first overlap deadlocks and none finish.
	hammer := func(build func() *http.Request) {
		wg.Go(func() {
			for {
				select {
				case <-stop:
					return
				default:
				}
				out := httptest.NewRecorder()
				mux.ServeHTTP(out, build())
			}
		})
	}
	hammer(func() *http.Request {
		return httptest.NewRequestWithContext(t.Context(), "GET",
			"/api/transcript?id="+sessionID, http.NoBody)
	})
	hammer(func() *http.Request {
		return httptest.NewRequestWithContext(t.Context(), "GET", "/api/mode", http.NoBody)
	})
	hammer(func() *http.Request {
		return httptest.NewRequestWithContext(t.Context(), "GET", "/api/pins", http.NoBody)
	})
	hammer(func() *http.Request {
		return httptest.NewRequestWithContext(t.Context(), "POST", "/api/pin",
			strings.NewReader(`{"sessionId":"`+sessionID+`"}`))
	})

	time.Sleep(3 * time.Second)
	close(stop)

	done := make(chan struct{})
	go func() { wg.Wait(); close(done) }()
	select {
	case <-done:
	case <-time.After(30 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("handlers deadlocked: a handler took s.mu while another already held it")
	}

	// The mode must still move: a wedged mode store fails here instead.
	req := httptest.NewRequestWithContext(t.Context(), http.MethodPost, "/api/mode",
		strings.NewReader(`{"mode":"readonly"}`))
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	rec = httptest.NewRecorder()
	mux.ServeHTTP(rec, req)
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, rec.Code)
	var view modeResponse
	require.NoError(t, json.NewDecoder(rec.Body).Decode(&view))
	assert.Equal(t, "readonly", view.Mode)
}

// The switcher is only useful if the mode actually reaches the gate: a pill
// that changes the label but not the behavior would greenlight tools the
// user believes are blocked.
func TestModeSwitchChangesGateDecisions(t *testing.T) {
	proj, err := project.Discover(t.TempDir())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, proj.LoadConfig())
	srv := &Server{proj: proj, modes: newModeState(), pins: newPinnedSessions(t.TempDir())}
	mux := srv.routes()

	// Write inside the project root: WorkspaceOnlyWrites only asks about paths
	// outside it, and this test is about the mode, not the workspace fence.
	writeReq := permission.Request{Action: permission.ActionWrite, Paths: []string{proj.Root() + "/f.txt"}}

	// interactive: a write the policy allows stays allowed.
	dec, _ := srv.gate().Check(t.Context(), writeReq)
	require.Equal(t, permission.Allow, dec)

	// readonly: the same write is denied.
	req := httptest.NewRequestWithContext(t.Context(), http.MethodPost, "/api/mode",
		strings.NewReader(`{"mode":"readonly"}`))
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	mux.ServeHTTP(rec, req)
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, rec.Code)

	dec, reason := srv.gate().Check(t.Context(), writeReq)
	assert.Equal(t, permission.Deny, dec, "readonly must deny writes")
	assert.Contains(t, reason, "readonly")

	// and switching back restores the original behavior.
	req = httptest.NewRequestWithContext(t.Context(), http.MethodPost, "/api/mode",
		strings.NewReader(`{"mode":"interactive"}`))
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	rec = httptest.NewRecorder()
	mux.ServeHTTP(rec, req)
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, rec.Code)
	dec, _ = srv.gate().Check(t.Context(), writeReq)
	assert.Equal(t, permission.Allow, dec)
}

// bash is the tool most likely to surprise a user: the gate must fold Ask into
// Deny in a suppressing mode instead of silently prompting anyway.
func TestModeSwitchFoldsBashAsk(t *testing.T) {
	proj, err := project.Discover(t.TempDir())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, proj.LoadConfig())
	srv := &Server{proj: proj, modes: newModeState(), pins: newPinnedSessions(t.TempDir())}
	mux := srv.routes()

	// Off the default allowlist but not on the deny list, so interactive mode
	// asks. A curl|sh would be denied outright, which is a different rule.
	bashReq := permission.Request{Action: permission.ActionBash, Command: "pip install numpy"}

	dec, _ := srv.gate().Check(t.Context(), bashReq)
	require.Equal(t, permission.Ask, dec, "interactive must ask about a risky command")

	req := httptest.NewRequestWithContext(t.Context(), http.MethodPost, "/api/mode",
		strings.NewReader(`{"mode":"headless-strict"}`))
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	mux.ServeHTTP(rec, req)
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, rec.Code)

	dec, reason := srv.gate().Check(t.Context(), bashReq)
	assert.Equal(t, permission.Deny, dec, "headless-strict must deny what would need approval")
	assert.Contains(t, reason, "headless-strict")
}

// A Server without a loaded config must not fail open: the zero Policy leaves
// BashDefault at Allow, which would let every command through. The fallback is
// DefaultPolicy, so a risky command still asks.
func TestPolicyFallbackIsNotPermissive(t *testing.T) {
	srv := &Server{modes: newModeState()}
	p := srv.policy()
	assert.Equal(t, permission.Ask, p.BashDefault, "the fallback policy asks by default")
	assert.NotEmpty(t, p.SensitivePathDeny, "the fallback policy still denies sensitive paths")

	dec, _ := srv.gate().Check(t.Context(), permission.Request{
		Action: permission.ActionBash, Command: "pip install numpy",
	})
	assert.Equal(t, permission.Ask, dec, "an unconfigured server must not allow everything")
}
package webserver

import (
	"context"
	"net/http"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/agent"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/permission"
)

// turnKey tags the session id a turn belongs to. The Ask handler runs on the
// engine's goroutine with no direct line back to the HTTP request, so the id
// travels on the context instead of a field on Engine.
type turnKey struct{}

func withSession(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) context.Context {
	return context.WithValue(ctx, turnKey{}, sessionID)
}

func sessionFromContext(ctx context.Context) string {
	id, _ := ctx.Value(turnKey{}).(string)
	return id
}

// loopOpts are the per-turn options for the web surface. No pending skills and
// no image attachments: the composer is plain text, so the defaults hold.
func loopOpts() agent.LoopOpts { return agent.LoopOpts{} }

// permissionAskResult converts the browser's answer into the engine's contract.
func permissionAskResult(approved bool, feedback string) permission.AskResult {
	return permission.AskResult{Approved: approved, Feedback: feedback}
}

// editorPageRequest clones r with its path rewritten to "/". The editor is
// served at /settings for a stable, guessable URL, but configserver's handler
// matches its document on the exact path "/". Cloning keeps the original
// request — and therefore anything a middleware or the mux sees — untouched.
func editorPageRequest(r *http.Request) *http.Request {
	uri := *r.URL
	uri.Path = "/"
	uri.RawPath = ""
	page := r.Clone(r.Context())
	page.URL = &uri
	return page
}
// Package todo parses a markdown checklist out of a task file for the TUI.
//
// This is deliberately not a todo model: the file the agent writes is the source
// of truth, and this package only reads it. Anthropic's TaskListV2 renders a
// structured todo list; a1 renders checkboxes the agent already produces
// naturally, which means no schema, no persistence, and no tool for the model
// to forget to call.
package todo

import (
	"os"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

// Item is one markdown list line.
type Item struct {
	// Indent is the leading-whitespace width in columns, so nesting survives
	// both spaces and tabs.
	Indent int
	// Text is the item's wording with the bullet and box removed.
	Text string
	// Done reports whether the box is ticked.
	Done bool
	// InProgress is set when the box is "- [~]" or "- [>]"; exactly one item
	// should carry it, and it renders differently from a plain open item.
	InProgress bool
	// Detail marks an unbulleted-without-box line — a sub-point under the
	// preceding boxed item. Details never contribute to the counts, because
	// nothing has been claimed about their state.
	Detail bool
}

// IsTask reports whether the item carries a box, so belongs in the counts.
func (it Item) IsTask() bool { return !it.Detail }

// File is a parsed checklist plus the provenance the renderer needs to avoid
// re-reading the file on every frame.
type File struct {
	// Path is the file the checklist came from.
	Path  string
	Items []Item
	// ModTime is the source file's mtime at parse time.
	ModTime time.Time
	// Size is the source file's size at parse time.
	Size int64
}

// Done counts ticked tasks.
func (f File) Done() int {
	n := 0
	for _, it := range f.Items {
		if it.Done {
			n++
		}
	}
	return n
}

// Open counts tasks that are neither ticked nor in progress.
func (f File) Open() int {
	n := 0
	for _, it := range f.Items {
		if it.IsTask() && !it.Done && !it.InProgress {
			n++
		}
	}
	return n
}

// Tasks counts every boxed item, done or not.
func (f File) Tasks() int {
	n := 0
	for _, it := range f.Items {
		if it.IsTask() {
			n++
		}
	}
	return n
}

// InProgress returns the item marked in progress, or nil.
func (f File) InProgress() *Item {
	for i := range f.Items {
		if f.Items[i].InProgress {
			return &f.Items[i]
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// Parse reads a checklist file. A missing or unreadable file returns the error
// from the filesystem so the caller can tell "absent" from "empty" — an
// uncreated TODO.md is the normal first-run state, not a failure.
func Parse(path string) (File, error) {
	f := File{Path: path}
	info, err := os.Stat(path)
	if err != nil {
		return f, err
	}
	// A directory stats fine, so it has to be rejected explicitly rather than
	// falling through to a ReadFile that fails differently (or not at all).
	if info.IsDir() {
		return f, os.ErrInvalid
	}
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return f, err
	}
	f.ModTime = info.ModTime()
	f.Size = info.Size()
	f.Items = ParseText(string(raw))
	return f, nil
}

// ParseText extracts list items from markdown text.
//
// Recognized boxes: "- [ ]" open, "- [x]" / "- [X]" done, "- [~]" / "- [>]" in
// progress. A bullet without a box ("- some detail") is kept as a Detail line
// under whichever boxed item precedes it, so nested notes survive without being
// miscounted as tasks.
//
// Anything else — prose, headings, quotes, tables, ordered lists, code-fence
// contents — is ignored. A code fence is tracked, because agents do write
// "- [ ]" samples inside examples and counting those would inflate the total.
func ParseText(text string) []Item {
	var items []Item
	fence := ""
	for _, line := range strings.Split(text, "\n") {
		if f, ok := codeFence(line, fence); ok {
			// The marker line is never an item; tracking the open marker keeps
			// the wrong kind of fence from closing the block.
			fence = f
			continue
		}
		if fence != "" {
			continue
		}
		it, ok := parseLine(line)
		if ok {
			items = append(items, it)
		}
	}
	return items
}

// codeFence tracks whether a line is a code-fence marker and which one. The
// open marker is returned so a ~~~ block cannot be closed by a ``` line, which
// is how agents actually nest fences in examples. A closing marker returns "".
func codeFence(line, open string) (string, bool) {
	trimmed := strings.TrimLeft(line, " \t")
	if open == "" {
		for _, mark := range []string{"```", "~~~"} {
			if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, mark) {
				return mark, true
			}
		}
		return "", false
	}
	if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, open) {
		return "", true
	}
	return "", false
}

func parseLine(line string) (Item, bool) {
	// The byte cursor and the column count are separate: a tab is one byte but
	// four columns, and using one counter for both skips past the bullet.
	i, cols := 0, 0
	for i < len(line) && (line[i] == ' ' || line[i] == '\t') {
		if line[i] == '\t' {
			cols += 4
		} else {
			cols++
		}
		i++
	}
	rest := line[i:]

	bullet, ok := bulletPrefix(rest)
	if !ok {
		return Item{}, false
	}
	body := rest[len(bullet):]

	// No box: an indented detail line attaches to the boxed item above it. A
	// top-level bullet without a box is skipped instead — it has no parent to
	// attach to and nothing has been claimed about its state.
	if !hasBox(body) {
		if cols == 0 {
			return Item{}, false
		}
		text := strings.TrimSpace(body)
		return Item{Indent: cols, Text: text, Detail: true}, text != ""
	}
	mark := body[1]
	it := Item{Indent: cols, Text: strings.TrimSpace(body[3:])}
	switch mark {
	case 'x', 'X':
		it.Done = true
	case '~', '>':
		it.InProgress = true
	case ' ':
		// An open box.
	default:
		// Not a checkbox (e.g. "[1]" leftover from an ordered list).
		return Item{}, false
	}
	if it.Text == "" {
		return Item{}, false
	}
	return it, true
}

func hasBox(body string) bool {
	return len(body) >= 3 && body[0] == '[' && body[2] == ']'
}

func bulletPrefix(rest string) (string, bool) {
	for _, b := range []string{"- ", "* ", "+ "} {
		if strings.HasPrefix(rest, b) {
			return b, true
		}
	}
	return "", false
}
package todo_test

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/todo"
)

const sample = `# Migration

Some prose that is not an item.

## Steps
- [x] Read the current writer
  - Handles escaped quotes
  - [x] Still fails on a missing trailing newline
- [~] Patch the parser
- [ ] Update the tests
- [ ] Update the docs

` + "```go\n" + `// - [x] not an item, inside a code fence
` + "```" + `

1. [ ] not an item: ordered list, not a checkbox
- [X] uppercase tick
`

func TestParseTextCounts(t *testing.T) {
	items := todo.ParseText(sample)
	require.Len(t, items, 7,
		"6 boxed items plus 1 indented detail; the code-fence and ordered lines do not count")
	assert.True(t, items[0].Done)
	assert.Equal(t, 0, items[0].Indent)
	assert.True(t, items[1].Detail, "an indented unboxed bullet is a detail line")
	assert.Equal(t, "Handles escaped quotes", items[1].Text)
	assert.True(t, items[2].Done, "the nested tick is its own item")
	assert.Equal(t, 2, items[2].Indent)
	assert.True(t, items[3].InProgress)
	assert.Equal(t, "Patch the parser", items[3].Text)
	assert.True(t, items[6].Done, "an uppercase X is a tick")
	assert.Equal(t, "uppercase tick", items[6].Text)
}

func TestFileCountsAndInProgress(t *testing.T) {
	f := todo.File{Items: todo.ParseText(sample)}
	assert.Equal(t, 6, f.Tasks(), "details are not tasks")
	assert.Equal(t, 3, f.Done())
	assert.Equal(t, 2, f.Open(), "the in-progress task is neither done nor open")
	got := f.InProgress()
	require.NotNil(t, got)
	assert.Equal(t, "Patch the parser", got.Text)
}

func TestParseMissingFileIsNotAnError(t *testing.T) {
	f, err := todo.Parse(filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "absent.md"))
	assert.Error(t, err, "the error is reported so the caller can distinguish absent from empty")
	assert.Empty(t, f.Items)
}

func TestParseRoundTripModTime(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	path := filepath.Join(dir, "TODO.md")
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(path, []byte(sample), 0o644))
	f, err := todo.Parse(path)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.NotZero(t, f.ModTime, "mtime is threaded through so the renderer can skip re-reads")
	assert.Equal(t, int64(len(sample)), f.Size)
	assert.Len(t, f.Items, 7)
}

func TestParseRejectsDirectory(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	_, err := todo.Parse(dir)
	assert.Error(t, err)
}

func TestParseEmptyBoxNeedsText(t *testing.T) {
	assert.Empty(t, todo.ParseText("- [ ]\n"))
	assert.Empty(t, todo.ParseText("-\n"))
}

func TestParseTabIndent(t *testing.T) {
	items := todo.ParseText("- [x] a\n\t- [ ] b\n")
	require.Len(t, items, 2)
	assert.Equal(t, 4, items[1].Indent, "a tab counts as four columns")
	assert.False(t, items[1].Done)
}

func TestParseCodeFenceIgnoresBoxes(t *testing.T) {
	// Agents paste "- [ ]" samples inside examples; counting them inflates the
	// total and the row lies about progress.
	text := "- [x] real\n```\n- [ ] not a task\n```\n- [ ] also real\n"
	items := todo.ParseText(text)
	require.Len(t, items, 2, "the fenced sample is skipped")
	assert.Equal(t, "real", items[0].Text)
	assert.Equal(t, "also real", items[1].Text)
}

func TestParseTildeFenceNeedsTildeClose(t *testing.T) {
	text := "~~~\n- [ ] inside\n```\n- [ ] still inside\n~~~\n- [x] outside\n"
	items := todo.ParseText(text)
	require.Len(t, items, 1, "a ``` line does not close a ~~~ block")
	assert.Equal(t, "outside", items[0].Text)
}

func TestParseIgnoresProseAndHeadings(t *testing.T) {
	assert.Empty(t, todo.ParseText("# Title\n\nsome words\n> a quote\n| table |\n"))
}
// Package contextbreakdown estimates how a turn's context budget is spent.
//
// Claude Code shows a per-category token accounting — system prompt, system
// tools, MCP tools, agents, then the messages — as a grid of squares sized by
// each category's share of the window. a1's version is deliberately an
// *estimate*: there is no tokenizer dependency, so the counts are derived from
// bytes with a documented ratio and labelled as approximate wherever they are
// shown. Guessing at exactness would be worse than admitting the ratio.
package contextbreakdown

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/agent/prompt"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/session"
)

// BytesPerToken is the estimate's conversion factor. 4 bytes/token is the usual
// English-text heuristic and is what every number here is built on; it is stated
// in the output so the user can discount it.
const BytesPerToken = 4

// Category is one line of the breakdown.
type Category struct {
	Name string
	// Tokens is the estimated count.
	Tokens int
	// Note explains an entry that is not a plain estimate — the "deferred"
	// categories count schema bytes that do not enter the context window.
	Note string
}

// Breakdown is the whole accounting for one turn.
type Breakdown struct {
	Categories []Category
	// ContextWindow is the model's usable window; 0 when unknown.
	ContextWindow int
	// Reserve is the headroom kept for the reply, if the caller knows it.
	Reserve int
}

// Total sums the categories that actually consume context.
func (b Breakdown) Total() int {
	n := 0
	for _, c := range b.Categories {
		if c.Note == "" {
			n += c.Tokens
		}
	}
	return n
}

// UsedPercent is the share of the window the breakdown accounts for.
func (b Breakdown) UsedPercent() int {
	if b.ContextWindow <= 0 {
		return 0
	}
	pct := b.Total() * 100 / b.ContextWindow
	return min(pct, 999)
}

// Estimate renders the breakdown as text for a /context response.
//
// The header states the ratio and that these are estimates. Presenting them as
// exact would be the one way this feature could mislead.
func (b Breakdown) Estimate() string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "Context estimate (~%d bytes/token, provider counts will differ)\n\n", BytesPerToken)

	width := 0
	for _, c := range b.Categories {
		if l := len(c.Name); l > width {
			width = l
		}
	}
	for _, c := range b.Categories {
		tokens := formatThousands(c.Tokens)
		note := ""
		if c.Note != "" {
			note = "  " + c.Note
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "%-*s  %10s%s\n", width, c.Name, tokens, note)
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "\n")
	total := formatThousands(b.Total())
	if b.ContextWindow > 0 {
		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "Total %s / %s (%d%% used)\n",
			total, formatThousands(b.ContextWindow), b.UsedPercent())
	} else {
		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "Total %s (window unknown for this model)\n", total)
	}
	return sb.String()
}

// Build assembles the breakdown for a snapshot. toolBytes/toolCount come from
// the engine (Engine.ToolSchemaBytes), which owns the registry.
//
// The message body count is the sum of every message's text, thinking, and tool
// payload — which is what actually sits in the request. Usage counters from the
// provider are *not* used here: they report what one call cost, not what the
// current context holds, and conflating them is how you get a readout that
// disagrees with the provider's own billing.
func Build(snap session.Snapshot, contextWindow, toolBytes, toolCount int) Breakdown {
	var b Breakdown
	b.ContextWindow = contextWindow

	b.Categories = append(b.Categories, Category{
		Name:   "System prompt",
		Tokens: PromptTokens(prompt.Build("", false, 0, nil)),
	})

	if toolCount > 0 {
		b.Categories = append(b.Categories, Category{
			Name:   "Tools",
			Tokens: estimateTokens(toolBytes),
			Note:   fmt.Sprintf("%d registered", toolCount),
		})
	}

	// Tool outputs are counted once from the map, not once per message: a
	// per-message loop would multiply every output by the number of messages.
	var msgs, thinking, toolIO int
	for _, m := range snap.Messages {
		msgs += len(m.Text)
		for _, blk := range m.Content {
			switch blk.Type {
			case session.BlockText:
				msgs += len(blk.Text)
			case session.BlockThinking:
				thinking += len(blk.Text)
			case session.BlockToolUse:
				toolIO += len(blk.Input)
			}
		}
	}
	for _, r := range snap.Tools {
		toolIO += len(r.Output) + len(r.Error)
	}

	if msgs > 0 {
		b.Categories = append(b.Categories, Category{Name: "Messages", Tokens: estimateTokens(msgs)})
	}
	if thinking > 0 {
		b.Categories = append(b.Categories, Category{Name: "Thinking", Tokens: estimateTokens(thinking)})
	}
	if toolIO > 0 {
		b.Categories = append(b.Categories, Category{Name: "Tool output", Tokens: estimateTokens(toolIO)})
	}
	return b
}

// PromptTokens estimates prompt tokens from a rendered prompt string.
func PromptTokens(s string) int { return estimateTokens(len(s)) }

func estimateTokens(n int) int { return (n + BytesPerToken - 1) / BytesPerToken }

func formatThousands(n int) string {
	s := fmt.Sprintf("%d", n)
	if len(s) <= 3 {
		return s
	}
	var out []byte
	for i, c := range []byte(s) {
		if i > 0 && (len(s)-i)%3 == 0 {
			out = append(out, ',')
		}
		out = append(out, c)
	}
	return string(out)
}
package contextbreakdown_test

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/contextbreakdown"
	"github.com/damien1141/a1/internal/session"
)

func TestBuildCategories(t *testing.T) {
	snap := session.Snapshot{
		Messages: []session.Message{
			{ID: "u1", Role: session.RoleUser, Text: "read the parser"},
			{
				ID: "a1", Role: session.RoleAssistant, State: session.StateComplete,
				Content: []session.ContentBlock{
					{Type: session.BlockText, Text: "checking"},
					{Type: session.BlockThinking, Text: "thinking about it"},
					{Type: session.BlockToolUse, ID: "t1", Name: "read", Input: "main.go"},
				},
			},
		},
		Tools: map[string]session.ToolRun{
			"t1": {
				ToolUseID: "t1", Name: "read", Status: session.ToolDone,
				Output: "package main", Detail: "main.go",
			},
		},
	}
	b := contextbreakdown.Build(snap, 200000, 9000, 12)

	names := []string{}
	for _, c := range b.Categories {
		names = append(names, c.Name)
	}
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"System prompt", "Tools", "Messages", "Thinking", "Tool output"}, names)

	// Every category has a positive estimate.
	for _, c := range b.Categories {
		assert.Positive(t, c.Tokens, "%s is estimated", c.Name)
	}

	// The tools row carries its note.
	assert.Equal(t, "12 registered", b.Categories[1].Note)

	used := b.UsedPercent()
	assert.Greater(t, used, 0)
	assert.LessOrEqual(t, used, 100, "the window bounds the percentage")
}

func TestTotalExcludesNotedCategories(t *testing.T) {
	b := contextbreakdown.Breakdown{
		Categories: []contextbreakdown.Category{
			{Name: "Real", Tokens: 100},
			{Name: "Deferred", Tokens: 5000, Note: "not in the window"},
		},
	}
	assert.Equal(t, 100, b.Total(),
		"a category with a note is informational and does not consume context")
}

func TestToolOutputCountedOnce(t *testing.T) {
	// The same tool run seen through many messages must not be multiplied.
	snap := session.Snapshot{
		Messages: []session.Message{
			{
				ID: "a1", Role: session.RoleAssistant, State: session.StateComplete,
				Content: []session.ContentBlock{{Type: session.BlockText, Text: "one"}},
			},
			{
				ID: "a2", Role: session.RoleAssistant, State: session.StateComplete,
				Content: []session.ContentBlock{{Type: session.BlockText, Text: "two"}},
			},
		},
		Tools: map[string]session.ToolRun{
			"t1": {ToolUseID: "t1", Name: "read", Status: session.ToolDone, Output: strings.Repeat("x", 400)},
		},
	}
	b := contextbreakdown.Build(snap, 0, 0, 0)
	for _, c := range b.Categories {
		if c.Name == "Tool output" {
			assert.Equal(t, 100, c.Tokens, "400 bytes once, not once per message")
		}
	}
}

func TestEstimateStatesItIsAnEstimate(t *testing.T) {
	snap := session.Snapshot{Messages: []session.Message{{ID: "u1", Role: session.RoleUser, Text: "hi"}}}
	got := contextbreakdown.Build(snap, 200000, 4000, 10).Estimate()
	assert.Contains(t, got, "estimate", "the header says so")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "~4 bytes/token", "the ratio is stated, not hidden")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "System prompt")
	assert.Contains(t, got, "200,000", "the window is formatted")
}

func TestEstimateUnknownWindow(t *testing.T) {
	got := contextbreakdown.Build(session.Snapshot{}, 0, 0, 0).Estimate()
	assert.Contains(t, got, "window unknown",
		"a missing window is reported, not treated as zero percent")
}

func TestEmptySnapshotHasNoMessageCategories(t *testing.T) {
	b := contextbreakdown.Build(session.Snapshot{}, 1000, 0, 0)
	for _, c := range b.Categories {
		assert.NotEqual(t, "Messages", c.Name)
		assert.NotEqual(t, "Tool output", c.Name)
	}
	// The system prompt is always present.
	require.NotEmpty(t, b.Categories)
	assert.Equal(t, "System prompt", b.Categories[0].Name)
}

func TestUsedPercentCapsSanely(t *testing.T) {
	b := contextbreakdown.Breakdown{
		Categories:    []contextbreakdown.Category{{Name: "a", Tokens: 5000}},
		ContextWindow: 100,
	}
	assert.LessOrEqual(t, b.UsedPercent(), 999, "an over-window breakdown does not print nonsense")
}
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
)

type inner struct {
	Allow *[]string `yaml:"allow"`
}
type outer struct {
	Bash *inner `yaml:"bash"`
}

func main() {
	for _, s := range []string{
		"bash:\n  default: ask\n",
		"bash:\n  allow: []\n",
		"bash:\n  allow:\n",
		"bash:\n  allow: [make]\n",
	} {
		var o outer
		err := yaml.Unmarshal([]byte(s), &o)
		fmt.Printf("%-40q err=%v nil=%v", s, err, o.Bash == nil || o.Bash.Allow == nil)
		if o.Bash != nil && o.Bash.Allow != nil {
			fmt.Printf(" len=%d val=%v", len(*o.Bash.Allow), *o.Bash.Allow)
		}
		fmt.Println()
	}
}
